किं न जानासि चित्तस्थं तथा वच्म्यपि शासनात् ॥
2.3.m: Hari said: / You are omniscient, O Maheśāna, the inner ruler, the Lord of all. / Do you not know what is in our hearts? Even so, I speak at your command.

2.3.s:
tārakāsurato duḥkhaṃ sambhūtaṃ vividhaṃ mṛḍa |
sarveṣāṃ nastadarthaṃ hi prasanno'kāri vai suraiḥ ||
2.3.d:
तारकासुरतो दुःखं सम्भूतं विविधं मृड ।
सर्वेषां नस्तदर्थं हि प्रसन्नोऽकारि वै सुरैः ॥
2.3.m: Manifold suffering has arisen from the demon Tāraka, O Mṛḍa; / for the sake of all of us, you have indeed been propitiated by the gods.

2.3.s:
śivā sā janitā śailāttvadarthaṃ hi himālayāt |
tasyāṃ tvadudbhavātputrāttasya mṛtyurna cānyathā ||
2.3.d:
शिवा सा जनिता शैलात्त्वदर्थं हि हिमालयात् ।
तस्यां त्वदुद्भवात्पुत्रात्तस्य मृत्युर्न चान्यथा ॥
2.3.m: That Śivā was born from the mountain Himālaya for your sake; / his death cannot occur otherwise than from a son born of you upon her.

2.3.s:
iti datto brahmaṇā hi tasmai daityāya yadvaraḥ |
tadanyasmādamṛtyuḥ sa bādhate nikhilaṃ jagat ||
2.3.d:
इति दत्तो ब्रह्मणा हि तस्मै दैत्याय यद्वरः ।
तदन्यस्मादमृत्युः स बाधते निखिलं जगत् ॥
2.3.m: For such a boon was given to that demon by Brahmā, / that he cannot be killed by any other; he afflicts the entire world.

2.3.s:
nāradasya nideśātsā karoti kaṭhinaṃ tapaḥ |
tattejasākhilaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram ||
2.3.d:
नारदस्य निदेशात्सा करोति कठिनं तपः ।
तत्तेजसाखिलं व्याप्तं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
2.3.m: At Nārada’s instruction she is performing severe tapas; / by her splendor the entire threefold world, moving and unmoving, is pervaded.

2.3.s:
varaṃ dātuṃ śivāyai hi gaccha tvaṃ parameśvara |
devaduḥkhaṃ jahi svāminnasmākaṃ sukhamāvaha ||
2.3.d:
वरं दातुं शिवायै हि गच्छ त्वं परमेश्वर ।
देवदुःखं जहि स्वामिन्नस्माकं सुखमावह ॥
2.3.m: Go, O Parameśvara, to grant a boon to Śivā; / destroy the distress of the gods, O Lord, and bring us happiness.

2.3.s:
devānāṃ me mahotsāho hṛdaye cāsti śaṅkara |
vivāhaṃ tava sandraṣṭuṃ tattvaṃ kuru yathocitam ||
2.3.d:
देवानां मे महोत्साहो हृदये चास्ति शङ्कर ।
विवाहं तव सन्द्रष्टुं तत्त्वं कुरु यथोचितम् ॥
2.3.m: And in the heart of the gods and in mine there is great eagerness, O Śaṅkara, / to witness your wedding; so do what is appropriate.

2.3.s:
ratyai yadbhavatā datto varastasya parātpara |
prāpto'vasara evāśu saphalaṃ svapaṇaṃ kuru ||
2.3.d:
रत्यै यद्भवता दत्तो वरस्तस्य परात्पर ।
प्राप्तोऽवसर एवाशु सफलं स्वपणं कुरु ॥
2.3.m: The boon that was given by you to Rati, O you higher than the highest— / its occasion has just arrived; quickly make your promise bear fruit.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā taṃ praṇamyaiva viṣṇurdevā maharṣayaḥ |
saṃstūya vividhaiḥ stotraiḥ santasthustatpuro'khilāḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा तं प्रणम्यैव विष्णुर्देवा महर्षयः ।
संस्तूय विविधैः स्तोत्रैः सन्तस्थुस्तत्पुरोऽखिलाः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus and bowed to him, Viṣṇu, the gods, and the great sages, / having praised him with manifold hymns, all stood before him.

2.3.s:
bhaktādhīnaḥ śaṅkaro'pi śrutvā devavacastadā |
vihasya pratyuvācāśu vedamaryādarakṣakaḥ ||
2.3.d:
भक्ताधीनः शङ्करोऽपि श्रुत्वा देववचस्तदा ।
विहस्य प्रत्युवाचाशु वेदमर्यादरक्षकः ॥
2.3.m: And Śaṅkara, who is obedient to his devotees, having heard the words of the gods then, / smiled and quickly replied, he who protects the ordinances of the Vedas.

2.3.s:
śaṅkara uvāca |
he hare he vidhe devāḥ śṛṇutādarato'khilāḥ |
yathocitamahaṃ vacmi saviśeṣaṃ vivekataḥ ||
2.3.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ।
हे हरे हे विधे देवाः शृणुतादरतोऽखिलाः ।
यथोचितमहं वच्मि सविशेषं विवेकतः ॥
2.3.m: Śaṅkara said: / O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods, all of you listen with respect; / I speak what is appropriate, in particular detail through discernment.

2.3.s:
nocitaṃ hi vidhānaṃ vai vivāhakaraṇaṃ nṛṇām |
mahānigaḍasaṃjño hi vivāho dṛḍhabandhanaḥ ||
2.3.d:
नोचितं हि विधानं वै विवाहकरणं नृणाम् ।
महानिगडसंज्ञो हि विवाहो दृढबन्धनः ॥
2.3.m: Indeed, entering into marriage is not a proper arrangement for men; / for marriage is known as a great iron chain, a tight bond.

2.3.s:
kusaṅgā bahavo loke strīsaṅgastatra cādhikaḥ |
uddharetsakalairbandhairna strīsaṅgātpramucyate ||
2.3.d:
कुसङ्गा बहवो लोके स्त्रीसङ्गस्तत्र चाधिकः ।
उद्धरेत्सकलैर्बन्धैर्न स्त्रीसङ्गात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
2.3.m: There are many bad associations in the world, and association with women is the worst among them; / one may be rescued from all bonds, but one is not freed from association with women.

2.3.s:
lohadārumayaiḥ pāśairdṛḍhaṃ baddho'pi mucyate |
stryādipāśasusambaddho mucyate na kadācana ||
2.3.d:
लोहदारुमयैः पाशैर्दृढं बद्धोऽपि मुच्यते ।
स्त्र्यादिपाशसुसम्बद्धो मुच्यते न कदाचन ॥
2.3.m: Even one tightly bound by fetters of iron or wood is released, / but one firmly bound by the fetters of women and the like is never released.

2.3.s:
vardhante viṣayāḥ śaśvanmahābandhanakāriṇaḥ |
viṣayākrāntamanasaḥ svapne mokṣo'pi durlabhaḥ ||
2.3.d:
वर्धन्ते विषयाः शश्वन्महाबन्धनकारिणः ।
विषयाक्रान्तमनसः स्वप्ने मोक्षोऽपि दुर्लभः ॥
2.3.m: Sense objects, which cause great bondage, constantly multiply; / for one whose mind is overcome by sense objects, liberation is difficult to attain even in a dream.

2.3.s:
sukhamicchati cetprājño vidhivadviṣayāṃstyajet |
viṣavadviṣayānāhurviṣayairyairnihanyate ||
2.3.d:
सुखमिच्छति चेत्प्राज्ञो विधिवद्विषयांस्त्यजेत् ।
विषवद्विषयानाहुर्विषयैर्यैर्निहन्यते ॥
2.3.m: If a wise man desires happiness, he should duly abandon sense objects; / they call sense objects like poison, by which sense objects one is destroyed.

2.3.s:
jano viṣayiṇā sākaṃ vārtātaḥ patati kṣaṇāt |
viṣayaṃ prāhurācāryāḥ sitāliptendravāruṇīm ||
2.3.d:
जनो विषयिणा साकं वार्तातः पतति क्षणात् ।
विषयं प्राहुराचार्याः सितालिप्तेन्द्रवारुणीम् ॥
2.3.m: A person falls in an instant merely from conversation with a sensual person; / teachers describe a sense object as a bitter gourd smeared with sugar.

2.3.s:
yadyapyevaṃ hi jānāmi sarvaṃ jñānaṃ viśeṣataḥ |
tathāpyahaṃ kariṣyāmi prārthanāṃ saphalāṃ ca vaḥ ||
2.3.d:
यद्यप्येवं हि जानामि सर्वं ज्ञानं विशेषतः ।
तथाप्यहं करिष्यामि प्रार्थनां सफलां च वः ॥
2.3.m: Even though I know all this wisdom especially well, / nevertheless I will grant your request and make it fruitful.

2.3.s:
bhaktādhīno'hamevāsmi tadvaśātsarvakāryakṛt |
ayathocitakartā hi prasiddho bhuvanatraye ||
2.3.d:
भक्ताधीनोऽहमेवास्मि तद्वशात्सर्वकार्यकृत् ।
अयथोचितकर्ता हि प्रसिद्धो भुवनत्रये ॥
2.3.m: Indeed, I am subordinate to my devotees; under their influence I do everything. / I am well known in the three worlds as one who acts against what is conventional.

2.3.s:
kāmarūpādhipasyaiva paṇaśca saphalaḥ kṛtaḥ |
sudakṣiṇasya bhūpasya bhavabandhagatasya hi ||
2.3.d:
कामरूपाधिपस्यैव पणश्च सफलः कृतः ।
सुदक्षिणस्य भूपस्य भवबन्धगतस्य हि ॥
2.3.m: The pledge of the ruler of Kāmarūpa was fulfilled [by me], / of King Sudakṣiṇa, who had fallen into the fetters of worldly existence.

2.3.s:
gautamakleśakartāhaṃ tryambakātmā sukhāvahaḥ |
tatkaṣṭapradaduṣṭānāṃ śāpadāyī viśeṣataḥ ||
2.3.d:
गौतमक्लेशकर्ताहं त्र्यम्बकात्मा सुखावहः ।
तत्कष्टप्रददुष्टानां शापदायी विशेषतः ॥
2.3.m: I relieved the distress of Gautama, bringing happiness as Tryambaka, / and especially gave a curse to the wicked who caused him torment.

2.3.s:
viṣaṃ pītaṃ surārthaṃ hi bhaktavatsalabhāvadhṛk |
devakaṣṭaṃ hṛtaṃ yatnātsarvadaiva mayā surāḥ ||
2.3.d:
विषं पीतं सुरार्थं हि भक्तवत्सलभावधृक् ।
देवकष्टं हृतं यत्नात्सर्वदैव मया सुराः ॥
2.3.m: Bearing the disposition of one affectionate toward devotees, I drank the poison for the sake of the gods; / the distress of the gods has always been removed by me with effort, O gods.

2.3.s:
bhaktārthamasahaṃ kaṣṭaṃ bahuśo bahuyatnataḥ |
viśvānaramunerduḥkhaṃ hṛtaṃ gṛhapatirbhavan ||
2.3.d:
भक्तार्थमसहं कष्टं बहुशो बहुयत्नतः ।
विश्वानरमुनेर्दुःखं हृतं गृहपतिर्भवन् ॥
2.3.m: For the sake of devotees, I endured distress many times with great effort; / becoming Gṛhapati, I removed the sorrow of the sage Viśvānara.

2.3.s:
kiṃ bahūktena ca hare vidhe satyaṃ bravīmyaham |
matpaṇo'stīti yūyaṃ vai sarve jānītha tattvataḥ ||
2.3.d:
किं बहूक्तेन च हरे विधे सत्यं ब्रवीम्यहम् ।
मत्पणोऽस्तीति यूयं वै सर्वे जानीथ तत्त्वतः ॥
2.3.m: What need is there of saying much, O Hari, O Vidhi? I speak the truth. / You all truly know that this is my pledge.

2.3.s:
yadā yadā vipattirhi bhaktānāṃ bhavati kvacit |
tadā tadā harāmyāśu tatkṣaṇātsarvaśaḥsadā ||
2.3.d:
यदा यदा विपत्तिर्हि भक्तानां भवति क्वचित् ।
तदा तदा हराम्याशु तत्क्षणात्सर्वशःसदा ॥
2.3.m: Whenever distress befalls devotees anywhere, / then I always remove it immediately, at that very moment, completely.

2.3.s:
jāne'haṃ tārakādduḥkhaṃ sarveṣāṃ vaḥ samutthitam |
asurāttaddhariṣyāmi satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham ||
2.3.d:
जानेऽहं तारकाद्दुःखं सर्वेषां वः समुत्थितम् ।
असुरात्तद्धरिष्यामि सत्यं सत्यं वदाम्यहम् ॥
2.3.m: I know the sorrow arisen for all of you from Tāraka; / I will take it away from that Asura—I speak the truth, the truth.

2.3.s:
nāsti yadyapi me kācidvivāhakaraṇe ruciḥ |
vivāhayiṣye girijāṃ putrotpādanahetave ||
2.3.d:
नास्ति यद्यपि मे काचिद्विवाहकरणे रुचिः ।
विवाहयिष्ये गिरिजां पुत्रोत्पादनहेतवे ॥
2.3.m: Although I have no desire at all to enter into marriage, / I shall marry Girijā for the sake of producing a son.

2.3.s:
gacchata svagṛhāṇyeva nirbhayāḥ sakalāḥ surāḥ |
kāryaṃ vaḥ sādhayiṣyāmi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
2.3.d:
गच्छत स्वगृहाण्येव निर्भयाः सकलाः सुराः ।
कार्यं वः साधयिष्यामि नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
2.3.m: Go to your own homes, all you gods, free from fear; / I shall accomplish your purpose; no doubt should be entertained here.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā maunamāsthāya samādhistho'bhavaddharaḥ |
sarve viṣṇvādayo devāḥ svadhāmāni yayurmune ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा मौनमास्थाय समाधिस्थोऽभवद्धरः ।
सर्वे विष्ण्वादयो देवाः स्वधामानि ययुर्मुने ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus and observing silence, Hara entered into deep meditation; / all the gods, headed by Viṣṇu, went to their own abodes, O sage.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, named Acceptance of the Marriage to Pārvatī, in the Pārvatīkhaṇḍa, the third [section] of the second Rudrasaṃhitā in the auspicious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.3.s:
nārada uvāca |
gateṣu teṣu deveṣu vidhiviṣṇvādikeṣu ca |
sarveṣu muniṣu prītyā kiṃ babhūva tataḥ param ||
2.3.d:
नारद उवाच ।
गतेषु तेषु देवेषु विधिविष्ण्वादिकेषु च ।
सर्वेषु मुनिषु प्रीत्या किं बभूव ततः परम् ॥
2.3.m: Nārada said: / When those gods, Vidhi, Viṣṇu, and the others, and all the sages had gone, / out of affection, what happened after that?

2.3.s:
kiṃ kṛtaṃ śambhunā tāta varaṃ dātuṃ samāgataḥ |
kiyatkālena ca kathaṃ tadvada prītimāvaha ||
2.3.d:
किं कृतं शम्भुना तात वरं दातुं समागतः ।
कियत्कालेन च कथं तद्वद प्रीतिमावह ॥
2.3.m: What was done by Śambhu, dear father? Did he arrive to grant a boon? / After how much time, and how? Tell that, bringing delight.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
gateṣu teṣu deveṣu brahmādiṣu nijāśramam |
tattapaḥ suparīkṣārthaṃ samādhistho'bhavadbhavaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
गतेषु तेषु देवेषु ब्रह्मादिषु निजाश्रमम् ।
तत्तपः सुपरीक्षार्थं समाधिस्थोऽभवद्भवः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / When those gods, Brahmā and the others, had gone to their own hermitage, / Bhava entered into deep meditation in order to thoroughly test her austerity.

2.3.s:
svātmānamātmanā kṛtvā svātmanyeva vyacintayat |
parātparataraṃ svasthaṃ nirmāyaṃ niravagraham ||
2.3.d:
स्वात्मानमात्मना कृत्वा स्वात्मन्येव व्यचिन्तयत् ।
परात्परतरं स्वस्थं निर्मायं निरवग्रहम् ॥
2.3.m: Establishing himself by himself, he contemplated solely within his own self / that which is beyond the highest, self-abiding, free from illusion, and unimpeded.

2.3.s:
tadvastubhūto bhagavānīśvaro vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ |
avijñātagatiḥsūtiḥsa haraḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
2.3.d:
तद्वस्तुभूतो भगवानीश्वरो वृषभध्वजः ।
अविज्ञातगतिःसूतिःस हरः परमेश्वरः ॥
2.3.m: The Lord, Īśvara, Vṛṣabhadhvaja, who is identical with that reality, / whose course and origin are unknown—he is Hara, Parameśvara.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
girijā hi tadā tāta tatāpa paramaṃ tapaḥ |
tapasā tena rudro'pi paraṃ vismayamāgataḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
गिरिजा हि तदा तात तताप परमं तपः ।
तपसा तेन रुद्रोऽपि परं विस्मयमागतः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Then, dear child, Girijā performed supreme austerity; / by that austerity even Rudra reached supreme astonishment.

2.3.s:
samādheścalitasso'bhūdbhaktādhīno'pi nānyathā |
vasiṣṭhādīnmunīnsapta sasmāra sūtikṛddharaḥ ||
2.3.d:
समाधेश्चलितस्सोऽभूद्भक्ताधीनोऽपि नान्यथा ।
वसिष्ठादीन्मुनीन्सप्त सस्मार सूतिकृद्धरः ॥
2.3.m: He moved from deep meditation, subordinate to devotees, and not otherwise; / Hara, the author of origin, remembered the seven sages headed by Vasiṣṭha.

2.3.s:
saptāpi munayaḥ śīghramāyayuḥ smṛtimātrataḥ |
prasannavadanāḥ sarve varṇayanto vidhiṃ bahu ||
2.3.d:
सप्तापि मुनयः शीघ्रमाययुः स्मृतिमात्रतः ।
प्रसन्नवदनाः सर्वे वर्णयन्तो विधिं बहु ॥
2.3.m: All seven sages came quickly merely upon being remembered, / all with cheerful faces, praising the creator in many ways.

2.3.s:
praṇamya taṃ maheśānaṃ tuṣṭuvurharṣanirbharāḥ |
vāṇyā gadgadayā baddhakarā vinatakandharāḥ ||
2.3.d:
प्रणम्य तं महेशानं तुष्टुवुर्हर्षनिर्भराः ।
वाण्या गद्गदया बद्धकरा विनतकन्धराः ॥
2.3.m: Having bowed to that Maheśāna, filled with joy, / with choked voices, folded hands, and bowed necks, they praised him.

2.3.s:
saptarṣaya ūcuḥ |
devadeva mahādeva karuṇāsāgara prabho |
jātā vayaṃ sudhanyā hi tvayā yadadhunā smṛtāḥ ||
2.3.d:
सप्तर्षय ऊचुः ।
देवदेव महादेव करुणासागर प्रभो ।
जाता वयं सुधन्या हि त्वया यदधुना स्मृताः ॥
2.3.m: The seven sages said: / O god of gods, O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, O Lord! / We have indeed become most blessed, since we have now been remembered by you.

2.3.s:
kimarthaṃ saṃsmṛtā nātha śāsanaṃ dehi taddhi naḥ |
svadāsasadṛśīṃ svāminkṛpāṃ kuru namo'stu te ||
2.3.d:
किमर्थं संस्मृता नाथ शासनं देहि तद्धि नः ।
स्वदाससदृशीं स्वामिन्कृपां कुरु नमोऽस्तु ते ॥
2.3.m: For what purpose have we been remembered, O Lord? Give us that command; / O Master, bestow your grace upon us as upon your own servants. Obeisance to you!

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya munīnāṃ tu vijñaptiṃ karuṇānidhiḥ |
provāca vihasanprītyā protphullanayanāmbujaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य मुनीनां तु विज्ञप्तिं करुणानिधिः ।
प्रोवाच विहसन्प्रीत्या प्रोत्फुल्लनयनाम्बुजः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing the petition of the sages, the treasure of compassion, / smiling with affection, his lotus eyes fully blooming, spoke.

2.3.s:
maheśvara uvāca |
he saptamunayastātāḥ śṛṇutāraṃ vaco mama |
asmaddhitakarā yūyaṃ sarvajñānavicakṣaṇāḥ ||
2.3.d:
महेश्वर उवाच ।
हे सप्तमुनयस्ताताः शृणुतारं वचो मम ।
अस्मद्धितकरा यूयं सर्वज्ञानविचक्षणाः ॥
2.3.m: Maheśvara said: / O seven sages, dear ones! Listen quickly to my words. / You are skilled in all knowledge, doers of what is beneficial to me.

2.3.s:
tapaścarati deveśī pārvatī girijādhunā |
gaurīśikharasaṃjñe hi parvate dṛḍhamānasā ||
2.3.d:
तपश्चरति देवेशी पार्वती गिरिजाधुना ।
गौरीशिखरसंज्ञे हि पर्वते दृढमानसा ॥
2.3.m: Now the ruler of the gods, Pārvatī, Girijā, is performing austerity / with a resolute mind on the mountain named Gaurīśikhara.

2.3.s:
māṃ patiṃ prāptukāmā hi sā sakhīsevitā dvijāḥ |
sarvānkāmānvihāyānyānparaṃ niścayamāgatā ||
2.3.d:
मां पतिं प्राप्तुकामा हि सा सखीसेविता द्विजाः ।
सर्वान्कामान्विहायान्यान्परं निश्चयमागता ॥
2.3.m: Desiring to obtain me as her husband, attended by her female friends, O twice-born ones, / having abandoned all other desires, she has reached a supreme resolve.

2.3.s:
tatra gacchata yūyaṃ macchāsanānmunisattamāḥ |
parīkṣāṃ dṛḍhatāyāstatkuruta premacetasaḥ ||
2.3.d:
तत्र गच्छत यूयं मच्छासनान्मुनिसत्तमाः ।
परीक्षां दृढतायास्तत्कुरुत प्रेमचेतसः ॥
2.3.m: Go there by my command, O best of sages; / you whose minds are filled with love, test the firmness of that [resolve].

2.3.s:
sarvathā chalasaṃyuktaṃ vacanīyaṃ vacaśca vaḥ |
na saṃśayaḥ prakartavyaḥ śāsanānmama suvratāḥ ||
2.3.d:
सर्वथा छलसंयुक्तं वचनीयं वचश्च वः ।
न संशयः प्रकर्तव्यः शासनान्मम सुव्रताः ॥
2.3.m: And words accompanied by deceit should be spoken by you in every way; / no doubt should be entertained, by my command, O you of good vows.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityājñaptāśca munayo jagmustatra drutaṃ hi te |
yatra rājati sā dīptā jaganmātā nagātmajā ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याज्ञप्ताश्च मुनयो जग्मुस्तत्र द्रुतं हि ते ।
यत्र राजति सा दीप्ता जगन्माता नगात्मजा ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Thus commanded, the sages went quickly indeed to that place / where that radiant daughter of the mountain, the mother of the universe, shone.

2.3.s:
tatra dṛṣṭvā śivā sākṣāttapaḥsiddhirivāparā |
mūrtā paramatejaskā vilasantī sutejasā ||
2.3.d:
तत्र दृष्ट्वा शिवा साक्षात्तपःसिद्धिरिवापरा ।
मूर्ता परमतेजस्का विलसन्ती सुतेजसा ॥
2.3.m: Seeing there Śivā in person, like another embodied perfection of austerity, / possessed of supreme splendor, shining with excellent radiance,

2.3.s:
hṛdā praṇamya tāṃ te tu ṛṣayassapta suvratāḥ |
sannatā vacanaṃ procuḥ pūjitāśca viśeṣataḥ ||
2.3.d:
हृदा प्रणम्य तां ते तु ऋषयस्सप्त सुव्रताः ।
सन्नता वचनं प्रोचुः पूजिताश्च विशेषतः ॥
2.3.m: bowing to her in their hearts, those seven sages of good vows, / being deeply humbled and especially honored [by her], spoke these words.

2.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
śṛṇu śailasute devi kimarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ |
icchasi tvaṃ suraṃ kaṃ ca kiṃ phalaṃ tadvadādhunā ||
2.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
शृणु शैलसुते देवि किमर्थं तप्यते तपः ।
इच्छसि त्वं सुरं कं च किं फलं तद्वदाधुना ॥
2.3.m: The sages said: / Listen, O daughter of the mountain, O goddess! For what purpose is this austerity being performed? / What god do you desire, and what is the fruit? Tell that now.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktā sā śivā devī girīndratanayā dvijaiḥ |
pratyuvāca vacaḥ satyaṃ sugūḍhamapi tatpuraḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्ता सा शिवा देवी गिरीन्द्रतनया द्विजैः ।
प्रत्युवाच वचः सत्यं सुगूढमपि तत्पुरः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Thus addressed by the twice-born ones, that goddess Śivā, daughter of the king of mountains, / spoke true, though very secret, words before them.

2.3.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
munīśvarāḥsaṃśṛṇuta madvākyaṃ prītito hṛdā |
bravīmi svavicāraṃ vai cintito yo dhiyā svayā ||
2.3.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
मुनीश्वराःसंशृणुत मद्वाक्यं प्रीतितो हृदा ।
ब्रवीमि स्वविचारं वै चिन्तितो यो धिया स्वया ॥
2.3.m: Pārvatī said: / O lords of sages, hear with your hearts my words with affection! / I tell my own thought, which has been deliberated by my own intellect.

2.3.s:
kariṣyatha prahāsaṃ me śrutvā vāco hyasambhavāḥ |
saṅkoco varṇanādviprā bhavatyeva karomi kim ||
2.3.d:
करिष्यथ प्रहासं मे श्रुत्वा वाचो ह्यसम्भवाः ।
सङ्कोचो वर्णनाद्विप्रा भवत्येव करोमि किम् ॥
2.3.m: You will laugh at me upon hearing these impossible words; / embarrassment indeed arises from describing them, O brahmins, but what can I do?

2.3.s:
idaṃ mano hi sudṛḍhamavaśaṃ parakarmakṛt |
jalopari mahābhittiṃ cikīrṣati mahonnatām ||
2.3.d:
इदं मनो हि सुदृढमवशं परकर्मकृत् ।
जलोपरि महाभित्तिं चिकीर्षति महोन्नताम् ॥
2.3.m: This mind of mine is very stubborn, uncontrolled, doing another's bidding; / it wishes to build a very high, great wall upon water.

2.3.s:
surarṣeḥ śāsanaṃ prāpya karomi sudṛḍhaṃ tapaḥ |
rudraḥ patirbhavenme hi vidhāyeti manoratham ||
2.3.d:
सुरर्षेः शासनं प्राप्य करोमि सुदृढं तपः ।
रुद्रः पतिर्भवेन्मे हि विधायेति मनोरथम् ॥
2.3.m: Having received the instruction of the divine sage, I perform severe austerity, / having formed the desire: ‘May Rudra become my husband!’

2.3.s:
apakṣo manmanaḥ pakṣī vyomni uḍḍīyate haṭhāt |
tadāśāṃ śaṅkaraḥ svāmī piparttu karuṇānidhiḥ ||
2.3.d:
अपक्षो मन्मनः पक्षी व्योम्नि उड्डीयते हठात् ।
तदाशां शङ्करः स्वामी पिपर्त्तु करुणानिधिः ॥
2.3.m: The wingless bird of my mind forcibly flies into the sky; / may the master Śaṅkara, the ocean of compassion, fulfill that hope of it.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya vacastasyā vihasya munayaśca te |
sammānya girijāṃ prītyā procuśchalavaco mṛṣā ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्या विहस्य मुनयश्च ते ।
सम्मान्य गिरिजां प्रीत्या प्रोचुश्छलवचो मृषा ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing her words and laughing, those sages, / having honored Girijā with affection, spoke deceitful and false words.

2.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
na jñātaṃ tasya caritaṃ vṛthāpaṇḍitamāninaḥ |
devarṣeḥ krūramanasaḥ sujñā bhūtvāpyagātmaje ||
2.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
न ज्ञातं तस्य चरितं वृथापण्डितमानिनः ।
देवर्षेः क्रूरमनसः सुज्ञा भूत्वाप्यगात्मजे ॥
2.3.m: The sages said: / Though you are wise, O daughter of the mountain, the conduct of that divine sage of cruel mind, / who vainly considers himself learned, was not known [by you].

2.3.s:
nāradaḥ kūṭavādī ca paracittapramanthakaḥ |
tasya vārtāśravaṇato hānirbhavati sarvathā ||
2.3.d:
नारदः कूटवादी च परचित्तप्रमन्थकः ।
तस्य वार्ताश्रवणतो हानिर्भवति सर्वथा ॥
2.3.m: Nārada is a speaker of deceit and an agitator of other people’s minds; / from hearing his words, ruin ensues in every way.

2.3.s:
tatra tvaṃ śṛṇu sad buddhyā cetihāsaṃ suśobhitam |
kramāttvāṃ bodhayanto hi prītyā tamupadhāraya ||
2.3.d:
तत्र त्वं शृणु सद् बुद्ध्या चेतिहासं सुशोभितम् ।
क्रमात्त्वां बोधयन्तो हि प्रीत्या तमुपधारय ॥
2.3.m: In that regard, listen with a good intellect to a very splendid ancient story; / instructing you in due order, attentively comprehend it with affection.

2.3.s:
brahmaputro hi yo dakṣaḥ suṣuve piturājñayā |
svapatnyāmayutaṃ putrānayuṅkta tapasi priyān ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मपुत्रो हि यो दक्षः सुषुवे पितुराज्ञया ।
स्वपत्न्यामयुतं पुत्रानयुङ्क्त तपसि प्रियान् ॥
2.3.m: Dakṣa, who was the son of Brahmā, by his father's command begot / ten thousand dear sons upon his wife, and directed them to austerity.

2.3.s:
te sutāḥ paścimadiśi nārāyaṇasaro gatāḥ |
tapo'rthe te pratijñāya nāradastatra vai yayau ||
2.3.d:
ते सुताः पश्चिमदिशि नारायणसरो गताः ।
तपोऽर्थे ते प्रतिज्ञाय नारदस्तत्र वै ययौ ॥
2.3.m: Those sons went to Lake Nārāyaṇa in the western direction; / when they had resolved upon austerity, Nārada went there.

2.3.s:
kūṭopadeśamāśrāvya tatra tānnārado muniḥ |
tadājñayā ca te sarve piturna gṛhamāyayuḥ ||
2.3.d:
कूटोपदेशमाश्राव्य तत्र तान्नारदो मुनिः ।
तदाज्ञया च ते सर्वे पितुर्न गृहमाययुः ॥
2.3.m: The sage Nārada, having imparted deceptive counsel to them there, / and through his instruction, none of them returned to their father's home.

2.3.s:
tacchrutvā kupito dakṣaḥ pitrāśvāsitamānasaḥ |
utpādya putrānprāyuṅkta sahasrapramitāṃstataḥ ||
2.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा कुपितो दक्षः पित्राश्वासितमानसः ।
उत्पाद्य पुत्रान्प्रायुङ्क्त सहस्रप्रमितांस्ततः ॥
2.3.m: Hearing this, Dakṣa became furious; but consoled in mind by his father, / he begot sons and dispatched thousands of them thereafter.

2.3.s:
te'pi tatra gatāḥ putrāḥ tapo'rthaṃ piturājñayā |
nārado'pi yayau tatra punastatsvopadeśakṛt ||
2.3.d:
तेऽपि तत्र गताः पुत्राः तपोऽर्थं पितुराज्ञया ।
नारदोऽपि ययौ तत्र पुनस्तत्स्वोपदेशकृत् ॥
2.3.m: Those sons also went there by their father's command to practice austerity; / and Nārada went there too, once again imparting his instruction.

2.3.s:
dadau tadupadeśaṃ te tebhyo bhrātṛpathaṃ yayuḥ |
āyayurna piturgehaṃ bhikṣuvṛttiratāśca te ||
2.3.d:
ददौ तदुपदेशं ते तेभ्यो भ्रातृपथं ययुः ।
आययुर्न पितुर्गेहं भिक्षुवृत्तिरताश्च ते ॥
2.3.m: He gave them the same instruction, and they followed the path of their brothers; / devoted to the lifestyle of mendicants, they did not return to their father's house.

2.3.s:
itthaṃ nāradasadvṛttirviśrutā śailakanyake |
anyāṃ śṛṇu hi tadvṛttiṃ vairāgyakaraṇīṃ nṛṇām ||
2.3.d:
इत्थं नारदसद्वृत्तिर्विश्रुता शैलकन्यके ।
अन्यां शृणु हि तद्वृत्तिं वैराग्यकरणीं नृणाम् ॥
2.3.m: Such is the famous conduct of Nārada, O daughter of the mountain! / Now hear about his other conduct, which produces detachment in men.

2.3.s:
vidyādharaścitraketuryo babhūva purākarot |
svopadeśamayaṃ dattvā tasmai śūnyaṃ ca tadgṛham ||
2.3.d:
विद्याधरश्चित्रकेतुर्यो बभूव पुराकरोत् ।
स्वोपदेशमयं दत्त्वा तस्मै शून्यं च तद्गृहम् ॥
2.3.m: Formerly there was the vidyādhara Citraketu; / by giving his instruction to him, he made his home empty.

2.3.s:
prahlādāya svopadeśānhiraṇyakaśipoḥ param |
dattvā duḥkhaṃ dadau cāyaṃ parabuddhiprabhedakaḥ ||
2.3.d:
प्रह्लादाय स्वोपदेशान्हिरण्यकशिपोः परम् ।
दत्त्वा दुःखं ददौ चायं परबुद्धिप्रभेदकः ॥
2.3.m: Giving his instruction to Prahlāda after that of Hiraṇyakaśipu, / he caused sorrow; he is indeed one who corrupts the minds of others.

2.3.s:
muninā nijavidyā yacchrāvitā karṇarocanā |
sa svagehaṃ vihāyāśu bhikṣāṃ carati prāyaśaḥ ||
2.3.d:
मुनिना निजविद्या यच्छ्राविता कर्णरोचना ।
स स्वगेहं विहायाशु भिक्षां चरति प्रायशः ॥
2.3.m: Whoever is made to hear his pleasing lore by that sage / quickly abandons his own home and generally wanders about begging for alms.

2.3.s:
nārado malinātmā hi sarvadojjvaladehavān |
jānīmastaṃ viśeṣeṇa vayaṃ tatsahavāsinaḥ ||
2.3.d:
नारदो मलिनात्मा हि सर्वदोज्ज्वलदेहवान् ।
जानीमस्तं विशेषेण वयं तत्सहवासिनः ॥
2.3.m: Nārada has an impure soul, though always possessing a radiant body. / We who dwell with him know him especially well.

2.3.s:
bakaṃ sādhuṃ varṇayanti na matsyānatti sarvathā |
sahavāsī vijānīyāccaritraṃ sahavāsinām ||
2.3.d:
बकं साधुं वर्णयन्ति न मत्स्यानत्ति सर्वथा ।
सहवासी विजानीयाच्चरित्रं सहवासिनाम् ॥
2.3.m: They describe the crane as pious, [saying] it never eats fish. / A fellow-dweller alone knows the character of his companions.

2.3.s:
labdhvā tadupadeśaṃ hi tvamapi prājñasammatā |
vṛthaiva mūrkhībhūtā tvaṃ tapaścarasi duṣkaram ||
2.3.d:
लब्ध्वा तदुपदेशं हि त्वमपि प्राज्ञसम्मता ।
वृथैव मूर्खीभूता त्वं तपश्चरसि दुष्करम् ॥
2.3.m: Having received his instruction, you too, though regarded as wise, / have in vain become foolish and are practicing severe austerity.

2.3.s:
yadarthamīdṛśaṃ bāle karoṣi vipulaṃ tapaḥ |
sodāsīno nirvikāro madanārirna saṃśayaḥ ||
2.3.d:
यदर्थमीदृशं बाले करोषि विपुलं तपः ।
सोदासीनो निर्विकारो मदनारिर्न संशयः ॥
2.3.m: He for whose sake you are performing such vast austerity, O child, / is unconcerned, free from modifications, the enemy of Madana—there is no doubt.

2.3.s:
amaṅgalavapurdhārī nirlajjo'sadano'kulī |
kuveṣī pretabhūtādisaṅgī nagno hi śūlabhṛt ||
2.3.d:
अमङ्गलवपुर्धारी निर्लज्जोऽसदनोऽकुली ।
कुवेषी प्रेतभूतादिसङ्गी नग्नो हि शूलभृत् ॥
2.3.m: He bears an inauspicious body, is shameless, homeless, of no family, / ill-attired, a companion of ghosts and spirits, naked, and a bearer of the trident.

2.3.s:
sa dhūrtastava vijñānaṃ vināśya nijamāyayā |
mohayāmāsa sadyuktyā kārayāmāsa vai tapaḥ ||
īdṛśaṃ hi varaṃ labdhvā kiṃ sukhaṃ sambhaviṣyati |
vicāraṃ kuru deveśi tvameva girijātmaje ||
2.3.d:
स धूर्तस्तव विज्ञानं विनाश्य निजमायया ।
मोहयामास सद्युक्त्या कारयामास वै तपः ॥
ईदृशं हि वरं लब्ध्वा किं सुखं सम्भविष्यति ।
विचारं कुरु देवेशि त्वमेव गिरिजात्मजे ॥
2.3.m:
That rogue destroyed your wisdom with his delusion, / deluded you with specious reasoning, and made you perform austerity.

Having obtained such a bridegroom, what happiness will there be? / Reflect carefully on this yourself, O ruler of the gods, daughter of the mountain!

2.3.s:
prathamaṃ dakṣajāṃ sādhvīṃ vivāhya sudhiyā satīm |
nirvāhaṃ kṛtavānnaiva mūḍhaḥ kiñciddināni hi ||
2.3.d:
प्रथमं दक्षजां साध्वीं विवाह्य सुधिया सतीम् ।
निर्वाहं कृतवान्नैव मूढः किञ्चिद्दिनानि हि ॥
2.3.m: First, having married Dakṣa’s daughter, the virtuous and intelligent Satī, / that fool did not sustain [her] even for a few days.

2.3.s:
tāṃ tathaiva sa vai doṣaṃ dattvātyākṣīt svayaṃ prabhuḥ |
dhyāyansvarūpamakalamaśokamaramatsukhī ||
2.3.d:
तां तथैव स वै दोषं दत्त्वात्याक्षीत् स्वयं प्रभुः ।
ध्यायन्स्वरूपमकलमशोकमरमत्सुखी ॥
2.3.m: Assigning blame to her in that very manner, that lord abandoned her himself; / meditating upon his spotless nature, free from sorrow, rejoicing in himself and happy.

2.3.s:
ekalaḥ paranirvāṇo hyasaṅgo'dvaya eva ca |
tena nāryāḥ kathaṃ devi nirvāhaḥ sambhaviṣyati ||
2.3.d:
एकलः परनिर्वाणो ह्यसङ्गोऽद्वय एव च ।
तेन नार्याः कथं देवि निर्वाहः सम्भविष्यति ॥
2.3.m: He is solitary, supremely liberated, unattached, and non-dual; / how then, O goddess, can sustenance be possible for a woman through him?

2.3.s:
adyāpi śāsanaṃ prāpya gṛhamāyāhi durmatim |
tyajāsmākaṃ mahābhāge bhaviṣyati ca śaṃ tava ||
2.3.d:
अद्यापि शासनं प्राप्य गृहमायाहि दुर्मतिम् ।
त्यजास्माकं महाभागे भविष्यति च शं तव ॥
2.3.m: Even today, accept our advice and return home; abandon this foolish thought / of ours, O noble lady, and good fortune will be yours.

2.3.s:
tvadyogyo hi varo viṣṇuḥ sarvasadguṇavānprabhuḥ |
vaikuṇṭhavāsī lakṣmīśo nānākrīḍāviśāradaḥ ||
2.3.d:
त्वद्योग्यो हि वरो विष्णुः सर्वसद्गुणवान्प्रभुः ।
वैकुण्ठवासी लक्ष्मीशो नानाक्रीडाविशारदः ॥
2.3.m: Viṣṇu is indeed a groom worthy of you, a lord possessing all good qualities, / dwelling in Vaikuṇṭha, lord of Lakṣmī, and skilled in various pastimes.

2.3.s:
tena te kārayiṣyāmo vivāhaṃ sarvasaukhyadam |
itīdṛśaṃ tyaja haṭhaṃ sukhitā bhava pārvati ||
2.3.d:
तेन ते कारयिष्यामो विवाहं सर्वसौख्यदम् ।
इतीदृशं त्यज हठं सुखिता भव पार्वति ॥
2.3.m: We will arrange your marriage with him, which will bestow all happiness. / Therefore, abandon such stubbornness and be happy, O Pārvatī!

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā pārvatī jagadambikā |
vihasya ca punaḥ prāha munīnjñānaviśāradān ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा पार्वती जगदम्बिका ।
विहस्य च पुनः प्राह मुनीन्ज्ञानविशारदान् ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard these words, Pārvatī, the mother of the universe, / smiled and spoke again to the sages skilled in wisdom.

2.3.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
satyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kathitaṃ svajñānena munīśvarāḥ |
parantu me haṭho naiva mukto bhavati he dvijāḥ ||
2.3.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
सत्यं भवद्भिः कथितं स्वज्ञानेन मुनीश्वराः ।
परन्तु मे हठो नैव मुक्तो भवति हे द्विजाः ॥
2.3.m: Pārvatī said: / Truth has been spoken by you according to your own wisdom, O lords of sages; / but my stubborn resolve cannot be abandoned, O twice-born ones.

2.3.s:
svatanoḥ śailajātatvātkāṭhinyaṃ sahajaṃ sthitam |
itthaṃ vicārya sudhiyā māṃ niṣeddhuṃ na cārhatha ||
2.3.d:
स्वतनोः शैलजातत्वात्काठिन्यं सहजं स्थितम् ।
इत्थं विचार्य सुधिया मां निषेद्धुं न चार्हथ ॥
2.3.m: Since my body was born from the mountain, hardness is inherent in it; / having considered this with good intellect, you ought not to forbid me.

2.3.s:
surarṣervacanaṃ pathyaṃ tyakṣye naiva kadācana |
gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ pathyamiti vedavido viduḥ ||
2.3.d:
सुरर्षेर्वचनं पथ्यं त्यक्ष्ये नैव कदाचन ।
गुरूणां वचनं पथ्यमिति वेदविदो विदुः ॥
2.3.m: I will never abandon the salutary word of the celestial sage; / the knowers of the Veda know that the word of spiritual preceptors is salutary.

2.3.s:
gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ satyamiti yeṣāṃ dṛḍhā matiḥ |
teṣāmihāmutra sukhaṃ paramaṃ nāsukhaṃ kvacit ||
2.3.d:
गुरूणां वचनं सत्यमिति येषां दृढा मतिः ।
तेषामिहामुत्र सुखं परमं नासुखं क्वचित् ॥
2.3.m: Those whose minds are firmly fixed that the word of spiritual preceptors is true / have supreme happiness here and in the hereafter, and never any sorrow.

2.3.s:
gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ satyamiti yaddhṛdaye na dhīḥ |
ihāmutrāpi teṣāṃ hi duḥkhaṃ na ca sukhaṃ kvacit ||
2.3.d:
गुरूणां वचनं सत्यमिति यद्धृदये न धीः ।
इहामुत्रापि तेषां हि दुःखं न च सुखं क्वचित् ॥
2.3.m: Those in whose heart there is no conviction that the word of spiritual preceptors is true / have only sorrow here and in the hereafter, and never any happiness.

2.3.s:
sarvathā na parityājyaṃ gurūṇāṃ vacanaṃ dvijāḥ |
gṛhaṃ vasedvā śūnyaṃ syānme haṭhaḥ sukhadaḥ sadā ||
2.3.d:
सर्वथा न परित्याज्यं गुरूणां वचनं द्विजाः ।
गृहं वसेद्वा शून्यं स्यान्मे हठः सुखदः सदा ॥
2.3.m: The word of spiritual preceptors must never be abandoned by any means, O twice-born ones; / whether one lives in a home or it becomes empty, my resolve will always bring happiness.

2.3.s:
yadbhavadbhiḥ subhaṇitaṃ vacanaṃ munisattamāḥ |
tadanyathā tadvivekaṃ varṇayāmi samāsataḥ ||
2.3.d:
यद्भवद्भिः सुभणितं वचनं मुनिसत्तमाः ।
तदन्यथा तद्विवेकं वर्णयामि समासतः ॥
2.3.m: As for the speech well spoken by you, O best of sages, / it is otherwise; I shall explain that discrimination briefly.

2.3.s:
guṇālayo vihārī ca viṣṇuḥ satyaṃ prakīrtitaḥ |
sadāśivo'guṇaḥ proktastatra kāraṇamucyate ||
2.3.d:
गुणालयो विहारी च विष्णुः सत्यं प्रकीर्तितः ।
सदाशिवोऽगुणः प्रोक्तस्तत्र कारणमुच्यते ॥
2.3.m: Viṣṇu is truly proclaimed as an abode of attributes and given to sport; / Sadāśiva is said to be devoid of attributes; the reason for that is explained.

2.3.s:
śivo brahmāvikāraḥ sa bhaktahetordhṛtākṛtiḥ |
prabhutāṃ laukikīṃ naiva sandarśayitumicchati ||
2.3.d:
शिवो ब्रह्माविकारः स भक्तहेतोर्धृताकृतिः ।
प्रभुतां लौकिकीं नैव सन्दर्शयितुमिच्छति ॥
2.3.m: Śiva is Brahman without modification; he assumes a form for the sake of devotees; / he does not wish to display worldly sovereignty.

2.3.s:
ataḥ paramahaṃsānāṃ dhāryate supriyā gatiḥ |
avadhūtasvarūpeṇa parānandena śambhunā ||
2.3.d:
अतः परमहंसानां धार्यते सुप्रिया गतिः ।
अवधूतस्वरूपेण परानन्देन शम्भुना ॥
2.3.m: Therefore, the delightful state of supreme ascetics is maintained / by Śambhu, whose nature is that of an avadhūta, full of supreme bliss.

2.3.s:
bhūṣaṇādirucirmāyāliptānāṃ brahmaṇo na ca |
sa prabhurnirguṇo'jo nirmāyo'lakṣyagatirvirāṭ ||
2.3.d:
भूषणादिरुचिर्मायालिप्तानां ब्रह्मणो न च ।
स प्रभुर्निर्गुणोऽजो निर्मायोऽलक्ष्यगतिर्विराट् ॥
2.3.m: A taste for ornaments and the like belongs to those tainted by illusion, not to Brahman; / that lord is without attributes, unborn, devoid of illusion, with unperceivable paths, the vast universal form.

2.3.s:
dharmajātyādibhiḥ śambhurnānugṛhṇāti vai dvijāḥ |
guroranugraheṇaiva śivaṃ jānāmi tattvataḥ ||
2.3.d:
धर्मजात्यादिभिः शम्भुर्नानुगृह्णाति वै द्विजाः ।
गुरोरनुग्रहेणैव शिवं जानामि तत्त्वतः ॥
2.3.m: Śambhu does not show grace on account of duty, caste, and so forth, O twice-born ones; / only through the grace of my guru do I know Śiva in truth.

2.3.s:
cecchivaḥ sa hi me viprā vivāhaṃ na kariṣyati |
avivāhā sadāhaṃ syāṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham ||
2.3.d:
चेच्छिवः स हि मे विप्रा विवाहं न करिष्यति ।
अविवाहा सदाहं स्यां सत्यं सत्यं वदाम्यहम् ॥
2.3.m: Even if that Śiva will not marry me, O vipras, / I shall remain unmarried forever; truth, truth I speak!

2.3.s:
udayati yadi bhānuḥ paścime digvibhāge pracalati yadi meruḥ śītatāṃ yāti vahniḥ |
vikasati yadi padmaṃ parvatāgre śilāyāṃ na hi calati haṭho me satyametadbravīmi ||
2.3.d:
उदयति यदि भानुः पश्चिमे दिग्विभागे प्रचलति यदि मेरुः शीततां याति वह्निः ।
विकसति यदि पद्मं पर्वताग्रे शिलायां न हि चलति हठो मे सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ॥
2.3.m: Even if the sun rises in the western direction, even if Meru moves, even if fire becomes cold, / even if a lotus blooms on a rock at the summit of a mountain, my resolve will never waver—this I speak truly!

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā tānpraṇamyāśu munīnsā parvatātmajā |
virarāma śivaṃ smṛtvā nirvikāreṇa cetasā ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा तान्प्रणम्याशु मुनीन्सा पर्वतात्मजा ।
विरराम शिवं स्मृत्वा निर्विकारेण चेतसा ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus and quickly bowed to those sages, that daughter of the mountain / ceased speaking, remembering Śiva with an unperturbed mind.

2.3.s:
ṛṣayo'pītthamājñāya girijāyāḥ suniścayam |
procurjayagiraṃ tatra daduścāśiṣamuttamām ||
2.3.d:
ऋषयोऽपीत्थमाज्ञाय गिरिजायाः सुनिश्चयम् ।
प्रोचुर्जयगिरं तत्र ददुश्चाशिषमुत्तमाम् ॥
2.3.m: The ṛṣis, too, having thus known the firm resolve of the daughter of the mountain, / shouted cries of victory there and bestowed their highest blessing.

2.3.s:
atha praṇamya tāṃ devīṃ munayo hṛṣṭamānasāḥ |
śivasthānaṃ drutaṃ jagmustatparīkṣākarā mune ||
2.3.d:
अथ प्रणम्य तां देवीं मुनयो हृष्टमानसाः ।
शिवस्थानं द्रुतं जग्मुस्तत्परीक्षाकरा मुने ॥
2.3.m: Then, having bowed to that goddess, the sages, glad in their minds, / quickly went to the abode of Śiva, having carried out his test, O sage.

2.3.s:
tatra gatvā śivaṃ natvā vṛttāntaṃ vinivedya tat |
tadājñāṃ samanuprāpya svarlokaṃ jagmurādarāt ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
तत्र गत्वा शिवं नत्वा वृत्तान्तं विनिवेद्य तत् ।
तदाज्ञां समनुप्राप्य स्वर्लोकं जग्मुरादरात् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
Going there, bowing to Śiva, and reporting that account to him, / they received his permission and respectfully departed for the celestial world.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Test by the Seven Sages', in the Pārvatī section of the Rudrasaṃhitā, the second [part] of the auspicious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
gateṣu teṣu muniṣu svaṃ lokaṃ śaṅkaraḥ svayam |
parīkṣituṃ tapo devyā aicchatsūtikaraḥ prabhuḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
गतेषु तेषु मुनिषु स्वं लोकं शङ्करः स्वयम् ।
परीक्षितुं तपो देव्या ऐच्छत्सूतिकरः प्रभुः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / When those sages had departed to their own realm, Śaṅkara himself, / the creator-lord, wished to test the goddess’s austerity.

2.3.s:
parīkṣāchadmanā śambhurdraṣṭuṃ tāṃ tuṣṭamānasaḥ |
jaṭilaṃ rūpamāsthāya sa yayau pārvatīvanam ||
2.3.d:
परीक्षाछद्मना शम्भुर्द्रष्टुं तां तुष्टमानसः ।
जटिलं रूपमास्थाय स ययौ पार्वतीवनम् ॥
2.3.m: Under the guise of a test, Śambhu, pleased in mind to see her, / assumed the form of an ascetic with matted hair and went to Pārvatī's forest.

2.3.s:
atīva sthaviro vipradehadhārī svatejasā |
prajvalanmanasā hṛṣṭo daṇḍī chatrī babhūva saḥ ||
2.3.d:
अतीव स्थविरो विप्रदेहधारी स्वतेजसा ।
प्रज्वलन्मनसा हृष्टो दण्डी छत्री बभूव सः ॥
2.3.m: Bearing the body of a very old brahmin, radiant with his own splendor, / he was delighted in mind, carrying a staff and an umbrella.

2.3.s:
tatrāpaśyatsthitāṃ devīṃ sakhībhiḥ parivāritām |
vedikopari śuddhāṃ tāṃ śivāmiva vidhoḥ kalām ||
2.3.d:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितां देवीं सखीभिः परिवारिताम् ।
वेदिकोपरि शुद्धां तां शिवामिव विधोः कलाम् ॥
2.3.m: There he saw the goddess seated upon an altar, surrounded by her female companions, / pure, like the auspicious crescent of the moon.

2.3.s:
śambhurnirīkṣya tāṃ devīṃ brahmacārisvarūpavān |
upakaṇṭhaṃ yayau prītyā tadāsau bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
2.3.d:
शम्भुर्निरीक्ष्य तां देवीं ब्रह्मचारिस्वरूपवान् ।
उपकण्ठं ययौ प्रीत्या तदासौ भक्तवत्सलः ॥
2.3.m: Beholding that goddess, Śambhu, having assumed the form of a student of the Veda, / then went near with affection, that one affectionate toward devotees.

2.3.s:
āgataṃ taṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇaṃ tejasādbhutam |
apūjayacchivā devī sarvapūjopahārakaiḥ ||
2.3.d:
आगतं तं तदा दृष्ट्वा ब्राह्मणं तेजसाद्भुतम् ।
अपूजयच्छिवा देवी सर्वपूजोपहारकैः ॥
2.3.m: Seeing that brāhmaṇa arrived then, wondrous in his splendor, / the goddess Śivā worshipped him with all offerings of worship.

2.3.s:
susatkṛtaṃ saṃvidhābhiḥ pūjitaṃ parayā mudā |
pārvatī kuśalaṃ prītyā papraccha dvijamādarāt ||
2.3.d:
सुसत्कृतं संविधाभिः पूजितं परया मुदा ।
पार्वती कुशलं प्रीत्या पप्रच्छ द्विजमादरात् ॥
2.3.m: Having duly honored him with hospitalities and worshipped him with supreme joy, / Pārvatī inquired with affection and respect about the twice-born's well-being:

2.3.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
brahmacārisvarūpeṇa kastvaṃ hi kuta āgataḥ |
idaṃ vanaṃ bhāsayase vada vedavidāṃ vara ||
2.3.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
ब्रह्मचारिस्वरूपेण कस्त्वं हि कुत आगतः ।
इदं वनं भासयसे वद वेदविदां वर ॥
2.3.m: Pārvatī said: / Who are you indeed in the form of a student of the Veda, and from where have you come? / You illuminate this forest; speak, best among knowers of the Veda!

2.3.s:
vipra uvāca |
ahamicchābhigāmī ca vṛddho vipratanuḥ sudhīḥ |
tapasvī sukhado'nyeṣāmupakārī na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.3.d:
विप्र उवाच ।
अहमिच्छाभिगामी च वृद्धो विप्रतनुः सुधीः ।
तपस्वी सुखदोऽन्येषामुपकारी न संशयः ॥
2.3.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / I wander wherever I please, an old wise man in a brāhmaṇa's body; / an ascetic, a granter of happiness to others, and a benefactor without doubt.

2.3.s:
kā tvaṃ kasyāsi tanayā kimarthaṃ vijane vane |
tapaścarasi durdharṣaṃ munibhiḥ prapadairapi ||
2.3.d:
का त्वं कस्यासि तनया किमर्थं विजने वने ।
तपश्चरसि दुर्धर्षं मुनिभिः प्रपदैरपि ॥
2.3.m: Who are you? Whose daughter are you? For what purpose in this solitary forest / do you perform severe austerity, unassailable even by sages on their tiptoes?

2.3.s:
na bālā na ca vṛddhāsi taruṇī bhāsi śobhanā |
kathaṃ patiṃ vinā tīkṣṇaṃ tapaścarasi vai vane ||
2.3.d:
न बाला न च वृद्धासि तरुणी भासि शोभना ।
कथं पतिं विना तीक्ष्णं तपश्चरसि वै वने ॥
2.3.m: You are neither a child nor old; you appear as a beautiful young woman. / Why do you perform fierce austerity in the forest without a husband?

2.3.s:
kiṃ tvaṃ tapasvinī bhadre kasyacitsahacāriṇī |
tapasvī sa na puṣṇāti devi tvāṃ ca gato'nyataḥ ||
2.3.d:
किं त्वं तपस्विनी भद्रे कस्यचित्सहचारिणी ।
तपस्वी स न पुष्णाति देवि त्वां च गतोऽन्यतः ॥
2.3.m: Are you a female ascetic, gentle lady, the companion of someone? / Has that ascetic gone elsewhere and does not support you, O goddess?

2.3.s:
vada kasya kule jātā kaḥ pitā tava kābhidhā |
mahāsaubhāgyarūpā tvaṃ vṛthā tava taporatiḥ ||
2.3.d:
वद कस्य कुले जाता कः पिता तव काभिधा ।
महासौभाग्यरूपा त्वं वृथा तव तपोरतिः ॥
2.3.m: Tell me, in whose family were you born? Who is your father? What is your name? / You possess great good fortune; in vain is your delight in austerity.

2.3.s:
kiṃ tvaṃ vedaprasūrlakṣmīḥ kiṃ surūpā sarasvatī |
etāsu madhye kā vā tvaṃ nāhaṃ tarkitumutsahe ||
2.3.d:
किं त्वं वेदप्रसूर्लक्ष्मीः किं सुरूपा सरस्वती ।
एतासु मध्ये का वा त्वं नाहं तर्कितुमुत्सहे ॥
2.3.m: Are you Lakṣmī, the mother of the Vedas, or beautiful Sarasvatī? / Which of these are you? I am unable to conjecture.

2.3.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
nāhaṃ vedaprasūrvipra na lakṣmīśca sarasvatī |
ahaṃ himācalasutā sāmprataṃ nāma pārvatī ||
2.3.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
नाहं वेदप्रसूर्विप्र न लक्ष्मीश्च सरस्वती ।
अहं हिमाचलसुता साम्प्रतं नाम पार्वती ॥
2.3.m: Pārvatī said: / I am not the mother of the Vedas, O brāhmaṇa, nor Lakṣmī, nor Sarasvatī. / I am the daughter of the Himālaya, presently named Pārvatī.

2.3.s:
purā dakṣasutā jātā satī nāmānyajanmani |
yogena tyaktadehāhaṃ yatpitrā ninditaḥ patiḥ ||
2.3.d:
पुरा दक्षसुता जाता सती नामान्यजन्मनि ।
योगेन त्यक्तदेहाहं यत्पित्रा निन्दितः पतिः ॥
2.3.m: Formerly, in another birth, I was born as Dakṣa's daughter named Satī. / I abandoned my body through yoga because my husband was reviled by my father.

2.3.s:
atra janmani samprāptaḥ śivo'pi vidhivaibhavāt |
māṃ tyaktvā bhasmasātkṛtya manmathaṃ sa jagāma ha ||
2.3.d:
अत्र जन्मनि सम्प्राप्तः शिवोऽपि विधिवैभवात् ।
मां त्यक्त्वा भस्मसात्कृत्य मन्मथं स जगाम ह ॥
2.3.m: In this birth, even though Śiva was obtained through the power of destiny, / he departed, having burned Manmatha to ashes and abandoned me.

2.3.s:
prayāte śaṅkare tāpodvijitāhaṃ piturgṛhāt |
āgatā tapase vipra sudṛḍhā svarṇadītaṭe ||
2.3.d:
प्रयाते शङ्करे तापोद्विजिताहं पितुर्गृहात् ।
आगता तपसे विप्र सुदृढा स्वर्णदीतटे ॥
2.3.m: When Śaṅkara had departed, distressed by torment, I came / from my father's house to the bank of the heavenly river, O brāhmaṇa, steadfast for austerity.

2.3.s:
kṛtvā tapaḥ kaṭhoraṃ ca suciraṃ prāṇavallabham |
na prāpyāgnau vivikṣantī tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃsthitā kṣaṇam ||
2.3.d:
कृत्वा तपः कठोरं च सुचिरं प्राणवल्लभम् ।
न प्राप्याग्नौ विविक्षन्ती त्वां दृष्ट्वा संस्थिता क्षणम् ॥
2.3.m: Having performed severe austerity for a very long time, and not obtaining the beloved of my life, / wishing to enter the fire, I have paused for a moment having seen you.

2.3.s:
gaccha tvaṃ praviśāmyagnau śivenāṅgīkṛtā na hi |
yatra yatra janurlapsye variṣyāmi śivaṃ varam ||
2.3.d:
गच्छ त्वं प्रविशाम्यग्नौ शिवेनाङ्गीकृता न हि ।
यत्र यत्र जनुर्लप्स्ये वरिष्यामि शिवं वरम् ॥
2.3.m: Go, for I shall enter the fire, since I have not been accepted by Śiva. / Wherever I take birth, I shall choose Śiva as my groom.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā pārvatī vahnau tatpuraḥ praviveśa sā |
niṣidhyamānā purato brāhmaṇena punaḥ punaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा पार्वती वह्नौ तत्पुरः प्रविवेश सा ।
निषिध्यमाना पुरतो ब्राह्मणेन पुनः पुनः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, Pārvatī entered the fire before him, / although she was being forbidden repeatedly by the brāhmaṇa before her.

2.3.s:
vahnipraveśaṃ kurvatyāḥ pārvatyāstatprabhāvataḥ |
babhūva tatkṣaṇaṃ sadyo vahniścandanapaṅkavat ||
2.3.d:
वह्निप्रवेशं कुर्वत्याः पार्वत्यास्तत्प्रभावतः ।
बभूव तत्क्षणं सद्यो वह्निश्चन्दनपङ्कवत् ॥
2.3.m: As Pārvatī was entering the fire, by her power, / in that very moment the fire instantly became like sandalwood paste.

2.3.s:
kṣaṇaṃ tadantare sthitvā hyutpatantīṃ divaṃ dvijaḥ |
punaḥ papraccha sahasā vihasansutanuṃ śivaḥ ||
2.3.d:
क्षणं तदन्तरे स्थित्वा ह्युत्पतन्तीं दिवं द्विजः ।
पुनः पप्रच्छ सहसा विहसन्सुतनुं शिवः ॥
2.3.m: Having remained inside it for a moment, as she was rising up to the sky, / the twice-born Śiva, smiling, quickly asked the slender-bodied lady again.

2.3.s:
dvija uvāca |
aho tapaste kiṃ bhadre na buddhaṃ kiñcideva hi |
na dagdho vahninā deho na ca prāptaṃ manīṣitam ||
2.3.d:
द्विज उवाच ।
अहो तपस्ते किं भद्रे न बुद्धं किञ्चिदेव हि ।
न दग्धो वह्निना देहो न च प्राप्तं मनीषितम् ॥
2.3.m: The twice-born said: / Ah, what austerity is yours, gentle lady? Nothing at all has been accomplished: / your body was not burned by the fire, nor was your desire attained.

2.3.s:
ataḥ satyaṃ nikāmaṃ vai vada devi manoratham |
mamāgre vipravaryasya sarvānandapradasya hi ||
2.3.d:
अतः सत्यं निकामं वै वद देवि मनोरथम् ।
ममाग्रे विप्रवर्यस्य सर्वानन्दप्रदस्य हि ॥
2.3.m: Therefore, speak your wish truly and fully, O goddess, / before me, an eminent brāhmaṇa, who bestows all joy.

2.3.s:
yathāvidhi tvayā devi kīrtyatāṃ sarvathātmanā |
tasmānmaitrī ca sañjātā kāryaṃ gopyaṃ tvayā na hi ||
2.3.d:
यथाविधि त्वया देवि कीर्त्यतां सर्वथात्मना ।
तस्मान्मैत्री च सञ्जाता कार्यं गोप्यं त्वया न हि ॥
2.3.m: Let it be recounted by you in full, O goddess, in accordance with the proper manner; / friendship has arisen between us, so your intention should not be concealed.

2.3.s:
kimicchasi varaṃ devi praṣṭumicchāmyataḥ param |
tvayyeva tadasau devi phalaṃ sarvaṃ pradṛśyate ||
2.3.d:
किमिच्छसि वरं देवि प्रष्टुमिच्छाम्यतः परम् ।
त्वय्येव तदसौ देवि फलं सर्वं प्रदृश्यते ॥
2.3.m: What boon do you desire, O goddess? I wish to ask further: / in you alone, O goddess, all fruit is clearly seen.

2.3.s:
parārthe ca tapaścedvai tiṣṭhettu tapa eva tat |
ratnaṃ haste samādāya hitvā kācastu sañcitaḥ ||
2.3.d:
परार्थे च तपश्चेद्वै तिष्ठेत्तु तप एव तत् ।
रत्नं हस्ते समादाय हित्वा काचस्तु सञ्चितः ॥
2.3.m: If austerity is for the sake of another, let that austerity remain so; / having taken a jewel in hand, you have cast it away and gathered glass.

2.3.s:
īdṛśaṃ tava saundaryaṃ kathaṃ vyarthīkṛtaṃ tvayā |
hitvā vastrāṇyanekāni carmādi ca dhṛtaṃ tvayā ||
2.3.d:
ईदृशं तव सौन्दर्यं कथं व्यर्थीकृतं त्वया ।
हित्वा वस्त्राण्यनेकानि चर्मादि च धृतं त्वया ॥
2.3.m: Why has such beauty of yours been rendered useless by you? / Casting off numerous garments, you have donned hide and the like!

2.3.s:
tatsarvaṃ kāraṇaṃ brūhi tapasastvasya satyataḥ |
tacchrutvā vipravaryo'haṃ yathā harṣamavāpnuyām ||
2.3.d:
तत्सर्वं कारणं ब्रूहि तपसस्त्वस्य सत्यतः ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा विप्रवर्योऽहं यथा हर्षमवाप्नुयाम् ॥
2.3.m: Tell in truth the entire reason for this austerity, / so that, having heard it, I, an eminent brāhmaṇa, may obtain joy.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
iti pṛṣṭā tadā tena sakhīṃ prairayatāmbikā |
tanmukhenaiva tatsarvaṃ kathayāmāsa suvratā ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इति पृष्टा तदा तेन सखीं प्रैरयताम्बिका ।
तन्मुखेनैव तत्सर्वं कथयामास सुव्रता ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Questioned thus by him then, Ambikā directed her female companion; / through her mouth alone she of good vows told everything.

2.3.s:
tayā ca preritā tatra pārvatyā vijayābhidhā |
prāṇapriyā suvratajñā sakhī jaṭilamabravīt ||
2.3.d:
तया च प्रेरिता तत्र पार्वत्या विजयाभिधा ।
प्राणप्रिया सुव्रतज्ञा सखी जटिलमब्रवीत् ॥
2.3.m: Prompted there by that Pārvatī, her companion named Vijayā, / dear as life and knowing good vows, spoke to the ascetic with matted locks:

2.3.s:
sakhyuvāca |
śṛṇu sādho pravakṣyāmi pārvatīcaritaṃ param |
hetuṃ ca tapasassarvaṃ yadi tvaṃ śrotumicchasi ||
2.3.d:
सख्युवाच ।
शृणु साधो प्रवक्ष्यामि पार्वतीचरितं परम् ।
हेतुं च तपसस्सर्वं यदि त्वं श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
2.3.m: The female companion said: / Listen, virtuous one, and I will narrate the supreme story of Pārvatī / and the entire cause of her austerity, if you wish to hear.

2.3.s:
sakhī me girirājasya suteyaṃ himabhūbhṛtaḥ |
khyātā vai pārvatī nāmnā tasyā mātāsti menakā ||
2.3.d:
सखी मे गिरिराजस्य सुतेयं हिमभूभृतः ।
ख्याता वै पार्वती नाम्ना तस्या मातास्ति मेनका ॥
2.3.m: This companion of mine is the daughter of the king of mountains, the Himālaya, / renowned by the name Pārvatī; her mother is Menakā.

2.3.s:
ūḍheyaṃ na ca kenāpi na vāñchati śivātparam |
trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi tapaścaraṇasādhinī ||
2.3.d:
ऊढेयं न च केनापि न वाञ्छति शिवात्परम् ।
त्रीणि वर्षसहस्राणि तपश्चरणसाधिनी ॥
2.3.m: She has not been wed by anyone, nor does she desire anyone other than Śiva; / she has been performing the practice of austerity for three thousand years.

2.3.s:
tadarthaṃ me'nayā sakhyā prārabdhaṃ tapa īdṛśam |
tadatra kāraṇaṃ vakṣye śṛṇu sādho dvijottama ||
2.3.d:
तदर्थं मेऽनया सख्या प्रारब्धं तप ईदृशम् ।
तदत्र कारणं वक्ष्ये शृणु साधो द्विजोत्तम ॥
2.3.m: For that purpose this austerity was undertaken by this friend of mine; / I shall explain the reason for that here; listen, virtuous one, best of the twice-born!

2.3.s:
hitvendrapramukhāndevān hariṃ brahmāṇameva ca |
patiṃ pinākapāṇiṃ vai prāptumicchati pārvatī ||
2.3.d:
हित्वेन्द्रप्रमुखान्देवान् हरिं ब्रह्माणमेव च ।
पतिं पिनाकपाणिं वै प्राप्तुमिच्छति पार्वती ॥
2.3.m: Leaving aside the gods led by Indra, Hari, and Brahmā himself, / Pārvatī wishes to obtain the wielder of the Pināka bow as her husband.

2.3.s:
iyaṃ sakhī madīyā vai vṛkṣānāropayatpurā |
teṣu sarveṣu sañjātaṃ phalapuṣpādikaṃ dvija ||
2.3.d:
इयं सखी मदीया वै वृक्षानारोपयत्पुरा ।
तेषु सर्वेषु सञ्जातं फलपुष्पादिकं द्विज ॥
2.3.m: This friend of mine planted trees formerly; / fruits, flowers, and the like have grown on all of them, O twice-born.

2.3.s:
rūpasārthāya janakakulālaṅkaraṇāya ca |
samuddiśya maheśānaṃ kāmasyānugrahāya ca ||
2.3.d:
रूपसार्थाय जनककुलालङ्करणाय च ।
समुद्दिश्य महेशानं कामस्यानुग्रहाय च ॥
2.3.m: For the fulfillment of her beauty and the ornamentation of her father's family, / aiming at the great lord and for the grace of Kāma,

2.3.s:
matsakhī nāradadeśāttapastapati dāruṇam |
manorathaṃ kutastasyā na phaliṣyati tāpasa ||
2.3.d:
मत्सखी नारददेशात्तपस्तपति दारुणम् ।
मनोरथं कुतस्तस्या न फलिष्यति तापस ॥
2.3.m: my friend performs fierce austerity on the instruction of Nārada. / How will her wish not bear fruit, O ascetic?

2.3.s:
yatte pṛṣṭaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha matsakhyā manasīpsitam |
mayā khyātaṃ ca tatprītyā kimanyacchrotumicchasi ||
2.3.d:
यत्ते पृष्टं द्विजश्रेष्ठ मत्सख्या मनसीप्सितम् ।
मया ख्यातं च तत्प्रीत्या किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
2.3.m: What you asked, best of the twice-born, regarding my friend's heartfelt wish, / has been declared by me with affection; what else do you wish to hear?

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā vijayāyā yathārthataḥ |
mune sa jaṭilo rudro vihasanvākyamabravīt ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा विजयाया यथार्थतः ।
मुने स जटिलो रुद्रो विहसन्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard these words of Vijayā according to the truth, / O sage, that ascetic with matted locks, Rudra, spoke smilingly:

2.3.s:
jaṭila uvāca |
sakhyedaṃ kathitaṃ tatra parihāso'numīyate |
yathārthaṃ cettadā devī svamukhenābhibhāṣatām ||
2.3.d:
जटिल उवाच ।
सख्येदं कथितं तत्र परिहासोऽनुमीयते ।
यथार्थं चेत्तदा देवी स्वमुखेनाभिभाषताम् ॥
2.3.m: The ascetic with matted locks said: / It seems this was spoken by your friend as a joke; / if it is true, then let the goddess speak with her own mouth.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityukte ca tadā tena jaṭilena dvijanmanā |
uvāca pārvatī devī svamukhenaiva taṃ dvijam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्ते च तदा तेन जटिलेन द्विजन्मना ।
उवाच पार्वती देवी स्वमुखेनैव तं द्विजम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
Brahmā said: / When spoken to thus by that twice-born ascetic with matted locks, / the goddess Pārvatī spoke to that twice-born with her own mouth.

Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, named 'The Dialogue between Śivā and the Ascetic with Matted Locks', in the Pārvatīkhaṇḍa, the third section of the second book, the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.3.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
śṛṇu dvijendra jaṭila madvṛttaṃ nikhilaṃ khalu |
sakhyuktaṃ me'dya yatsatyaṃ tattathaiva na cānyathā ||
2.3.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
शृणु द्विजेन्द्र जटिल मद्वृत्तं निखिलं खलु ।
सख्युक्तं मेऽद्य यत्सत्यं तत्तथैव न चान्यथा ॥
2.3.m: Pārvatī said: / Listen, best of the twice-born with matted locks, to my whole account indeed; / what was spoken today by my friend is true, exactly so and not otherwise.

2.3.s:
manasā vacasā sākṣātkarmaṇā patibhāvataḥ |
satyaṃ bravīmi no'satyaṃ vṛto vai śaṅkaro mayā ||
2.3.d:
मनसा वचसा साक्षात्कर्मणा पतिभावतः ।
सत्यं ब्रवीमि नोऽसत्यं वृतो वै शङ्करो मया ॥
2.3.m: In thought, speech, and visibly in deed, with the sentiment of a husband, / I speak the truth, not untruth: Śaṅkara has indeed been chosen by me.

2.3.s:
jānāmi durlabhaṃ vastu kathamprāpyaṃ mayā bhavet |
tathāpi mana autsukyāttapyate'dya tapo mayā ||
2.3.d:
जानामि दुर्लभं वस्तु कथम्प्राप्यं मया भवेत् ।
तथापि मन औत्सुक्यात्तप्यतेऽद्य तपो मया ॥
2.3.m: I know it is an unattainable thing—how could it be attained by me? / Even so, out of longing in my mind, austerity is practiced by me today.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā vacanaṃ tasmai sthitā sā girijā tadā |
uvāca brāhmaṇastatra tacchrutvā pārvatīvacaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं तस्मै स्थिता सा गिरिजा तदा ।
उवाच ब्राह्मणस्तत्र तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्वतीवचः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken these words to him, Girijā then fell silent. / Having heard Pārvatī's speech, the brahmin there said:

2.3.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca |
etāvatkālaparyantaṃ mamecchā mahatī hyabhūt |
kiṃ vastu kāṅkṣatī devī kurute sumahattapaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच ।
एतावत्कालपर्यन्तं ममेच्छा महती ह्यभूत् ।
किं वस्तु काङ्क्षती देवी कुरुते सुमहत्तपः ॥
2.3.m: The brahmin said: / "Indeed, up until now, I had a great desire to know / what thing the goddess desires that she performs such great austerity.

2.3.s:
tajjñātvā nikhilaṃ devi śrutvā tvanmukhapaṅkajāt |
ito gacchāmyahaṃ sthānādyathecchasi tathā kuru ||
2.3.d:
तज्ज्ञात्वा निखिलं देवि श्रुत्वा त्वन्मुखपङ्कजात् ।
इतो गच्छाम्यहं स्थानाद्यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
2.3.m: Having known all that, O goddess, having heard it from your lotus-mouth, / I will go from this place; do as you please.

2.3.s:
na kathyate tvayā mahyaṃ mitratvaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet |
yathā kāryaṃ tathā bhāvi kathanīyaṃ sukhena ca ||
2.3.d:
न कथ्यते त्वया मह्यं मित्रत्वं निष्फलं भवेत् ।
यथा कार्यं तथा भावि कथनीयं सुखेन च ॥
2.3.m: If it is not told by you to me, friendship becomes fruitless. / What is to be done must happen accordingly, and it should be spoken of with pleasure."

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā vacanaṃ tasya yāvadgantumiyeṣa saḥ |
tāvacca pārvatī devī praṇamyovāca taṃ dvijam ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं तस्य यावद्गन्तुमियेष सः ।
तावच्च पार्वती देवी प्रणम्योवाच तं द्विजम् ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken his speech, as he wished to leave, / the goddess Pārvatī bowed and addressed that twice-born:

2.3.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
kiṃ gamiṣyasi viprendra sthito bhava hitaṃ vada |
ityukte ca tayā tatra sthitvovāca sa daṇḍadhṛk ||
2.3.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
किं गमिष्यसि विप्रेन्द्र स्थितो भव हितं वद ।
इत्युक्ते च तया तत्र स्थित्वोवाच स दण्डधृक् ॥
2.3.m: Pārvatī said: / "Why will you leave, O best of brahmins? Stay and speak what is beneficial." / When this was spoken by her, he who held a staff stood there and said:

2.3.s:
dvija uvāca |
yadi śrotumanā devi māṃ sthāpayasi bhaktitaḥ |
vadāmi tattvaṃ tatsarvaṃ yena te vayunaṃ bhavet ||
2.3.d:
द्विज उवाच ।
यदि श्रोतुमना देवि मां स्थापयसि भक्तितः ।
वदामि तत्त्वं तत्सर्वं येन ते वयुनं भवेत् ॥
2.3.m: The twice-born said: / "If, intending to hear, O goddess, you make me stay out of devotion, / I shall tell you the truth of all that, so that you may have wisdom.

2.3.s:
jānāmyahaṃ mahādevaṃ sarvathā gurudharmataḥ |
pravadāmi yathārthaṃ hi sāvadhānatayā śṛṇu ||
2.3.d:
जानाम्यहं महादेवं सर्वथा गुरुधर्मतः ।
प्रवदामि यथार्थं हि सावधानतया शृणु ॥
2.3.m: I know Mahādeva completely through the duty toward the guru. / I tell you as it truly is; listen attentively.

2.3.s:
vṛṣadhvajo mahādevo bhasmadigdho jaṭādharaḥ |
vyāghracarmāmbaradharaḥ saṃvīto gajakṛttinā ||
2.3.d:
वृषध्वजो महादेवो भस्मदिग्धो जटाधरः ।
व्याघ्रचर्माम्बरधरः संवीतो गजकृत्तिना ॥
2.3.m: Vṛṣadhvaja, Mahādeva, is smeared with ashes and wears matted locks; / he wears a tiger-skin garment and is covered with an elephant hide.

2.3.s:
kapāladhārī sarpaughaiḥ sarvagātreṣu veṣṭitaḥ |
viṣadigdho'bhakṣyabhakṣo virūpākṣo vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
2.3.d:
कपालधारी सर्पौघैः सर्वगात्रेषु वेष्टितः ।
विषदिग्धोऽभक्ष्यभक्षो विरूपाक्षो विभीषणः ॥
2.3.m: He carries a skull, is wrapped around all his limbs by hosts of serpents, / smeared with poison, eats what should not be eaten, has deformed eyes, and is terrifying.

2.3.s:
avyaktajanmā satataṃ gṛhabhogavivarjitaḥ |
digambaro daśabhujo bhūtapretānvitassadā ||
2.3.d:
अव्यक्तजन्मा सततं गृहभोगविवर्जितः ।
दिगम्बरो दशभुजो भूतप्रेतान्वितस्सदा ॥
2.3.m: His birth is unmanifest, he is constantly devoid of domestic pleasures, / sky-clad, ten-armed, and always accompanied by ghosts and spirits.

2.3.s:
kena vā kāraṇena tvaṃ taṃ bhartāraṃ samīhase |
kva jñānaṃ te gataṃ devi tadvadādya vicārataḥ ||
2.3.d:
केन वा कारणेन त्वं तं भर्तारं समीहसे ।
क्व ज्ञानं ते गतं देवि तद्वदाद्य विचारतः ॥
2.3.m: For what reason, then, do you desire him as a husband? / Where has your discernment gone, O goddess? Tell me that today upon reflection.

2.3.s:
pūrvaṃ śrutaṃ mayā caiva vrataṃ tasya bhayaṅkaram |
śṛṇu te nigadāmyadya yadi te śravaṇe ruciḥ ||
2.3.d:
पूर्वं श्रुतं मया चैव व्रतं तस्य भयङ्करम् ।
शृणु ते निगदाम्यद्य यदि ते श्रवणे रुचिः ॥
2.3.m: Formerly, indeed, I heard of his dreadful practice. / Listen, I tell you today if you take pleasure in hearing.

2.3.s:
dakṣasya duhitā sādhvī satī vṛṣabhavāhanam |
vavre patiṃ purā daivāttatsambhogaḥ pariśrutaḥ ||
2.3.d:
दक्षस्य दुहिता साध्वी सती वृषभवाहनम् ।
वव्रे पतिं पुरा दैवात्तत्सम्भोगः परिश्रुतः ॥
2.3.m: Dakṣa's virtuous daughter Satī, in ancient times by fate, chose him who rides a bull / as her husband; the enjoyment of that has been heard of.

2.3.s:
kapālijāyeti satī dakṣeṇa parivarjitā |
yajñe bhāgapradānāya śambhuścāpi vivarjitaḥ ||
2.3.d:
कपालिजायेति सती दक्षेण परिवर्जिता ।
यज्ञे भागप्रदानाय शम्भुश्चापि विवर्जितः ॥
2.3.m: Thinking 'She is the wife of a skull-bearer', Satī was shunned by Dakṣa, / and Śambhu, too, was excluded from the offering of a share at the sacrifice.

2.3.s:
sā tathaivāpamānena bhṛśaṃ kopākulā satī |
tatyājāsūnpriyām̐statra tayā tyaktaśca śaṅkaraḥ ||
2.3.d:
सा तथैवापमानेन भृशं कोपाकुला सती ।
तत्याजासून्प्रियाम्̐स्तत्र तया त्यक्तश्च शङ्करः ॥
2.3.m: By that very insult, the virtuous Satī, deeply agitated by anger, / abandoned her dear breaths of life there, and Śaṅkara was abandoned by her.

2.3.s:
tvaṃ strīratnaṃ tava pitā rājā nikhilabhūbhṛtām |
tathāvidhaṃ patiṃ kasmādugreṇa tapasehase ||
2.3.d:
त्वं स्त्रीरत्नं तव पिता राजा निखिलभूभृताम् ।
तथाविधं पतिं कस्मादुग्रेण तपसेहसे ॥
2.3.m: You are a jewel among women, your father is king of all mountains; / why do you desire such a husband through fierce austerity?

2.3.s:
dattvā suvarṇamudrāṃ ca grahītuṃ kācamicchasi |
hitvā ca candanaṃ śubhraṃ kardamaṃ leptumicchasi ||
2.3.d:
दत्त्वा सुवर्णमुद्रां च ग्रहीतुं काचमिच्छसि ।
हित्वा च चन्दनं शुभ्रं कर्दमं लेप्तुमिच्छसि ॥
2.3.m: Having given a gold coin, you wish to take glass; / and having left aside white sandalwood, you wish to smear yourself with mud.

2.3.s:
sūryatejaḥ parityajya khadyotadyutimicchasi |
cīnāṃśukaṃ vihāyaiva carmāmbaramihecchasi ||
2.3.d:
सूर्यतेजः परित्यज्य खद्योतद्युतिमिच्छसि ।
चीनांशुकं विहायैव चर्माम्बरमिहेच्छसि ॥
2.3.m: Having abandoned the radiance of the sun, you desire the brilliance of a firefly; / casting off Chinese silk, you desire an animal skin here as a garment.

2.3.s:
gṛhavāsaṃ parityajya vanavāsaṃ samīhase |
lohamicchasi deveśi tyaktvā śevadhimuttamam ||
2.3.d:
गृहवासं परित्यज्य वनवासं समीहसे ।
लोहमिच्छसि देवेशि त्यक्त्वा शेवधिमुत्तमम् ॥
2.3.m: Having abandoned life in a home, you desire dwelling in a forest; / O ruler of the gods, having cast away the supreme treasure, you desire iron.

2.3.s:
indrādilokapālāṃśca hitvā śivamanuvratā |
naitatsūktaṃ hi lokeṣu viruddhaṃ dṛśyate'dhunā ||
2.3.d:
इन्द्रादिलोकपालांश्च हित्वा शिवमनुव्रता ।
नैतत्सूक्तं हि लोकेषु विरुद्धं दृश्यतेऽधुना ॥
2.3.m: Having abandoned Indra and the other world-protectors, you are devoted to Śiva; / this is surely not well-spoken among people; it is now seen to be contradictory.

2.3.s:
kva tvaṃ kamalapatrākṣī kvāsau vai trivilocanaḥ |
śaśāṅkavadanā tvaṃ ca pañcavaktraḥ śivaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
2.3.d:
क्व त्वं कमलपत्राक्षी क्वासौ वै त्रिविलोचनः ।
शशाङ्कवदना त्वं च पञ्चवक्त्रः शिवः स्मृतः ॥
2.3.m: Where are you, lotus-petal-eyed, and where is he, three-eyed? / You have a moon-like face, while Śiva is traditionally known to have five faces.

2.3.s:
veṇī śirasi te divyā sarpiṇīva vibhāsitā |
jaṭājūṭaṃ śivasyaiva prasiddhaṃ paricakṣate ||
2.3.d:
वेणी शिरसि ते दिव्या सर्पिणीव विभासिता ।
जटाजूटं शिवस्यैव प्रसिद्धं परिचक्षते ॥
2.3.m: The splendid braid on your head shines like a female serpent, / while Śiva's famous mass of matted hair is well described.

2.3.s:
candanaṃ ca tvadīyāṅge citābhasma śivasya ca |
kva dukūlaṃ tvadīyaṃ vai śāṅkaraṃ kva gajājinam ||
2.3.d:
चन्दनं च त्वदीयाङ्गे चिताभस्म शिवस्य च ।
क्व दुकूलं त्वदीयं वै शाङ्करं क्व गजाजिनम् ॥
2.3.m: There is sandalwood on your limbs, and funeral pyre ashes on Śiva's; / where is your fine silk garment, and where is Śaṅkara's elephant hide?

2.3.s:
kva bhūṣaṇāni divyāni kva sarpāḥ śaṅkarasya ca |
kva carā devatāḥsarvāḥ kva ca bhūtabalipriyaḥ ||
2.3.d:
क्व भूषणानि दिव्यानि क्व सर्पाः शङ्करस्य च ।
क्व चरा देवताःसर्वाः क्व च भूतबलिप्रियः ॥
2.3.m: Where are divine ornaments, and where are Śaṅkara's snakes? / Where are all the roaming deities, and where is he who loves offerings from spirits?

2.3.s:
kva vā mṛdaṅgavādaśca kva ca taḍḍamarustathā |
kva ca bherīkalāpaśca kva ca śṛṅgaravo'śubhaḥ ||
2.3.d:
क्व वा मृदङ्गवादश्च क्व च तड्डमरुस्तथा ।
क्व च भेरीकलापश्च क्व च शृङ्गरवोऽशुभः ॥
2.3.m: Where is the playing of the mṛdaṅga, and where is that ḍamaru drum? / Where is the cluster of kettle-drums, and where is the inauspicious sound of the horn?

2.3.s:
kva ca ḍhakkāmayaḥ śabdo galanādaḥ kva cāśubhaḥ |
bhavatyāśca śivasyaiva na yuktaṃ rūpamuttamam ||
2.3.d:
क्व च ढक्कामयः शब्दो गलनादः क्व चाशुभः ।
भवत्याश्च शिवस्यैव न युक्तं रूपमुत्तमम् ॥
2.3.m: Where is the sound made by a ḍhakkā drum, and where is the inauspicious sound from his throat? / The excellent form of yourself and of Śiva are not suited to each other.

2.3.s:
yadi dravyaṃ bhavettasya kathaṃ syātsa digambaraḥ |
vāhanaṃ ca balīvardaḥ sāmagrī kāpi tasya na ||
2.3.d:
यदि द्रव्यं भवेत्तस्य कथं स्यात्स दिगम्बरः ।
वाहनं च बलीवर्दः सामग्री कापि तस्य न ॥
2.3.m: If he had wealth, how could he be sky-clad? / And his mount is an ox; he has no possessions whatsoever.

2.3.s:
vareṣu ye guṇāḥ proktā nārīṇāṃ sukhadāyakāḥ |
tanmadhye hi virūpākṣe eko'pi na guṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
2.3.d:
वरेषु ये गुणाः प्रोक्ता नारीणां सुखदायकाः ।
तन्मध्ये हि विरूपाक्षे एकोऽपि न गुणः स्मृतः ॥
2.3.m: Among the qualities stated for bridegrooms that bring pleasure to women, / not even one quality is mentioned among them in the deformed-eyed one.

2.3.s:
tavāpi kāmo dayito dagdhastena hareṇa ca |
anādarastadā dṛṣṭo hitvā tvāmanyato gataḥ ||
2.3.d:
तवापि कामो दयितो दग्धस्तेन हरेण च ।
अनादरस्तदा दृष्टो हित्वा त्वामन्यतो गतः ॥
2.3.m: Even Kāma, so dear to you, was burnt by that Hara; / disrespect was seen then: abandoning you, he went elsewhere.

2.3.s:
jātirna dṛśyate tasya vidyājñānaṃ tathaiva ca |
sahāyāśca piśācā hi viṣaṃ kaṇṭhe hi dṛśyate ||
2.3.d:
जातिर्न दृश्यते तस्य विद्याज्ञानं तथैव च ।
सहायाश्च पिशाचा हि विषं कण्ठे हि दृश्यते ॥
2.3.m: His caste is not known, nor his learning and knowledge; / his companions are indeed goblins, and poison is visible in his throat.

2.3.s:
ekākī ca sadā nityaṃ virāgī ca viśeṣataḥ |
tasmāttvaṃ hi hareṇaiva mano yoktuṃ tu cārhasi ||
2.3.d:
एकाकी च सदा नित्यं विरागी च विशेषतः ।
तस्मात्त्वं हि हरेणैव मनो योक्तुं तु चार्हसि ॥
2.3.m: He is always solitary and especially dispassionate; / therefore, you should not fasten your mind to Hara.

2.3.s:
kva ca hārastvadīyo vai kva ca tanmuṇḍamālikā |
aṅgarāgaḥ kva te divyaḥ citābhasma kva tattanau ||
2.3.d:
क्व च हारस्त्वदीयो वै क्व च तन्मुण्डमालिका ।
अङ्गरागः क्व ते दिव्यः चिताभस्म क्व तत्तनौ ॥
2.3.m: Where is your necklace, and where is his garland of skulls? / Where is your divine cosmetic ointment, and where are pyre ashes on his body?

2.3.s:
sarvaṃ viruddhaṃ rūpādi tava devi harasya ca |
mahyaṃ na rocate hyetadyadicchasi tathā kuru ||
2.3.d:
सर्वं विरुद्धं रूपादि तव देवि हरस्य च ।
मह्यं न रोचते ह्येतद्यदिच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
2.3.m: Everything—form and the like—of you and of Hara is contradictory, O goddess; / this does not please me; do as you wish.

2.3.s:
asadvastu ca yatkiñcit tatsarvaṃ svayamīhase |
nivartaya manastasmānno cedicchasi tatkuru ||
2.3.d:
असद्वस्तु च यत्किञ्चित् तत्सर्वं स्वयमीहसे ।
निवर्तय मनस्तस्मान्नो चेदिच्छसि तत्कुरु ॥
2.3.m: Whatever is bad, all that you desire for yourself; / turn your mind away from that; or else, if you wish, do that."

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā tasya viprasya pārvatī |
uvāca kruddhamanasā śivanindāparaṃ dvijam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा तस्य विप्रस्य पार्वती ।
उवाच क्रुद्धमनसा शिवनिन्दापरं द्विजम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
Brahmā said: / Having heard such words from that brahmin, Pārvatī / spoke with an angry mind to the twice-born who was intent on reviling Śiva.

Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Deceitful Words of the Brahmacārin', in the Pārvatīkhaṇḍa, the third [section] in the second Rudrasaṃhitā of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.3.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
etāvaddhi mayā jñātaṃ kaścidanyo'yamāgataḥ |
idānīṃ sakalaṃ jñātamavadhyastvaṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
2.3.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
एतावद्धि मया ज्ञातं कश्चिदन्योऽयमागतः ।
इदानीं सकलं ज्ञातमवध्यस्त्वं विशेषतः ॥
2.3.m: Pārvatī said: / "Up until now I thought, 'Some other person has arrived'; / now all is known; you are especially not to be killed.

2.3.s:
tvayoktaṃ viditaṃ deva tadalīkaṃ na cānyathā |
yadi tvayoditaṃ syādvai viruddhaṃ nocyate tvayā ||
2.3.d:
त्वयोक्तं विदितं देव तदलीकं न चान्यथा ।
यदि त्वयोदितं स्याद्वै विरुद्धं नोच्यते त्वया ॥
2.3.m: What was said by you has become known, O god; that is not false nor otherwise; / if it was spoken by you, what is contrary is not spoken by you.

2.3.s:
kadāciddṛśyate tādṛk veṣadhārī maheśvaraḥ |
svalīlayā parabrahma svarāgopāttavigrahaḥ ||
2.3.d:
कदाचिद्दृश्यते तादृक् वेषधारी महेश्वरः ।
स्वलीलया परब्रह्म स्वरागोपात्तविग्रहः ॥
2.3.m: Sometimes Maheśvara is seen wearing such an appearance; / by his own play, the supreme Brahman has assumed a physical body through his own will.

2.3.s:
brahmacārisvarūpeṇa pratārayitumudyataḥ |
āgataśchalasaṃyuktaṃ vaco'vādīḥ kuyuktitaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मचारिस्वरूपेण प्रतारयितुमुद्यतः ।
आगतश्छलसंयुक्तं वचोऽवादीः कुयुक्तितः ॥
2.3.m: Taking the form of a brahmacārin, you are intent on deceiving me; / having arrived, you have spoken words accompanied by deceit through false reasoning.

2.3.s:
śaṅkarasya svarūpaṃ tu jānāmi suviśeṣataḥ |
śivatattvamato vacmi suvicārya yathārhataḥ ||
2.3.d:
शङ्करस्य स्वरूपं तु जानामि सुविशेषतः ।
शिवतत्त्वमतो वच्मि सुविचार्य यथार्हतः ॥
2.3.m: I know the true nature of Śaṅkara thoroughly; / therefore, having reflected properly, I speak of the reality of Śiva as is fitting.

2.3.s:
vastuto nirguṇo brahma saguṇaḥ kāraṇena saḥ |
kuto jātirbhavettasya nirguṇasya guṇātmanaḥ ||
2.3.d:
वस्तुतो निर्गुणो ब्रह्म सगुणः कारणेन सः ।
कुतो जातिर्भवेत्तस्य निर्गुणस्य गुणात्मनः ॥
2.3.m: In truth, Brahman is without qualities; with qualities he exists because of a cause. / Whence could there be caste for him who is without qualities, whose self consists of qualities?

2.3.s:
sa sarvāsāṃ hi vidyānāmadhiṣṭhānaṃ sadāśivaḥ |
kiṃ tasya vidyayā kāryaṃ pūrṇasya paramātmanaḥ ||
2.3.d:
स सर्वासां हि विद्यानामधिष्ठानं सदाशिवः ।
किं तस्य विद्यया कार्यं पूर्णस्य परमात्मनः ॥
2.3.m: Sadāśiva is indeed the foundation of all branches of knowledge; / what need has he, the complete Supreme Self, for learning?

2.3.s:
vedā ucchvāsarūpeṇa purā dattāśca viṣṇave |
śambhunā tena kalpādau tatsamaḥ ko'sti suprabhuḥ ||
2.3.d:
वेदा उच्छ्वासरूपेण पुरा दत्ताश्च विष्णवे ।
शम्भुना तेन कल्पादौ तत्समः कोऽस्ति सुप्रभुः ॥
2.3.m: The Vedas were formerly given in the form of breath to Viṣṇu / by that Śambhu at the beginning of the kalpa; who is an excellent lord equal to him?

2.3.s:
sarveṣāmādibhūtasya vayomānaṃ kutastataḥ |
prakṛtistu tato jātā kiṃ śaktestasya kāraṇam ||
2.3.d:
सर्वेषामादिभूतस्य वयोमानं कुतस्ततः ।
प्रकृतिस्तु ततो जाता किं शक्तेस्तस्य कारणम् ॥
2.3.m: For him who is the primal source of all, whence could there be an estimation of age? / Prakṛti indeed arose from him; what cause could there be for his power?

2.3.s:
ye bhajanti ca taṃ prītyā śaktīśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ sadā |
tasmai śaktitrayaṃ śambhuḥ sa dadāti sadāvyayam ||
2.3.d:
ये भजन्ति च तं प्रीत्या शक्तीशं शङ्करं सदा ।
तस्मै शक्तित्रयं शम्भुः स ददाति सदाव्ययम् ॥
2.3.m: And those who always worship with love that Śaṅkara, the lord of Śakti, / to such a one Śambhu grants the threefold power that is eternal and imperishable.

2.3.s:
tasyaiva bhajanājjīvo mṛtyuṃ jayati nirbhayaḥ |
tasmānmṛtyuñjayannāma prasiddhaṃ bhuvanatraye ||
2.3.d:
तस्यैव भजनाज्जीवो मृत्युं जयति निर्भयः ।
तस्मान्मृत्युञ्जयन्नाम प्रसिद्धं भुवनत्रये ॥
2.3.m: Only through devotion to him does the individual soul fearlessly conquer death; / therefore his name 'Mṛtyuñjaya' ('Conqueror of Death') is renowned throughout the three worlds.

2.3.s:
tasyaiva pakṣapātena viṣṇurviṣṇutvamāpnuyāt |
brahmatvaṃ ca yathā brahmā devā devatvameva ca ||
2.3.d:
तस्यैव पक्षपातेन विष्णुर्विष्णुत्वमाप्नुयात् ।
ब्रह्मत्वं च यथा ब्रह्मा देवा देवत्वमेव च ॥
2.3.m: Only by his favor does Viṣṇu attain his status as Viṣṇu, / Brahmā his status as Brahmā, and the gods their godhood as well.

2.3.s:
darśanārthaṃ śivasyādau yathā gacchati devarāṭ |
bhūtādayastatparasya dvārapālāḥ śivasya tu ||
2.3.d:
दर्शनार्थं शिवस्यादौ यथा गच्छति देवराट् ।
भूतादयस्तत्परस्य द्वारपालाः शिवस्य तु ॥
2.3.m: When the king of gods goes first to behold Śiva, / the spirits and others, who are devoted to him, are Śiva's doorkeepers.

2.3.s:
daṇḍaiśca mukuṭaṃ viddhaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ bhavati sarvataḥ |
kiṃ tasya bahupakṣeṇa svayameva mahāprabhuḥ ||
2.3.d:
दण्डैश्च मुकुटं विद्धं मृष्टं भवति सर्वतः ।
किं तस्य बहुपक्षेण स्वयमेव महाप्रभुः ॥
2.3.m: His crown is struck by their staves and becomes polished all around. / What need does he have of an extensive retinue? He is himself the great lord.

2.3.s:
kalyāṇarūpiṇastasya sevayeha na kiṃ bhavet |
kiṃ nyūnaṃ tasya devasya māmicchati sadāśivaḥ ||
2.3.d:
कल्याणरूपिणस्तस्य सेवयेह न किं भवेत् ।
किं न्यूनं तस्य देवस्य मामिच्छति सदाशिवः ॥
2.3.m: What would not come to pass through the service of him who is auspiciousness itself? / What deficiency does that god have, that Sadāśiva desires me?

2.3.s:
saptajanmadaridraḥ syātsevedyo yadi śaṅkaram |
tasyaitatsevanālloke lakṣmīḥ syādanapāyinī ||
2.3.d:
सप्तजन्मदरिद्रः स्यात्सेवेद्यो यदि शङ्करम् ।
तस्यैतत्सेवनाल्लोके लक्ष्मीः स्यादनपायिनी ॥
2.3.m: Even if one were destitute for seven lifetimes, should one worship Śaṅkara, / through his service fortune would become unfailing in this world.

2.3.s:
yadagre siddhayo'ṣṭau ca nityaṃ nṛtyanti toṣitum |
avāṅmukhāḥ sadā tatra taddhitaṃ durlabhaṃ kutaḥ ||
2.3.d:
यदग्रे सिद्धयोऽष्टौ च नित्यं नृत्यन्ति तोषितुम् ।
अवाङ्मुखाः सदा तत्र तद्धितं दुर्लभं कुतः ॥
2.3.m: Before whom the eight supernatural powers dance eternally with bowed heads / to bring him pleasure, whence could his own welfare be hard to attain?

2.3.s:
yadyasya maṅgalānīha sevate śaṅkarasya na |
yathāpi maṅgalaṃ tasya smaraṇādeva jāyate ||
2.3.d:
यद्यस्य मङ्गलानीह सेवते शङ्करस्य न ।
यथापि मङ्गलं तस्य स्मरणादेव जायते ॥
2.3.m: Though he himself pursues no auspicious things here, / nonetheless, auspiciousness arises from the mere remembrance of that Śaṅkara.

2.3.s:
yasya pūjāprabhāveṇa kāmāḥ siddhyanti sarvaśaḥ |
kuto vikārastasyāsti nirvikārasya sarvadā ||
2.3.d:
यस्य पूजाप्रभावेण कामाः सिद्ध्यन्ति सर्वशः ।
कुतो विकारस्तस्यास्ति निर्विकारस्य सर्वदा ॥
2.3.m: By the power of worshipping whom all desires are completely fulfilled, / whence could there be any perturbation in him who is eternally changeless?

2.3.s:
śiveti maṅgalaṃ nāma mukhe yasya nirantaram |
tasyaiva darśanādanye pavitrāḥ santi sarvadā ||
2.3.d:
शिवेति मङ्गलं नाम मुखे यस्य निरन्तरम् ।
तस्यैव दर्शनादन्ये पवित्राः सन्ति सर्वदा ॥
2.3.m: On whose lips the auspicious name 'Śiva' continuously rests, / by the mere sight of that person others are always purified.

2.3.s:
yadyapūtaṃ bhavedbhasma citāyāśca tvayoditam |
nityamasyāṅgagaṃ devaiḥ śirobhirdhāryate katham ||
2.3.d:
यद्यपूतं भवेद्भस्म चितायाश्च त्वयोदितम् ।
नित्यमस्याङ्गगं देवैः शिरोभिर्धार्यते कथम् ॥
2.3.m: If the ash from the funeral pyre were unholy, as you have claimed, / why is that which constantly clings to his body borne upon their heads by the gods?

2.3.s:
yo devo jagatāṃ kartā bhartā hartā guṇānvitaḥ |
nirguṇaḥ śivasaṃjñaśca sa vijñeyaḥ kathaṃ bhavet ||
2.3.d:
यो देवो जगतां कर्ता भर्ता हर्ता गुणान्वितः ।
निर्गुणः शिवसंज्ञश्च स विज्ञेयः कथं भवेत् ॥
2.3.m: The god who, endowed with qualities, is the creator, sustainer, and destroyer of the worlds, / and who, devoid of qualities, is named Śiva—how could he be known?

2.3.s:
aguṇaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ śivasya paramātmanaḥ |
tatkathaṃ hi vijānanti tvādṛśāstadbahirmukhāḥ ||
2.3.d:
अगुणं ब्रह्मणो रूपं शिवस्य परमात्मनः ।
तत्कथं हि विजानन्ति त्वादृशास्तद्बहिर्मुखाः ॥
2.3.m: The form of Brahman, of Śiva the supreme self, is beyond qualities; / how indeed can persons like you, turned away from him, understand it?

2.3.s:
durācārāśca pāpāśca vebhyaste vinirgatāḥ |
tattvaṃ te naiva jānanti śivasyāguṇarūpiṇaḥ ||
2.3.d:
दुराचाराश्च पापाश्च वेभ्यस्ते विनिर्गताः ।
तत्त्वं ते नैव जानन्ति शिवस्यागुणरूपिणः ॥
2.3.m: Those of wicked conduct and full of sin, who have strayed from the Vedas, / do not at all comprehend the reality of Śiva whose nature is devoid of qualities.

2.3.s:
śivanindāṃ karotīha tattvamajñāya yaḥ pumān |
ājanmasañcitaṃ puṇyaṃ bhasmībhavati tasya tat ||
2.3.d:
शिवनिन्दां करोतीह तत्त्वमज्ञाय यः पुमान् ।
आजन्मसञ्चितं पुण्यं भस्मीभवति तस्य तत् ॥
2.3.m: Whatever man here reviles Śiva without knowing his true nature, / the merit accumulated by him since birth turns to ashes.

2.3.s:
tvayā nindā kṛtā yātra harasyāmitatejasaḥ |
tvatpūjā ca kṛtā yanme tasmātpāpaṃ bhajāmyaham ||
2.3.d:
त्वया निन्दा कृता यात्र हरस्यामिततेजसः ।
त्वत्पूजा च कृता यन्मे तस्मात्पापं भजाम्यहम् ॥
2.3.m: Because you have uttered reproach here against Hara of immeasurable splendour, / and because I have paid you respect, I have incurred sin.

2.3.s:
śivavidveṣiṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sacailaṃ snānamācaret |
śivavidveṣiṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāyaścitaṃ samācaret ||
2.3.d:
शिवविद्वेषिणं दृष्ट्वा सचैलं स्नानमाचरेत् ।
शिवविद्वेषिणं दृष्ट्वा प्रायश्चितं समाचरेत् ॥
2.3.m: Upon seeing a hater of Śiva, one must bathe with one's clothes on; / upon seeing a hater of Śiva, one must perform an expiation.

2.3.s:
re re duṣṭa tvayā coktamahaṃ jānāmi śaṅkaram |
niścayena na vijñātaśśiva eva sanātanaḥ ||
2.3.d:
रे रे दुष्ट त्वया चोक्तमहं जानामि शङ्करम् ।
निश्चयेन न विज्ञातश्शिव एव सनातनः ॥
2.3.m: Ah, you wicked fellow! You said, 'I know Śaṅkara.' / In truth, eternal Śiva has not been comprehended by you at all.

2.3.s:
yathā tathā bhavedrudro yathā vā bahurūpavān |
mamābhīṣṭatamo nityaṃ nirvikārī satāṃ priyaḥ ||
2.3.d:
यथा तथा भवेद्रुद्रो यथा वा बहुरूपवान् ।
ममाभीष्टतमो नित्यं निर्विकारी सतां प्रियः ॥
2.3.m: However Rudra may be, or endowed with many forms, / he is eternally my most beloved, changeless and dear to the righteous.

2.3.s:
viṣṇurbrahmāpi na samaḥ tasya kvāpi mahātmanaḥ |
kuto'nye nirjarādyāśca kālādhīnāḥ sadaiva te ||
2.3.d:
विष्णुर्ब्रह्मापि न समः तस्य क्वापि महात्मनः ।
कुतोऽन्ये निर्जराद्याश्च कालाधीनाः सदैव ते ॥
2.3.m: Even Viṣṇu or Brahmā is nowhere equal to that great soul; / how then could other immortals and the like, who are always subject to Time?

2.3.s:
iti buddhyā samālokya svayā satyā sutattvataḥ |
śivārthaṃ vanamāgatya karomi vipulaṃ tapaḥ ||
2.3.d:
इति बुद्ध्या समालोक्य स्वया सत्या सुतत्त्वतः ।
शिवार्थं वनमागत्य करोमि विपुलं तपः ॥
2.3.m: Having reflected in this manner with my own true discernment, in exact accordance with reality, / I have come to the forest for Śiva's sake and am performing vast austerity.

2.3.s:
sa eva parameśānaḥ sarveśo bhaktavatsalaḥ |
samprāptuṃ me'bhilāṣo hi dīnānugrahakārakam ||
2.3.d:
स एव परमेशानः सर्वेशो भक्तवत्सलः ।
सम्प्राप्तुं मेऽभिलाषो हि दीनानुग्रहकारकम् ॥
2.3.m: He alone is Parameśāna, the lord of all, affectionate toward devotees; / my yearning is indeed to attain him who bestows grace upon the wretched.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā girijā sā hi girīśvarasutā mune |
virarāma śivaṃ dadhyau nirvikāreṇa cetasā ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा गिरिजा सा हि गिरीश्वरसुता मुने ।
विरराम शिवं दध्यौ निर्विकारेण चेतसा ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, O sage, Girijā, the daughter of the mountain lord, / fell silent and meditated upon Śiva with an unperturbed mind.

2.3.s:
tadākarṇya vaco devyā brahmacārī sa vai dvijaḥ |
punarvacanamākhyātuṃ yāvadeva pracakrame ||
2.3.d:
तदाकर्ण्य वचो देव्या ब्रह्मचारी स वै द्विजः ।
पुनर्वचनमाख्यातुं यावदेव प्रचक्रमे ॥
2.3.m: Hearing those words of the goddess, that twice-born brahmacārin / set about once again to speak words.

2.3.s:
uvāca girijā tāvatsvasakhīṃ vijayāṃ drutam |
śivasaktamanovṛttiḥ śivanindāparāṅmukhī ||
2.3.d:
उवाच गिरिजा तावत्स्वसखीं विजयां द्रुतम् ।
शिवसक्तमनोवृत्तिः शिवनिन्दापराङ्मुखी ॥
2.3.m: Then Girijā, the movement of whose mind was attached to Śiva / and averse to the reviling of Śiva, spoke quickly to her companion Vijayā:

2.3.s:
girijovāca |
vāraṇīyaḥ prayatnena sakhyayaṃ hi dvijādhamaḥ |
punarvaktumanāścaiva śivanindāṃ kariṣyati ||
2.3.d:
गिरिजोवाच ।
वारणीयः प्रयत्नेन सख्ययं हि द्विजाधमः ।
पुनर्वक्तुमनाश्चैव शिवनिन्दां करिष्यति ॥
2.3.m: Girijā said: / 'Friend, this vilest of the twice-born must be restrained with effort! / Wishing to speak again, he will surely revile Śiva.

2.3.s:
na kevalaṃ bhavetpāpaṃ nindāṃ kartuśśivasya hi |
yo vai śṛṇoti tannindāṃ pāpabhāk sa bhavediha ||
2.3.d:
न केवलं भवेत्पापं निन्दां कर्तुश्शिवस्य हि ।
यो वै शृणोति तन्निन्दां पापभाक् स भवेदिह ॥
2.3.m: Sin does not accrue merely to the one who reviles Śiva; / whoever listens to that reproach also partakes of sin in this world.

2.3.s:
śivanindākaro vadhyaḥ sarvathā śivakiṅkaraiḥ |
brāhmaṇaścetsa vai tyājyo gantavyaṃ tatsthalāddrutam ||
2.3.d:
शिवनिन्दाकरो वध्यः सर्वथा शिवकिङ्करैः ।
ब्राह्मणश्चेत्स वै त्याज्यो गन्तव्यं तत्स्थलाद्द्रुतम् ॥
2.3.m: A reviler of Śiva is to be slain by all means by Śiva's servants; / if he is a brāhmaṇa, he should be abandoned and one must quickly depart from that place.

2.3.s:
ayaṃ duṣṭaḥ punarnindāṃ kariṣyati śivasya hi |
brāhmaṇatvādavadhyaścettyājyo'dṛśyaśca sarvathā ||
2.3.d:
अयं दुष्टः पुनर्निन्दां करिष्यति शिवस्य हि ।
ब्राह्मणत्वादवध्यश्चेत्त्याज्योऽदृश्यश्च सर्वथा ॥
2.3.m: This wicked man will revile Śiva again; / because he is a brāhmaṇa, if he is not to be slain, he must be abandoned and completely hidden from sight.

2.3.s:
hitvaitatsthalamadyaiva yāsyāmo'nyatra mā ciram |
atha sambhāṣaṇaṃ na syādanenā'viduṣā punaḥ ||
2.3.d:
हित्वैतत्स्थलमद्यैव यास्यामोऽन्यत्र मा चिरम् ।
अथ सम्भाषणं न स्यादनेनाऽविदुषा पुनः ॥
