तस्माद्देया त्वया कन्या शङ्कराय महात्मने ॥
2.3.m: The sages said: / ‘Śiva is proclaimed the father of the universe; Śivā is considered the mother of the universe; / therefore your daughter must be given to the great-souled Śaṅkara.

2.3.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā himagire sārthakaṃ te bhavejjanuḥ |
jagadgurorgurustvaṃ hi bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.3.d:
एवं कृत्वा हिमगिरे सार्थकं ते भवेज्जनुः ।
जगद्गुरोर्गुरुस्त्वं हि भविष्यसि न संशयः ॥
2.3.m: Having done this, O snowy mountain, your birth will become meaningful; / for you will become the guru of the guru of the universe, there is no doubt.’

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
evaṃ vacanamākarṇya saptarṣīṇāṃ munīśvara |
praṇamya tānkarau baddhvā girirājo'bravīdidam ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवं वचनमाकर्ण्य सप्तर्षीणां मुनीश्वर ।
प्रणम्य तान्करौ बद्ध्वा गिरिराजोऽब्रवीदिदम् ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing this speech of the Seven Sages, O lord of sages, / the king of mountains bowed, folded his hands, and spoke this.

2.3.s:
himālaya uvāca |
saptarṣayo mahābhāgā bhavadbhiryadudīritam |
tatpramāṇīkṛtaṃ me hi puraiva giriśecchayā ||
2.3.d:
हिमालय उवाच ।
सप्तर्षयो महाभागा भवद्भिर्यदुदीरितम् ।
तत्प्रमाणीकृतं मे हि पुरैव गिरिशेच्छया ॥
2.3.m: Himālaya said: / ‘O Seven Sages of great fortune, what has been uttered by you / was indeed accepted as authority by me previously, by the will of Giriśa.

2.3.s:
idānīmeka āgatya vipro vaiṣṇavadharmavān |
śivamuddiśya suprītyā viparītaṃ vaco'bravīt ||
2.3.d:
इदानीमेक आगत्य विप्रो वैष्णवधर्मवान् ।
शिवमुद्दिश्य सुप्रीत्या विपरीतं वचोऽब्रवीत् ॥
2.3.m: Just now a brāhmaṇa arrived who follows the Vaiṣṇava way; / with great affection he spoke contradictory words concerning Śiva.

2.3.s:
tadārabhya śivāmātā jñānabhraṣṭā babhūva ha |
sutāvivāhaṃ rudreṇa yoginā tena necchati ||
2.3.d:
तदारभ्य शिवामाता ज्ञानभ्रष्टा बभूव ह ।
सुताविवाहं रुद्रेण योगिना तेन नेच्छति ॥
2.3.m: Starting from then, the mother of Śivā has lost her senses; / she does not wish for her daughter's marriage with that yogin Rudra.

2.3.s:
kopāgāramagātsā hi sutaptā malināmbarā |
kṛtvā mahāhaṭhaṃ viprā bodhyamānāpi nābudhat ||
ahaṃ ca jñānavibhraṣṭo jāto'haṃ satyamīryate |
dātuṃ sutāṃ maheśāya necchāmi bhikṣurūpiṇe ||
2.3.d:
कोपागारमगात्सा हि सुतप्ता मलिनाम्बरा ।
कृत्वा महाहठं विप्रा बोध्यमानापि नाबुधत् ॥
अहं च ज्ञानविभ्रष्टो जातोऽहं सत्यमीर्यते ।
दातुं सुतां महेशाय नेच्छामि भिक्षुरूपिणे ॥
2.3.m:
She went to the chamber of wrath, intensely distressed, wearing soiled clothes; / having made a stubborn refusal, O brāhmaṇas, she did not understand even though being reasoned with.

And I too have become bereft of proper knowledge; the truth is being told: / I do not wish to give my daughter to Maheśa who has the form of a beggar.’

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā śailarājastu śivamāyāvimohitaḥ |
tūṣṇīṃ babhūva tatrastho munīnāṃ madhyato mune ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा शैलराजस्तु शिवमायाविमोहितः ।
तूष्णीं बभूव तत्रस्थो मुनीनां मध्यतो मुने ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, the king of mountains, deluded by the māyā of Śiva, / fell silent as he stood there among the sages, O sage.

2.3.s:
sarve saptarṣayaste hi śivamāyāṃ praśasya vai |
preṣayāmāsuratha tāṃ menakāṃ pratyarundhatīm ||
2.3.d:
सर्वे सप्तर्षयस्ते हि शिवमायां प्रशस्य वै ।
प्रेषयामासुरथ तां मेनकां प्रत्यरुन्धतीम् ॥
2.3.m: All those Seven Sages, having praised the māyā of Śiva, / then dispatched Arundhatī to Menakā.

2.3.s:
atha patyuḥ samādāya nideśaṃ jñānadā hi sā |
jagāmārundhatī tūrṇaṃ yatra menā ca pārvatī ||
2.3.d:
अथ पत्युः समादाय निदेशं ज्ञानदा हि सा ।
जगामारुन्धती तूर्णं यत्र मेना च पार्वती ॥
2.3.m: Then, taking the command of her husband, she, the bestower of knowledge, / Arundhatī quickly went to where Menā and Pārvatī were.

2.3.s:
gatvā dadarśa menāṃ tāṃ śayānāṃ śokamūrcchitām |
uvāca madhuraṃ sādhvī sāvadhānā hitaṃ vacaḥ ||
2.3.d:
गत्वा ददर्श मेनां तां शयानां शोकमूर्च्छिताम् ।
उवाच मधुरं साध्वी सावधाना हितं वचः ॥
2.3.m: Having gone, she saw Menā lying down, fainting from grief; / the virtuous woman, attentive, spoke sweet and beneficial words.

2.3.s:
arundhatyuvāca |
uttiṣṭha menake sādhvi tvadgṛhe'hamarundhatī |
āgatā munayaścāpi saptāyātāḥ kṛpālavaḥ ||
2.3.d:
अरुन्धत्युवाच ।
उत्तिष्ठ मेनके साध्वि त्वद्गृहेऽहमरुन्धती ।
आगता मुनयश्चापि सप्तायाताः कृपालवः ॥
2.3.m: Arundhatī said: / Arise, virtuous Menakā! I, Arundhatī, have come to your house, / and also the seven compassionate sages have arrived.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
arundhatīsvaraṃ śrutvā śīghramutthāya menakā |
uvāca śirasā natvā tāṃ padmāmiva tejasā ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
अरुन्धतीस्वरं श्रुत्वा शीघ्रमुत्थाय मेनका ।
उवाच शिरसा नत्वा तां पद्मामिव तेजसा ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing Arundhatī’s voice, Menakā, rising quickly, / bowing her head, spoke to her who was like Lakṣmī in splendor.

2.3.s:
menovāca |
aho'dya kimidaṃ puṇyamasmākaṃ puṇyajanmanām |
vadhūrjagadvidheḥ patnī vasiṣṭhasyāgateha vai ||
2.3.d:
मेनोवाच ।
अहोऽद्य किमिदं पुण्यमस्माकं पुण्यजन्मनाम् ।
वधूर्जगद्विधेः पत्नी वसिष्ठस्यागतेह वै ॥
2.3.m: Menā said: / Ah, what is this merit today of ours who are born of merit, / that the daughter-in-law of the creator of the world, the wife of Vasiṣṭha, has indeed come here!

2.3.s:
kimarthamāgatā devi tanme brūhi viśeṣataḥ |
ahaṃ dāsīsamā te hi sasutā karuṇāṃ kuru ||
2.3.d:
किमर्थमागता देवि तन्मे ब्रूहि विशेषतः ।
अहं दासीसमा ते हि ससुता करुणां कुरु ॥
2.3.m: For what purpose have you come, O goddess? Tell me that in detail. / Indeed, along with my daughter I am like your maidservant; have compassion!

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā menakā sādhvī bodhayitvā ca tāṃ bahu |
tatrāgatā ca suprītyā yatra saptarṣayo'pi te ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा मेनका साध्वी बोधयित्वा च तां बहु ।
तत्रागता च सुप्रीत्या यत्र सप्तर्षयोऽपि ते ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, virtuous Menakā, having comforted her greatly, / went with great joy to where those seven sages also were.

2.3.s:
atha śaileśvaraṃ te ca bodhayāmāsurādarāt |
smṛtvā śivapadadvandvaṃ sarve vākyaviśāradāḥ ||
2.3.d:
अथ शैलेश्वरं ते च बोधयामासुरादरात् ।
स्मृत्वा शिवपदद्वन्द्वं सर्वे वाक्यविशारदाः ॥
2.3.m: Then, remembering the pair of Śiva’s feet, they, / all skilled in speech, respectfully instructed the lord of mountains.

2.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
śailendra śrūyatāṃ vākyamasmākaṃ śubhakāraṇam |
śivāya pārvatīṃ dehi saṃhartuḥ śvaśuro bhava ||
2.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
शैलेन्द्र श्रूयतां वाक्यमस्माकं शुभकारणम् ।
शिवाय पार्वतीं देहि संहर्तुः श्वशुरो भव ॥
2.3.m: The sages said: / O lord of mountains, listen to our word, which brings good fortune: / give Pārvatī to Śiva, and become the father-in-law of the destroyer!

2.3.s:
ayācitāraṃ sarveśaṃ prārthayāmāsa yatnataḥ |
tārakasya vināśāya brahmā sambandhakarmaṇi ||
2.3.d:
अयाचितारं सर्वेशं प्रार्थयामास यत्नतः ।
तारकस्य विनाशाय ब्रह्मा सम्बन्धकर्मणि ॥
2.3.m: For the destruction of Tāraka, Brahmā with effort / entreated the lord of all, who asks for nothing, in the matter of this alliance.

2.3.s:
notsuko dārasaṃyoge śaṅkaro yogināṃ varaḥ |
vidheḥ prārthanayā devastava kanyāṃ grahīṣyati ||
2.3.d:
नोत्सुको दारसंयोगे शङ्करो योगिनां वरः ।
विधेः प्रार्थनया देवस्तव कन्यां ग्रहीष्यति ॥
2.3.m: Śaṅkara, the best of yogins, is not eager for union with a wife; / at the entreaty of the creator, the god will accept your daughter.

2.3.s:
duhituste tapastaptaṃ pratijñānaṃ cakāra sā |
hetudvayena yogīndro vivāhaṃ ca kariṣyati ||
2.3.d:
दुहितुस्ते तपस्तप्तं प्रतिज्ञानं चकार सा ।
हेतुद्वयेन योगीन्द्रो विवाहं च करिष्यति ॥
2.3.m: Your daughter performed austerity, and he made a solemn promise; / by this twofold cause, the lord of yogins will celebrate the marriage.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ṛṣīṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya sa himālayaḥ |
uvāca kiñcidbhītastu paraṃ vinayapūrvakam ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
ऋषीणां वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य स हिमालयः ।
उवाच किञ्चिद्भीतस्तु परं विनयपूर्वकम् ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing the speech of the sages, that Himālaya smiled / and spoke with utmost humility, yet somewhat frightened.

2.3.s:
himālaya uvāca |
śivasya rājasāmagrīṃ na hi paśyāmi kāñcana |
kañcidāśrayamaiśvaryaṃ kaṃ vā svajanabāndhavam ||
2.3.d:
हिमालय उवाच ।
शिवस्य राजसामग्रीं न हि पश्यामि काञ्चन ।
कञ्चिदाश्रयमैश्वर्यं कं वा स्वजनबान्धवम् ॥
2.3.m: Himālaya said: / I do not see any royal paraphernalia of Śiva, / nor any shelter, sovereignty, or any kinsman and relative.

2.3.s:
necchāmyati vinirliptayogine svāṃ sutāmaham |
yūyaṃ vedavidhātuśca putrā vadata niścitam ||
2.3.d:
नेच्छाम्यति विनिर्लिप्तयोगिने स्वां सुतामहम् ।
यूयं वेदविधातुश्च पुत्रा वदत निश्चितम् ॥
2.3.m: I do not wish [to give] my daughter to a yogin who is utterly detached. / You are the sons of the creator of the Vedas; speak decisively!

2.3.s:
varāyānanurūpāya pitā kanyāṃ dadāti cet |
kāmānmohādbhayāllobhātsa naṣṭo narakaṃ vrajet ||
2.3.d:
वरायाननुरूपाय पिता कन्यां ददाति चेत् ।
कामान्मोहाद्भयाल्लोभात्स नष्टो नरकं व्रजेत् ॥
2.3.m: If a father gives his daughter to an unsuitable groom / out of passion, delusion, fear, or greed, he is ruined and goes to hell.

2.3.s:
na hi dāsyāmyahaṃ kanyāmicchayā śūlapāṇaye |
yadvidhānaṃ bhavedyogyamṛṣayastadvidhīyatām ||
2.3.d:
न हि दास्याम्यहं कन्यामिच्छया शूलपाणये ।
यद्विधानं भवेद्योग्यमृषयस्तद्विधीयताम् ॥
2.3.m: I will not willingly give my daughter to the trident-bearer. / Whatever proper arrangement may be made, O sages, let that be done.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya vacastasya himāgasya munīśvara |
pratyuvāca vasiṣṭhastaṃ teṣāṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य हिमागस्य मुनीश्वर ।
प्रत्युवाच वसिष्ठस्तं तेषां वाक्यविशारदः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of Himālaya, O lord of sages, / Vasiṣṭha, the most skilled in speech among them, replied to him.

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
śṛṇu śaileśa madvākyaṃ sarvathā te hitāvaham |
dharmāviruddhaṃ satyaṃ ca paratreha mudāvaham ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
शृणु शैलेश मद्वाक्यं सर्वथा ते हितावहम् ।
धर्माविरुद्धं सत्यं च परत्रेह मुदावहम् ॥
2.3.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Listen, O lord of mountains, to my speech, which brings you welfare in every way, / which does not contradict dharma, is true, and brings joy in this world and the next.

2.3.s:
vacanaṃ trividhaṃ śaila laukike vaidike'pi ca |
sarvaṃ jānāti śāstrajño nirmalajñānacakṣuṣā ||
2.3.d:
वचनं त्रिविधं शैल लौकिके वैदिकेऽपि च ।
सर्वं जानाति शास्त्रज्ञो निर्मलज्ञानचक्षुषा ॥
2.3.m: Speech is threefold, O mountain, both in ordinary life and in the Veda; / one who knows the scriptures knows all through the eye of pure knowledge.

2.3.s:
asatyamahitaṃ paścātsāmprataṃ śrutisundaram |
subuddhirvakti śatrurhi hitaṃ naiva kadācana ||
2.3.d:
असत्यमहितं पश्चात्साम्प्रतं श्रुतिसुन्दरम् ।
सुबुद्धिर्वक्ति शत्रुर्हि हितं नैव कदाचन ॥
2.3.m: That which is untruthful, harmful in the end, but pleasant to the ear in the present, / an enemy speaks with clever intent, never for one’s welfare.

2.3.s:
ādāvaprītijanakaṃ pariṇāme sukhāvaham |
dayālurdharmaśīlo hi bodhayatyeva bāndhavaḥ ||
2.3.d:
आदावप्रीतिजनकं परिणामे सुखावहम् ।
दयालुर्धर्मशीलो हि बोधयत्येव बान्धवः ॥
2.3.m: That which causes displeasure at first, but brings happiness in the outcome, / a compassionate, virtuous relative instructs indeed.

2.3.s:
śrutimātrātsudhātulyaṃ sarvakālasukhāvaham |
satyasāraṃ hitakaraṃ vacanaṃ śreṣṭhamīpsitam ||
2.3.d:
श्रुतिमात्रात्सुधातुल्यं सर्वकालसुखावहम् ।
सत्यसारं हितकरं वचनं श्रेष्ठमीप्सितम् ॥
2.3.m: That which is like nectar upon mere hearing, brings happiness at all times, / is the essence of truth, and produces welfare, is the best, desired speech.

2.3.s:
evaṃ ca trividhaṃ śaila nītiśāstroditaṃ vacaḥ |
kathyatāṃ triṣu madhye kiṃ bruve vākyaṃ tvadīpsitam ||
brāhmasampadvihīnaśca śaṅkarastridaśeśvaraḥ |
tattvajñānasamudreṣu sannimagnaikamānasaḥ | 35 ||
2.3.d:
एवं च त्रिविधं शैल नीतिशास्त्रोदितं वचः ।
कथ्यतां त्रिषु मध्ये किं ब्रुवे वाक्यं त्वदीप्सितम् ॥
ब्राह्मसम्पद्विहीनश्च शङ्करस्त्रिदशेश्वरः ।
तत्त्वज्ञानसमुद्रेषु सन्निमग्नैकमानसः । 35 ॥
2.3.m:
Thus speech is proclaimed to be of three kinds in the treatise on polity, O mountain; / say, among the three, which speech, desired by you, should I utter?

Śaṅkara, the lord of the gods, is devoid of material wealth, / for his single mind is immersed in the oceans of knowledge of truth.

2.3.s:
jñānānandasyeśvarasya brāhmavastuṣu kā spṛhā |
gṛhī dadāti svasutāṃ rājyasampattiśāline ||
2.3.d:
ज्ञानानन्दस्येश्वरस्य ब्राह्मवस्तुषु का स्पृहा ।
गृही ददाति स्वसुतां राज्यसम्पत्तिशालिने ॥
2.3.m: What longing can the Lord, whose nature is the bliss of knowledge, have for material things? / A householder gives his daughter to one endowed with the wealth of a kingdom.

2.3.s:
kanyakāṃ duḥkhine dattvā kanyāghātī bhavetpitā |
ko veda śaṅkaro duḥkhī kubero yasya kiṅkaraḥ ||
2.3.d:
कन्यकां दुःखिने दत्त्वा कन्याघाती भवेत्पिता ।
को वेद शङ्करो दुःखी कुबेरो यस्य किङ्करः ॥
2.3.m: Giving a girl to a wretched man, a father becomes the killer of his daughter. / But who knows Śaṅkara to be wretched, he whose servant is Kubera?

2.3.s:
bhrūbhaṅgalīlayā sṛṣṭiṃ sraṣṭuṃ hartuṃ kṣamo hi saḥ |
nirguṇaḥ paramātmā ca pareśaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ ||
2.3.d:
भ्रूभङ्गलीलया सृष्टिं स्रष्टुं हर्तुं क्षमो हि सः ।
निर्गुणः परमात्मा च परेशः प्रकृतेः परः ॥
2.3.m: By the play of his knitted brows, he is able to create and destroy creation; / he is without attributes, the supreme Self, the supreme Lord, beyond Prakṛti.

2.3.s:
yasya ca trividhā mūrtirvidhātuḥ sṛṣṭikarmaṇi |
sṛṣṭisthityantajananī brahmaviṣṇuharābhidhā ||
2.3.d:
यस्य च त्रिविधा मूर्तिर्विधातुः सृष्टिकर्मणि ।
सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तजननी ब्रह्मविष्णुहराभिधा ॥
2.3.m: The creator whose form is threefold in the work of creation, / bringing about creation, preservation, and dissolution, named Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Hara.

2.3.s:
brahmā ca brahmalokastho viṣṇuḥ kṣīrodavāsakṛt |
haraḥ kailāsanilayaḥ sarvāḥ śivavibhūtayaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मा च ब्रह्मलोकस्थो विष्णुः क्षीरोदवासकृत् ।
हरः कैलासनिलयः सर्वाः शिवविभूतयः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā resides in the world of Brahmā; Viṣṇu makes his abode in the Milk Ocean; / Hara has his dwelling on Kailāsa: all are manifestations of Śiva.

2.3.s:
dhatte ca trividhā mūrtīḥ prakṛtiḥ śivasambhavā |
aṃśena līlayā sṛṣṭau kalayā bahudhā api ||
2.3.d:
धत्ते च त्रिविधा मूर्तीः प्रकृतिः शिवसम्भवा ।
अंशेन लीलया सृष्टौ कलया बहुधा अपि ॥
2.3.m: And Prakṛti, born of Śiva, assumes threefold forms: / by a portion, in play, in creation, and also in many ways through her parts.

2.3.s:
mukhodbhavā svayaṃ vāṇī vāgadhiṣṭhātṛdevatā |
vakṣaḥsthalodbhavā lakṣmīḥ sarvasampatsvarūpiṇī ||
2.3.d:
मुखोद्भवा स्वयं वाणी वागधिष्ठातृदेवता ।
वक्षःस्थलोद्भवा लक्ष्मीः सर्वसम्पत्स्वरूपिणी ॥
2.3.m: Born from his mouth is Sarasvatī herself, the presiding deity of speech; / born from his chest is Lakṣmī, the embodiment of all prosperity.

2.3.s:
śivā tejassu devānāmāvirbhāvaṃ cakāra sā |
nihatya dānavānsarvāndevebhyaśca śriyaṃ dadau ||
2.3.d:
शिवा तेजस्सु देवानामाविर्भावं चकार सा ।
निहत्य दानवान्सर्वान्देवेभ्यश्च श्रियं ददौ ॥
2.3.m: Śivā made her appearance in the splendors of the gods; / having slain all the demons, she gave prosperity to the gods.

2.3.s:
prāpa kalpāntare janma jaṭhare dakṣayoṣitaḥ |
nāmnā satī haraṃ prāpa dakṣastasmai dadau ca tām ||
2.3.d:
प्राप कल्पान्तरे जन्म जठरे दक्षयोषितः ।
नाम्ना सती हरं प्राप दक्षस्तस्मै ददौ च ताम् ॥
2.3.m: In another kalpa she took birth in the womb of Dakṣa’s wife; / named Satī, she obtained Hara, and Dakṣa gave her to him.

2.3.s:
dehaṃ tatyāja yogena śrutvā sā bhartṛnindanam |
sādya tvattastu menāyāṃ jajñe jaṭharataśśivā ||
2.3.d:
देहं तत्याज योगेन श्रुत्वा सा भर्तृनिन्दनम् ।
साद्य त्वत्तस्तु मेनायां जज्ञे जठरतश्शिवा ॥
2.3.m: She abandoned her body through yoga upon hearing the censure of her husband. / She, Śivā, has now been born from you, from the womb of Menā.

2.3.s:
śivā śivasya patnīyaṃ śaila janmani janmani |
kalpe kalpe buddhirūpā jñānināṃ jananī parā ||
2.3.d:
शिवा शिवस्य पत्नीयं शैल जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
कल्पे कल्पे बुद्धिरूपा ज्ञानिनां जननी परा ॥
2.3.m: This Śivā is the wife of Śiva, O mountain, birth after birth, / in kalpa after kalpa, the embodiment of intellect, the supreme mother of the wise.

2.3.s:
jāyate sma sadā siddhā siddhidā siddhirūpiṇī |
satyā asthi citābhasma bhaktyā dhatte haraḥ svayam ||
2.3.d:
जायते स्म सदा सिद्धा सिद्धिदा सिद्धिरूपिणी ।
सत्या अस्थि चिताभस्म भक्त्या धत्ते हरः स्वयम् ॥
2.3.m: She was ever born perfected, the giver of perfection, embodying perfection. / Hara himself carries with devotion the bone and funeral ash of Satī.

2.3.s:
atastvaṃ svecchayā kanyāṃ dehi bhadrāṃ harāya ca |
athavā sā svayaṃ kāntasthāne yāsyatyadāsyasi ||
2.3.d:
अतस्त्वं स्वेच्छया कन्यां देहि भद्रां हराय च ।
अथवा सा स्वयं कान्तस्थाने यास्यत्यदास्यसि ॥
2.3.m: Therefore, of your own accord, give your auspicious daughter to Hara; / or else, if you do not give her, she will go on her own to her beloved's abode.

2.3.s:
kṛtvā pratijñāṃ deveśo dṛṣṭvā kleśamasaṅkhyakam |
duhituste tapaḥsthānamājagāma dvijātmakaḥ ||
2.3.d:
कृत्वा प्रतिज्ञां देवेशो दृष्ट्वा क्लेशमसङ्ख्यकम् ।
दुहितुस्ते तपःस्थानमाजगाम द्विजात्मकः ॥
2.3.m: Having made a promise and having seen the countless afflictions / of your daughter, the lord of gods came to the place of austerity in the form of a twice-born.

2.3.s:
tāmāśvāsya varaṃ dattvā jagāma nijamandiram |
tatprārthanāvaśācchambhuryayāce tvāṃ śivāṃ gire ||
2.3.d:
तामाश्वास्य वरं दत्त्वा जगाम निजमन्दिरम् ।
तत्प्रार्थनावशाच्छम्भुर्ययाचे त्वां शिवां गिरे ॥
2.3.m: Comforting her and giving a boon, he went to his own abode; / at her entreaty, O mountain, Sambhu asked you for Śivā.

2.3.s:
aṅgīkṛtaṃ yuvābhyāṃ tacchivabhaktiratātmanā |
viparītamatirjātā vada kasmādgirīśvara ||
2.3.d:
अङ्गीकृतं युवाभ्यां तच्छिवभक्तिरतात्मना ।
विपरीतमतिर्जाता वद कस्माद्गिरीश्वर ॥
2.3.m: That was accepted by both of you whose minds were devoted to devotion to Śiva; / tell me, why has your mind become contrary, O lord of mountains?

2.3.s:
tadgatvā prabhuṇā devaprārthitena tvadantikam |
prasthāpitā vayaṃ śīghraṃ ṛṣayaḥ sāpyarundhatī ||
2.3.d:
तद्गत्वा प्रभुणा देवप्रार्थितेन त्वदन्तिकम् ।
प्रस्थापिता वयं शीघ्रं ऋषयः साप्यरुन्धती ॥
2.3.m: Therefore, having been entreated by the gods, we, the sages / and also Arundhatī, have been sent quickly to your presence by the Lord.

2.3.s:
śikṣayāmo vayaṃ tvā hi dehi rudrāya pārvatīm |
evaṅkṛte mahānando bhaviṣyati gire tava ||
2.3.d:
शिक्षयामो वयं त्वा हि देहि रुद्राय पार्वतीम् ।
एवङ्कृते महानन्दो भविष्यति गिरे तव ॥
2.3.m: Indeed we instruct you: give Pārvatī to Rudra; / when this is done, O mountain, there will be great joy for you.

2.3.s:
śivāṃ śivāya śailendra svecchayā cenna dāsyasi |
bhavitā tadvivāho'tra bhavitavyabalena hi ||
2.3.d:
शिवां शिवाय शैलेन्द्र स्वेच्छया चेन्न दास्यसि ।
भविता तद्विवाहोऽत्र भवितव्यबलेन हि ॥
2.3.m: If you will not give Śivā to Śiva of your own accord, O lord of mountains, / their marriage will surely take place here by the power of destiny.

2.3.s:
varaṃ dadau śivāyai sa tapantyai tāta śaṅkaraḥ |
na hīśvarapratijñātaṃ viparītāya kalpate ||
2.3.d:
वरं ददौ शिवायै स तपन्त्यै तात शङ्करः ।
न हीश्वरप्रतिज्ञातं विपरीताय कल्पते ॥
2.3.m: Dear father, that Śaṅkara gave a boon to Śivā who was practicing austerity; / indeed, the solemn promise of the Lord cannot turn out otherwise.

2.3.s:
aho pratijñā durlaṅghyā sādhūnāmīśavartinām |
sarveṣāṃ jagatāṃ madhye kimīśasya punargire ||
2.3.d:
अहो प्रतिज्ञा दुर्लङ्घ्या साधूनामीशवर्तिनाम् ।
सर्वेषां जगतां मध्ये किमीशस्य पुनर्गिरे ॥
2.3.m: Ah, a promise of virtuous men abiding in the Lord cannot be transgressed / in all the worlds; how much less that of the Lord himself, O mountain?

2.3.s:
eko mahendraḥ śailānāṃ pakṣāṃściccheda līlayā |
pārvatī līlayā meroḥ śṛṅgabhaṅgaṃ cakāra ca ||
2.3.d:
एको महेन्द्रः शैलानां पक्षांश्चिच्छेद लीलया ।
पार्वती लीलया मेरोः शृङ्गभङ्गं चकार च ॥
2.3.m: The singular Mahendra severed the wings of the mountains in play, / and Pārvatī broke the peak of Meru in play.

2.3.s:
ekārthe nahi śaileśa naśyāḥ sarvā hi sampadaḥ |
ekaṃ tyajetkulasyārthe śrutireṣā sanātanī ||
2.3.d:
एकार्थे नहि शैलेश नश्याः सर्वा हि सम्पदः ।
एकं त्यजेत्कुलस्यार्थे श्रुतिरेषा सनातनी ॥
2.3.m: All one's fortunes, O lord of mountains, must not be lost for the sake of one thing; / 'One should abandon one [person] for the sake of the family'—this is the eternal Vedic teaching.

2.3.s:
dattvā viprāya svasutāmanaraṇyo nṛpeśvaraḥ |
brāhmaṇādbhayamāpanno rarakṣa nijasampadam ||
2.3.d:
दत्त्वा विप्राय स्वसुतामनरण्यो नृपेश्वरः ।
ब्राह्मणाद्भयमापन्नो ररक्ष निजसम्पदम् ॥
2.3.m: Having given his daughter to a brāhmaṇa, the king of kings Anaraṇya, / terrified of the brāhmaṇa, preserved his own fortune.

2.3.s:
tamāśu bodhayāmāsurnītiśāstravido janāḥ |
brahmaśāpādvibhītañca guravo jñātisattamāḥ ||
2.3.d:
तमाशु बोधयामासुर्नीतिशास्त्रविदो जनाः ।
ब्रह्मशापाद्विभीतञ्च गुरवो ज्ञातिसत्तमाः ॥
2.3.m: People learned in the texts of statecraft, elders, and the best of his kinsmen / quickly advised him when he was terrified of a brāhmaṇa's curse.

2.3.s:
śailarāja tvamapyevaṃ sutāṃ dattvā śivāya ca |
rakṣa sarvānbandhuvargānvaśaṃ kuru surānapi ||
2.3.d:
शैलराज त्वमप्येवं सुतां दत्त्वा शिवाय च ।
रक्ष सर्वान्बन्धुवर्गान्वशं कुरु सुरानपि ॥
2.3.m: O king of mountains, you too, by giving your daughter to Śiva in this way, / protect all your kinsfolk and bring even the gods under your sway!”

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya vasiṣṭhasya vacanaṃ sa prahasya ca |
papraccha nṛpavārtāñca hṛdayena vidūyatā ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वसिष्ठस्य वचनं स प्रहस्य च ।
पप्रच्छ नृपवार्ताञ्च हृदयेन विदूयता ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard these words of Vasiṣṭha, he smiled, / and with an aching heart inquired about the story of that king.

2.3.s:
himālaya uvāca |
kasya vaṃśodbhavo brahman anaraṇyo nṛpaśca saḥ |
sutāṃ dattvā sa ca kathaṃ rarakṣākhilasampadaḥ ||
2.3.d:
हिमालय उवाच ।
कस्य वंशोद्भवो ब्रह्मन् अनरण्यो नृपश्च सः ।
सुतां दत्त्वा स च कथं ररक्षाखिलसम्पदः ॥
2.3.m: Himālaya said: / “In whose lineage was that king Anaraṇya born, O brāhmaṇa? / And how did he preserve all his fortunes by giving away his daughter?”

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
iti śrutvā vasiṣṭhastu śailavākyaṃ prasannadhīḥ |
provāca giraye tasmai nṛpavārttāṃ sukhāvahām ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इति श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठस्तु शैलवाक्यं प्रसन्नधीः ।
प्रोवाच गिरये तस्मै नृपवार्त्तां सुखावहाम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
Brahmā said: / Hearing this, Vasiṣṭha, pleased in mind at the mountain's words, / recounted to that mountain the delightful story of the king.

Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, entitled 'Consoling the Mountain', in the third section, the Pārvatīkhaṇḍa, of the second book, the Rudrasaṃhitā, of the glorious Śivamahāpurāṇa.

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
manorvaṃśodbhavo rājā so'naraṇyo nṛpeśvaraḥ |
indrasāvarṇisaṃjñasya caturdaśamitasya hi ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
मनोर्वंशोद्भवो राजा सोऽनरण्यो नृपेश्वरः ।
इन्द्रसावर्णिसंज्ञस्य चतुर्दशमितस्य हि ॥
2.3.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / “Born in the lineage of Manu, that lord of kings was King Anaraṇya, / in the line of the fourteenth [Manu] named Indrasāvarṇi.

2.3.s:
anaraṇyo nṛpaśreṣṭhaḥ saptadvīpamahīpatiḥ |
śambhubhakto viśeṣeṇa maṅgalāraṇyajo balī ||
2.3.d:
अनरण्यो नृपश्रेष्ठः सप्तद्वीपमहीपतिः ।
शम्भुभक्तो विशेषेण मङ्गलारण्यजो बली ॥
2.3.m: Anaraṇya was the best of kings, lord of the earth with its seven continents, / an ardent devotee of Śambhu, born in the auspicious forest, and mighty.

2.3.s:
bhṛguṃ purodhasaṃ kṛtvā śataṃ yajñāṃścakāra saḥ |
na svīcakāra śakratvaṃ dīyamānaṃ surairapi ||
2.3.d:
भृगुं पुरोधसं कृत्वा शतं यज्ञांश्चकार सः ।
न स्वीचकार शक्रत्वं दीयमानं सुरैरपि ॥
2.3.m: Appointing Bhṛgu as his family priest, he performed a hundred sacrifices; / he did not accept the position of Indra even when offered by the gods.

2.3.s:
babhūvuḥ śataputrāśca rājñastasya himālaya |
kanyaikā sundarī nāmnā padmā padmālayā samā ||
2.3.d:
बभूवुः शतपुत्राश्च राज्ञस्तस्य हिमालय ।
कन्यैका सुन्दरी नाम्ना पद्मा पद्मालया समा ॥
2.3.m: That king, O Himālaya, had a hundred sons / and one beautiful daughter named Padmā, who was like Lakṣmī herself.

2.3.s:
yaḥ snehaḥ putraśatake kanyāyāñca tato'dhikaḥ |
nṛpasya tasya tasyāṃ hi babhūva nagasattama ||
2.3.d:
यः स्नेहः पुत्रशतके कन्यायाञ्च ततोऽधिकः ।
नृपस्य तस्य तस्यां हि बभूव नगसत्तम ॥
2.3.m: Whatever affection that king had for his hundred sons, O best of mountains, / he had even greater affection for that daughter.

2.3.s:
prāṇādhikā priyatamā mahiṣyaḥ sarvayoṣitaḥ |
nṛpasya patnyaḥ pañcāsan sarvāḥ saubhāgyasaṃyutāḥ ||
2.3.d:
प्राणाधिका प्रियतमा महिष्यः सर्वयोषितः ।
नृपस्य पत्न्यः पञ्चासन् सर्वाः सौभाग्यसंयुताः ॥
2.3.m: His chief queens were dearer than his own life; all the women / of the king were fifty wives, all endowed with good fortune.

2.3.s:
sā kanyā yauvanasthā ca babhūva svapiturgṛhe |
patraṃ prasthāpayāmāsa suvarānayanāya saḥ ||
2.3.d:
सा कन्या यौवनस्था च बभूव स्वपितुर्गृहे ।
पत्रं प्रस्थापयामास सुवरानयनाय सः ॥
2.3.m: That maiden reached youth in her father’s house, / and he sent out a letter to bring a suitable groom.

2.3.s:
ekadā pippalādarṣirgantuṃ svāśramamutsukaḥ |
tapaḥsthāne nirjane ca gandharvaṃ sa dadarśa ha ||
2.3.d:
एकदा पिप्पलादर्षिर्गन्तुं स्वाश्रममुत्सुकः ।
तपःस्थाने निर्जने च गन्धर्वं स ददर्श ह ॥
2.3.m: Once, the sage Pippalāda, eager to go to his hermitage, / saw a Gandharva in a secluded place of austerity,

2.3.s:
strīyutaṃ magnacittaṃ ca śṛṅgāre rasasāgare |
viharantaṃ mahāpremṇā kāmaśāstraviśāradam ||
2.3.d:
स्त्रीयुतं मग्नचित्तं च शृङ्गारे रससागरे ।
विहरन्तं महाप्रेम्णा कामशास्त्रविशारदम् ॥
2.3.m: accompanied by a woman, his mind immersed in love, an ocean of passion, / sporting with great affection, expert in the treatise on love.

2.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ muniśārdūlaḥ sakāmaḥ sambabhūva saḥ |
tapaḥsvadattacittaścācintayaddārasaṅgraham ||
2.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं मुनिशार्दूलः सकामः सम्बभूव सः ।
तपःस्वदत्तचित्तश्चाचिन्तयद्दारसङ्ग्रहम् ॥
2.3.m: Seeing him, that tiger among sages was overcome by desire; / turning his mind away from austerities, he thought of taking a wife.

2.3.s:
evaṃvṛttasya tasyaiva pippalādasya sanmuneḥ |
kiyatkālo gatastatra kāmonmathitacetasaḥ ||
2.3.d:
एवंवृत्तस्य तस्यैव पिप्पलादस्य सन्मुनेः ।
कियत्कालो गतस्तत्र कामोन्मथितचेतसः ॥
2.3.m: Some time passed for that good sage Pippalāda who behaved thus, / his mind churned by desire.

2.3.s:
ekadā puṣpabhadrāyāṃ snātuṃ gacchanmunīśvaraḥ |
dadarśa padmāṃ yuvatīṃ padmāmiva manoramām ||
2.3.d:
एकदा पुष्पभद्रायां स्नातुं गच्छन्मुनीश्वरः ।
ददर्श पद्मां युवतीं पद्मामिव मनोरमाम् ॥
2.3.m: Once, as the lord of sages was going to bathe in the Puṣpabhadrā, / he saw the maiden Padmā, charming like Lakṣmī.

2.3.s:
keyaṃ kanyeti papraccha samīpasthāñjanānmuniḥ |
janā nivedayāñcakrurnatvā śāpaniyantritāḥ ||
2.3.d:
केयं कन्येति पप्रच्छ समीपस्थाञ्जनान्मुनिः ।
जना निवेदयाञ्चक्रुर्नत्वा शापनियन्त्रिताः ॥
2.3.m: The sage asked the people standing nearby, 'Who is this maiden?' / Restrained by fear of his curse, the people bowed and reported:

2.3.s:
janā ūcuḥ |
anaraṇyasuteyaṃ vai padmā nāma ramāparā |
varārohā prārthyamānā nṛpaśreṣṭhairguṇālayā ||
2.3.d:
जना ऊचुः ।
अनरण्यसुतेयं वै पद्मा नाम रमापरा ।
वरारोहा प्रार्थ्यमाना नृपश्रेष्ठैर्गुणालया ॥
2.3.m: The people said: / 'This is King Anaraṇya’s daughter named Padmā, another Ramā, / possessed of shapely hips, an abode of virtues, sought in marriage by the best of kings.'

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
tacchrutvā sa munirvākyaṃ janānāṃ tathyavādinām |
cukṣobhātīva manasi tallipsurabhavacca saḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा स मुनिर्वाक्यं जनानां तथ्यवादिनाम् ।
चुक्षोभातीव मनसि तल्लिप्सुरभवच्च सः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing those truthful words of the people, that sage / was greatly agitated in mind and longed to obtain her.

2.3.s:
muniḥ snātvābhīṣṭadevaṃ sampūjya vidhivacchivam |
jagāma kāmī bhikṣārthamanaraṇyasabhāṃ gire ||
2.3.d:
मुनिः स्नात्वाभीष्टदेवं सम्पूज्य विधिवच्छिवम् ।
जगाम कामी भिक्षार्थमनरण्यसभां गिरे ॥
2.3.m: The sage bathed, worshipped his chosen deity Śiva according to rule, / and, filled with lust, went to Anaraṇya's court to beg for alms, O mountain.

2.3.s:
rājā śīghraṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇanāma bhayākulaḥ |
madhuparkādikaṃ dattvā pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ ||
2.3.d:
राजा शीघ्रं मुनिं दृष्ट्वा प्रणनाम भयाकुलः ।
मधुपर्कादिकं दत्त्वा पूजयामास भक्तितः ॥
2.3.m: Seeing the sage, the king quickly bowed, trembling with fear; / offering the honey-mixture and other respects, he worshipped him with devotion.

2.3.s:
kāmātsarvaṃ gṛhītvā ca yayāce kanyakāṃ muniḥ |
maunī babhūva nṛpatiḥ kiñcinnirvaktumakṣamaḥ ||
2.3.d:
कामात्सर्वं गृहीत्वा च ययाचे कन्यकां मुनिः ।
मौनी बभूव नृपतिः किञ्चिन्निर्वक्तुमक्षमः ॥
2.3.m: Having accepted everything, the sage, through desire, asked for the maiden; / the king fell silent, unable to utter anything.

2.3.s:
muniryayāce kanyāṃ sa tāṃ dehīti nṛpeśvara |
anyathā bhasmasātsarvaṃ kariṣyāmi kṣaṇena ca ||
2.3.d:
मुनिर्ययाचे कन्यां स तां देहीति नृपेश्वर ।
अन्यथा भस्मसात्सर्वं करिष्यामि क्षणेन च ॥
2.3.m: The sage demanded the maiden, saying, 'Give her, O lord of kings! / Otherwise, I will reduce everything to ashes in an instant!'

2.3.s:
sarve babhūvurācchannā gaṇāstattejasā mune |
rudoda rājā sagaṇo dṛṣṭvā vipraṃ jarāturam ||
2.3.d:
सर्वे बभूवुराच्छन्ना गणास्तत्तेजसा मुने ।
रुदोद राजा सगणो दृष्ट्वा विप्रं जरातुरम् ॥
2.3.m: All the attendants were overwhelmed by that sage's splendor; / the king wept along with his attendants upon seeing the brāhmaṇa afflicted with old age.

2.3.s:
mahiṣyo rurudussarvā itikartavyatākṣamāḥ |
mūrcchāmāpa mahārājñī kanyāmātā śucākulā ||
2.3.d:
महिष्यो रुरुदुस्सर्वा इतिकर्तव्यताक्षमाः ।
मूर्च्छामाप महाराज्ञी कन्यामाता शुचाकुला ॥
2.3.m: All the queens wept, at a loss as to what should be done; / overcome with grief, the chief queen, the mother of the girl, fainted.

2.3.s:
babhūvustanayāḥ sarve śokākulitamānasāḥ |
sarvaṃ śokākulaṃ jātaṃ nṛpasambandhi śailapa ||
2.3.d:
बभूवुस्तनयाः सर्वे शोकाकुलितमानसाः ।
सर्वं शोकाकुलं जातं नृपसम्बन्धि शैलप ॥
2.3.m: All the sons became distressed in mind with sorrow; / everything connected with the king became distraught with grief, O lord of mountains.

2.3.s:
etasminnantare prājño dvijo gururanuttamaḥ |
purohitaśca matimān āgato nṛpasannidhim ||
2.3.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे प्राज्ञो द्विजो गुरुरनुत्तमः ।
पुरोहितश्च मतिमान् आगतो नृपसन्निधिम् ॥
2.3.m: At that moment, the wise brāhmaṇa, the peerless teacher, / and the intelligent family priest came into the king's presence.

2.3.s:
rājā praṇamya sampūjya rudoda ca tayoḥ puraḥ |
sarvaṃ nivedayāñcakre papracchocitamāśu tat ||
2.3.d:
राजा प्रणम्य सम्पूज्य रुदोद च तयोः पुरः ।
सर्वं निवेदयाञ्चक्रे पप्रच्छोचितमाशु तत् ॥
2.3.m: Bowing and honoring them, the king wept before the two; / he informed them of everything and quickly asked what was appropriate.

2.3.s:
atha rājño gururvipraḥ paṇḍitaśca purohitaḥ |
api dvau śāstranītijñau bodhayāmāsaturnṛpam ||
2.3.d:
अथ राज्ञो गुरुर्विप्रः पण्डितश्च पुरोहितः ।
अपि द्वौ शास्त्रनीतिज्ञौ बोधयामासतुर्नृपम् ॥
2.3.m: Then the king's guru, a learned brāhmaṇa, and the wise family priest, / both knowledgeable in the scriptures and statecraft, counseled the king,

2.3.s:
śokākulāṃśca mahiṣīrnṛpabālāṃśca kanyakām |
uttamāṃ nītimādṛtya sarveṣāṃ hitakāriṇīm ||
2.3.d:
शोकाकुलांश्च महिषीर्नृपबालांश्च कन्यकाम् ।
उत्तमां नीतिमादृत्य सर्वेषां हितकारिणीम् ॥
2.3.m: as well as the queens distraught with grief, the king's young sons, and the maiden, / holding fast to the highest principle of policy that brings welfare to all.

2.3.s:
gurupurodhasāvūcatuḥ
śṛṇu rājanmahāprājña vaco nau saddhitāvaham |
mā śucaḥ saparīvāraḥ śāstre kuru matiṃ satīm ||
2.3.d:
गुरुपुरोधसावूचतुः
शृणु राजन्महाप्राज्ञ वचो नौ सद्धितावहम् ।
मा शुचः सपरीवारः शास्त्रे कुरु मतिं सतीम् ॥
2.3.m: The guru and the family priest said: / 'Listen, O great-minded king, to our words that bring true welfare; / do not grieve along with your family; fix your noble mind upon the scripture.

2.3.s:
adya vābdadinānte vā dātavyā kanyakā nṛpa |
pātrāya viprāyānyasmai kasmaicidvā viśeṣataḥ ||
2.3.d:
अद्य वाब्ददिनान्ते वा दातव्या कन्यका नृप ।
पात्राय विप्रायान्यस्मै कस्मैचिद्वा विशेषतः ॥
2.3.m: Today or at the end of a year, the maiden must be given away, O king, / especially to a worthy recipient, a brāhmaṇa, or someone else.

2.3.s:
satpātraṃ brāhmaṇādanyaṃ na paśyāvo jagattraye |
sutāṃ dattvā ca munaye rakṣa svāṃ sarvasampadam ||
2.3.d:
सत्पात्रं ब्राह्मणादन्यं न पश्यावो जगत्त्रये ।
सुतां दत्त्वा च मुनये रक्ष स्वां सर्वसम्पदम् ॥
2.3.m: In the three worlds we see no worthy recipient other than a brāhmaṇa; / give your daughter to the sage and preserve all your fortune.

2.3.s:
rājannekanimittena sarvasampadvinaśyati |
sarvaṃ rakṣati taṃ tyaktvā vinā taṃ śaraṇāgatam ||
2.3.d:
राजन्नेकनिमित्तेन सर्वसम्पद्विनश्यति ।
सर्वं रक्षति तं त्यक्त्वा विना तं शरणागतम् ॥
2.3.m: O king, all fortune is ruined for the sake of one thing; / by abandoning that one, he preserves everything—except one who has taken refuge.'

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
rājā prājñavacaḥ śrutvā vilapya ca muhurmuhuḥ |
kanyāṃ sālaṅkṛtāṃ kṛtvā munīndrāya dadau kila ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
राजा प्राज्ञवचः श्रुत्वा विलप्य च मुहुर्मुहुः ।
कन्यां सालङ्कृतां कृत्वा मुनीन्द्राय ददौ किल ॥
2.3.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Hearing the words of the wise men and lamenting again and again, / the king adorned the maiden and gave her to the chief of sages.

2.3.s:
kāntāṃ gṛhītvā sa munirvivāhya vidhivadgire |
padmāṃ padmopamāṃ tāṃ vai muditaḥsvālayaṃ yayau ||
2.3.d:
कान्तां गृहीत्वा स मुनिर्विवाह्य विधिवद्गिरे ।
पद्मां पद्मोपमां तां वै मुदितःस्वालयं ययौ ॥
2.3.m: Taking his beloved, marrying that Padmā who was like Lakṣmī / according to rule, O mountain, the delighted sage went to his abode.

2.3.s:
rājā sarvānparityajya dattvā vṛddhāya cātmajām |
glāniṃ citte samādhāya jagāma tapase vanam ||
2.3.d:
राजा सर्वान्परित्यज्य दत्त्वा वृद्धाय चात्मजाम् ।
ग्लानिं चित्ते समाधाय जगाम तपसे वनम् ॥
2.3.m: Having given his daughter to an old man, the king abandoned everyone, / and, harboring sorrow in his heart, went to the forest to perform austerities.

2.3.s:
tadbhāryāpi vanaṃ yāte prāṇanāthe tadā gire |
bhartuśca duhituḥ śokātprāṇāṃstatyāja sundarī ||
2.3.d:
तद्भार्यापि वनं याते प्राणनाथे तदा गिरे ।
भर्तुश्च दुहितुः शोकात्प्राणांस्तत्याज सुन्दरी ॥
2.3.m: When the lord of her life had departed for the forest, O mountain, / that beautiful wife also surrendered her life out of grief for her husband and daughter.

2.3.s:
pūjyāḥ putrāśca bhṛtyāśca mūrcchāmāpurnṛpaṃ vinā |
śuśucuḥ śvāsasaṃyuktā jñātvā sarve'pare janāḥ ||
2.3.d:
पूज्याः पुत्राश्च भृत्याश्च मूर्च्छामापुर्नृपं विना ।
शुशुचुः श्वाससंयुक्ता ज्ञात्वा सर्वेऽपरे जनाः ॥
2.3.m: The venerable sons and servants fainted without the king; / when other people learned of it, they grieved, sighing deeply.

2.3.s:
anaraṇyo vanaṃ gatvā tapastaptvāti śaṅkaram |
samārādhya yayau bhaktyā śivalokamanāmayam ||
2.3.d:
अनरण्यो वनं गत्वा तपस्तप्त्वाति शङ्करम् ।
समाराध्य ययौ भक्त्या शिवलोकमनामयम् ॥
2.3.m: Having gone to the forest, Anaraṇya practiced intense austerity, / worshipped Śaṅkara, and through devotion went to the sorrowless realm of Śiva.

2.3.s:
nṛpasya kīrtimānnāmnā jyeṣṭhaputro'tha dhārmikaḥ |
putravatpālayāmāsa prajā rājyaṃ cakāra ha ||
2.3.d:
नृपस्य कीर्तिमान्नाम्ना ज्येष्ठपुत्रोऽथ धार्मिकः ।
पुत्रवत्पालयामास प्रजा राज्यं चकार ह ॥
2.3.m: Then the righteous eldest son of the king, named Kīrtimant, / ruled the kingdom, protecting the subjects like his own sons.”

2.3.s:
śailarāja tvamapyevaṃ sutāṃ dattvā śivāya ca |
rakṣa sarvakulaṃ sarvānvaśānkuru surānapi ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
शैलराज त्वमप्येवं सुतां दत्त्वा शिवाय च ।
रक्ष सर्वकुलं सर्वान्वशान्कुरु सुरानपि ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
O king of mountains, you too, by giving your daughter to Śiva, / preserve your entire clan and bring all the gods under your sway.”

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, entitled “Description of the Story of Anaraṇya,” in the third section, the Pārvatīkhaṇḍa, of the second book, the Rudrasaṃhitā, of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.3.s:
nārada uvāca |
anaraṇyasya caritaṃ sutādānasamanvitam |
śrutvā girivarastāta kiṃ cakāra ca tadvada ||
2.3.d:
नारद उवाच ।
अनरण्यस्य चरितं सुतादानसमन्वितम् ।
श्रुत्वा गिरिवरस्तात किं चकार च तद्वद ॥
2.3.m: Nārada said: / Having heard the story of Anaraṇya along with the giving of his daughter, / O dear father, what did the best of mountains do? Tell me that.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
anaraṇyasya caritaṃ kanyādānasamanvitam |
śrutvā papraccha śaileśo vasiṣṭhaṃ sāñjaliḥ punaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
अनरण्यस्य चरितं कन्यादानसमन्वितम् ।
श्रुत्वा पप्रच्छ शैलेशो वसिष्ठं साञ्जलिः पुनः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard the story of Anaraṇya along with the giving of his maiden, / the lord of mountains, with folded hands, questioned Vasiṣṭha again.

2.3.s:
śaileśa uvāca |
vasiṣṭha muniśārdūla brahmaputra kṛpānidhe |
anaraṇyacaritrante kathitaṃ paramādbhutam ||
2.3.d:
शैलेश उवाच ।
वसिष्ठ मुनिशार्दूल ब्रह्मपुत्र कृपानिधे ।
अनरण्यचरित्रन्ते कथितं परमाद्भुतम् ॥
2.3.m: The lord of mountains said: / “O Vasiṣṭha, tiger among sages, son of Brahmā, treasure of compassion! / The story of Anaraṇya narrated by you is exceedingly wonderful.

2.3.s:
anaraṇyasutā yasmāt pippalādaṃ muniṃ patim |
samprāpya kimakārṣītsā taccaritraṃ mudāvaham ||
2.3.d:
अनरण्यसुता यस्मात् पिप्पलादं मुनिं पतिम् ।
सम्प्राप्य किमकार्षीत्सा तच्चरित्रं मुदावहम् ॥
2.3.m: Since the daughter of Anaraṇya, having obtained the sage Pippalāda as her husband, / what did she do? [Tell me] her delightful story.”

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
pippalādo munivaro vayasā jarjaro'dhikaḥ |
gatvā nijāśramaṃ nāryānaraṇyasutayā tayā ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
पिप्पलादो मुनिवरो वयसा जर्जरोऽधिकः ।
गत्वा निजाश्रमं नार्यानरण्यसुतया तया ॥
2.3.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Pippalāda, the best of sages, severely worn out by old age, / went to his own hermitage with that woman, the daughter of Anaraṇya.

2.3.s:
uvāsa tatra suprītyā tapasvī nātilampaṭaḥ |
tatrāraṇye girivare sa nityaṃ nijadharmakṛt ||
2.3.d:
उवास तत्र सुप्रीत्या तपस्वी नातिलम्पटः ।
तत्रारण्ये गिरिवरे स नित्यं निजधर्मकृत् ॥
2.3.m: There he dwelt with great delight, an ascetic free from excessive lust, / performing his own duties daily in that forest on the excellent mountain.

2.3.s:
athānaraṇyakanyā sā siṣeve bhaktito munim |
karmaṇā manasā vācā lakṣmīrnārāyaṇaṃ yathā ||
2.3.d:
अथानरण्यकन्या सा सिषेवे भक्तितो मुनिम् ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा लक्ष्मीर्नारायणं यथा ॥
2.3.m: Then that daughter of Anaraṇya served the sage with devotion, / in deed, mind, and speech, like Lakṣmī serving Nārāyaṇa.

2.3.s:
ekadā svarṇadīṃ snātuṃ gacchantīṃ susmitāṃ ca tām |
dadarśa pathi dharmaśca māyayā nṛparūpadhṛk ||
2.3.d:
एकदा स्वर्णदीं स्नातुं गच्छन्तीं सुस्मितां च ताम् ।
ददर्श पथि धर्मश्च मायया नृपरूपधृक् ॥
2.3.m: Once, as she, smiling gently, was going to the celestial river to bathe, / Dharma saw her on the road, having assumed the form of a king by his illusory power.

2.3.s:
cāruratnarathasthaśca nānālaṅkārabhūṣitaḥ |
navīnayauvanaśśrīmānkāmadevasamaprabhaḥ ||
2.3.d:
चारुरत्नरथस्थश्च नानालङ्कारभूषितः ।
नवीनयौवनश्श्रीमान्कामदेवसमप्रभः ॥
2.3.m: Seated in a beautiful jewel-chariot, adorned with various ornaments, / endowed with fresh youth, resplendent, equal in radiance to Kāmadeva,

2.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sundarīṃ padmāmuvāca sa vṛṣo vibhuḥ |
vijñātuṃ bhāvamantaḥsthaṃ tasyāśca muniyoṣitaḥ ||
2.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा तां सुन्दरीं पद्मामुवाच स वृषो विभुः ।
विज्ञातुं भावमन्तःस्थं तस्याश्च मुनियोषितः ॥
2.3.m: having seen that beautiful woman, Padmā, the mighty Dharma spoke, / in order to know the inner state of that sage’s wife.

2.3.s:
dharma uvāca |
ayi sundari lakṣmīrvai rājayogye manohare |
atīva yauvanasthe ca kāmini sthirayauvane ||
2.3.d:
धर्म उवाच ।
अयि सुन्दरि लक्ष्मीर्वै राजयोग्ये मनोहरे ।
अतीव यौवनस्थे च कामिनि स्थिरयौवने ॥
2.3.m: Dharma said: / “O beautiful woman, a veritable Lakṣmī fit for a king, captivating, / exceedingly youthful, desirable, of enduring youth!

2.3.s:
jarāturasya vṛddhasya pippalādasya vai muneḥ |
satyaṃ vadāmi tanvaṅgi samīpe naiva rājase ||
2.3.d:
जरातुरस्य वृद्धस्य पिप्पलादस्य वै मुनेः ।
सत्यं वदामि तन्वङ्गि समीपे नैव राजसे ॥
2.3.m: Beside the sage Pippalāda, afflicted by old age and senile, / truly I say, O slender-limbed woman, you do not shine at all.

2.3.s:
vipraṃ tapassu nirataṃ nirghṛṇaṃ maraṇonmukham |
tyaktvā māṃ paśya rājendraṃ ratiśūraṃ smarāturam ||
2.3.d:
विप्रं तपस्सु निरतं निर्घृणं मरणोन्मुखम् ।
त्यक्त्वा मां पश्य राजेन्द्रं रतिशूरं स्मरातुरम् ॥
2.3.m: Leaving the brāhmaṇa intent on austerities, pitiless and facing death, / look upon me, a supreme king, valiant in love and stricken by desire.

2.3.s:
prāpnoti sundarī puṇyātsaundaryaṃ pūrvajanmanaḥ |
saphalaṃ tadbhavetsarvaṃ rasikāliṅganena ca ||
2.3.d:
प्राप्नोति सुन्दरी पुण्यात्सौन्दर्यं पूर्वजन्मनः ।
सफलं तद्भवेत्सर्वं रसिकालिङ्गनेन च ॥
2.3.m: A beautiful woman attains beauty from the merit of a previous birth; / all that becomes fruitful through the embrace of a connoisseur of pleasure.

2.3.s:
sahasrasundarīkāntaṃ kāmaśāstraviśāradam |
kiṅkaraṃ kuru māṃ kānte samparityajya taṃ patim ||
2.3.d:
सहस्रसुन्दरीकान्तं कामशास्त्रविशारदम् ।
किङ्करं कुरु मां कान्ते सम्परित्यज्य तं पतिम् ॥
2.3.m: Beloved of a thousand beautiful women, skilled in the science of love, / make me your servant, O lovely one, completely abandoning that husband.

2.3.s:
nirjane kānane ramye śaile śaile nadītaṭe |
viharasva mayā sārdhaṃ janmedaṃ saphalaṃ kuru ||
2.3.d:
निर्जने कानने रम्ये शैले शैले नदीतटे ।
विहरस्व मया सार्धं जन्मेदं सफलं कुरु ॥
2.3.m: In a secluded, delightful forest, on mountain after mountain, and on riverbanks, / sport with me and make this birth fruitful.”

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
ityevamuktavantaṃ sā svarathādavaruhya ca |
grahītumutsukaṃ haste tamuvāca pativratā ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्तवन्तं सा स्वरथादवरुह्य च ।
ग्रहीतुमुत्सुकं हस्ते तमुवाच पतिव्रता ॥
2.3.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / To him who had spoken thus, having descended from his chariot / and eager to take her by the hand, the devoted wife said:

2.3.s:
padmovāca |
gaccha dūraṃ gaccha dūraṃ pāpiṣṭhastvaṃ narādhipa |
māṃ cetpaśyasi kāmena sadyo naṣṭo bhaviṣyasi ||
2.3.d:
पद्मोवाच ।
गच्छ दूरं गच्छ दूरं पापिष्ठस्त्वं नराधिप ।
मां चेत्पश्यसि कामेन सद्यो नष्टो भविष्यसि ॥
2.3.m: Padmā said: / “Go far away, go far away, you most sinful lord of men! / If you look upon me with desire, you will instantly be destroyed.

2.3.s:
pippalādaṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ tapasā pūtavigraham |
tyaktvā kathaṃ bhajeyaṃ tvāṃ strījitaṃ ratilampaṭam ||
2.3.d:
पिप्पलादं मुनिश्रेष्ठं तपसा पूतविग्रहम् ।
त्यक्त्वा कथं भजेयं त्वां स्त्रीजितं रतिलम्पटम् ॥
2.3.m: Abandoning Pippalāda, the best of sages, whose body is purified by austerity, / how could I resort to you, enslaved by women and greedy for sexual pleasure?

2.3.s:
strījitasparśamātreṇa sarvaṃ puṇyaṃ praṇaśyati |
strījitaḥ parapāpī ca taddarśanamaghāvaham ||
2.3.d:
स्त्रीजितस्पर्शमात्रेण सर्वं पुण्यं प्रणश्यति ।
स्त्रीजितः परपापी च तद्दर्शनमघावहम् ॥
2.3.m: By the mere touch of one who is enslaved by women, all merit is destroyed; / one conquered by women is an utter sinner, and the sight of him brings sin.

2.3.s:
satkriyo hyaśucirnityaṃ sa pumān yaḥ striyā jitaḥ |
nindanti pitaro devā mānavāḥ sakalāśca tam ||
2.3.d:
सत्क्रियो ह्यशुचिर्नित्यं स पुमान् यः स्त्रिया जितः ।
निन्दन्ति पितरो देवा मानवाः सकलाश्च तम् ॥
2.3.m: A man who is enslaved by a woman is constantly impure, even if performing virtuous rites; / the ancestors, gods, and all human beings revile him.

2.3.s:
tasya kiṃ jñāna sutapojapahomaprapūjanaiḥ |
vidyayā dānataḥ kiṃ vā strībhiryasya mano hṛtam ||
2.3.d:
तस्य किं ज्ञान सुतपोजपहोमप्रपूजनैः ।
विद्यया दानतः किं वा स्त्रीभिर्यस्य मनो हृतम् ॥
2.3.m: What use are knowledge, severe austerity, recitation, fire-offerings, or worship / to him whose mind is stolen by women, or what use is learning or giving?

2.3.s:
mātaraṃ māṃ striyo bhāvaṃ kṛtvā yena bravīṣi ha |
bhaviṣyati kṣayastena kālena mama śāpataḥ ||
2.3.d:
मातरं मां स्त्रियो भावं कृत्वा येन ब्रवीषि ह ।
भविष्यति क्षयस्तेन कालेन मम शापतः ॥
2.3.m: Because you speak to me, a mother, looking upon me as a sexual partner, / there shall be your decline in the course of time through my curse.”

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
śrutvā dharmaḥ satīśāpaṃ nṛpamūrtiṃ vihāya ca |
dhṛtvā svamūrtiṃ deveśaḥ kampamāna uvāca saḥ ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
श्रुत्वा धर्मः सतीशापं नृपमूर्तिं विहाय च ।
धृत्वा स्वमूर्तिं देवेशः कम्पमान उवाच सः ॥
2.3.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Hearing the curse of the chaste woman and casting off the form of a king, / the lord of gods, assuming his own form, said trembling:

2.3.s:
dharma uvāca |
mātarjānīhi māṃ dharmaṃ jñānināṃ ca gurorgurum |
parastrīmātṛbuddhiṃ ca kurvantaṃ satataṃ sati ||
2.3.d:
धर्म उवाच ।
मातर्जानीहि मां धर्मं ज्ञानिनां च गुरोर्गुरुम् ।
परस्त्रीमातृबुद्धिं च कुर्वन्तं सततं सति ॥
2.3.m: Dharma said: / “O mother, know me as Dharma, the teacher of teachers among the wise, / who ever regards another’s wife as a mother, O chaste woman!

2.3.s:
ahaṃ tavāntaraṃ jñātumāgatastava sannidhim |
tavāhañca mano jāne tathāpi vidhinoditaḥ ||
2.3.d:
अहं तवान्तरं ज्ञातुमागतस्तव सन्निधिम् ।
तवाहञ्च मनो जाने तथापि विधिनोदितः ॥
2.3.m: I came to your presence to test your inner heart; / I already know your mind, yet I was impelled by fate.

2.3.s:
kṛtaṃ me damanaṃ sādhvi na viruddhaṃ yathocitam |
śāstiḥ samutpathasthānāmīśvareṇa vinirmitā ||
2.3.d:
कृतं मे दमनं साध्वि न विरुद्धं यथोचितम् ।
शास्तिः समुत्पथस्थानामीश्वरेण विनिर्मिता ॥
2.3.m: You have subdued me, O virtuous lady, and it is not improper; it is fitting. / Punishment for those who stray onto the wrong path has been established by the Lord.

2.3.s:
svayaṃ pradātā sarvebhyaḥ sukhaduḥkhavarānkṣamaḥ |
sampadaṃ vipadaṃ yo hi namastasmai śivāya hi ||
2.3.d:
स्वयं प्रदाता सर्वेभ्यः सुखदुःखवरान्क्षमः ।
सम्पदं विपदं यो हि नमस्तस्मै शिवाय हि ॥
2.3.m: He who himself dispenses to all the boons of happiness and sorrow, / prosperity and misfortune, homage indeed to that Śiva!

2.3.s:
śatruṃ mitraṃ saṃvidhātuṃ prītiñca kalahaṃ kṣamaḥ |
sraṣṭuṃ naṣṭuṃ ca yassṛṣṭiṃ namastasmai śivāya hi ||
2.3.d:
शत्रुं मित्रं संविधातुं प्रीतिञ्च कलहं क्षमः ।
स्रष्टुं नष्टुं च यस्सृष्टिं नमस्तस्मै शिवाय हि ॥
2.3.m: He who is able to make an enemy, a friend, love, and quarrel, / to create the creation and to destroy it, homage indeed to that Śiva!

2.3.s:
yena śuklīkṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ jale śaityaṃ kṛtaṃ purā |
dāhīkṛto hutāśaśca namastasmai śivāya hi ||
2.3.d:
येन शुक्लीकृतं क्षीरं जले शैत्यं कृतं पुरा ।
दाहीकृतो हुताशश्च नमस्तस्मै शिवाय हि ॥
2.3.m: By whom milk was made white, coldness was placed in water of old, / and the consumer of offerings made burning, homage indeed to that Śiva!

2.3.s:
prakṛtirnirmitā yena tattvāni mahadāditaḥ |
brahmaviṣṇumaheśādyā namastasmai śivāya hi ||
2.3.d:
प्रकृतिर्निर्मिता येन तत्त्वानि महदादितः ।
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाद्या नमस्तस्मै शिवाय हि ॥
2.3.m: By whom Prakṛti was created, and the principles beginning with the Mahat, / as well as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the rest, homage indeed to that Śiva!”

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā puratastasyāstasthau dharmo jagadguruḥ |
kiñcinnovāca cakitastatpātivratyatoṣitaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा पुरतस्तस्यास्तस्थौ धर्मो जगद्गुरुः ।
किञ्चिन्नोवाच चकितस्तत्पातिव्रत्यतोषितः ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, Dharma, the spiritual teacher of the world, stood before her; / he said nothing further, astounded, pleased with her marital fidelity.

2.3.s:
padmāpi nṛpakanyā sā pippalādapriyā tadā |
sādhvī taṃ dharmamājñāya vismitovāca parvata ||
2.3.d:
पद्मापि नृपकन्या सा पिप्पलादप्रिया तदा ।
साध्वी तं धर्ममाज्ञाय विस्मितोवाच पर्वत ॥
2.3.m: Padmā too, that king’s daughter and beloved wife of Pippalāda, / realizing that he was Dharma, O mountain, was astonished and spoke, the virtuous woman:

2.3.s:
padmovāca |
tvameva dharma sarveṣāṃ sākṣī nikhilakarmaṇām |
kathaṃ mano me vijñātuṃ viḍambayasi māṃ vibho ||
2.3.d:
पद्मोवाच ।
त्वमेव धर्म सर्वेषां साक्षी निखिलकर्मणाम् ।
कथं मनो मे विज्ञातुं विडम्बयसि मां विभो ॥
2.3.m: Padmā said: / “You alone, O Dharma, are the witness to all the deeds of everyone; / why do you mock me, O omnipresent one, in order to test my mind?

2.3.s:
yattatsarvaṃ kṛtaṃ brahman nāparādho babhūva me |
tvaṃ ca śapto mayājñānātstrīsvabhāvād vṛthā vṛṣa ||
2.3.d:
यत्तत्सर्वं कृतं ब्रह्मन् नापराधो बभूव मे ।
त्वं च शप्तो मयाज्ञानात्स्त्रीस्वभावाद् वृथा वृष ॥
2.3.m: Whatever was done, O brāhmaṇa, was not my fault; / and you were cursed by me in vain through ignorance, from the nature of a woman, O bull [of Dharma].

2.3.s:
kā vyavasthā bhavettasya cintayāmīti sāmpratam |
citte sphuratu sā buddhiryayā śaṃ saṃllabhāmi vai ||
2.3.d:
का व्यवस्था भवेत्तस्य चिन्तयामीति साम्प्रतम् ।
चित्ते स्फुरतु सा बुद्धिर्यया शं संल्लभामि वै ॥
2.3.m: What will be the remedy for it? I am pondering this right now. / May that thought flash in my mind by which I may obtain peace.

2.3.s:
ākāśo'sau diśaḥsarvā yadi naśyantu vāyavaḥ |
tathāpi sādhvīśāpastu na naśyati kadācana ||
2.3.d:
आकाशोऽसौ दिशःसर्वा यदि नश्यन्तु वायवः ।
तथापि साध्वीशापस्तु न नश्यति कदाचन ॥
2.3.m: Even if this sky, all the directions, and the winds should perish, / the curse of a chaste woman nevertheless never fails.

2.3.s:
satye pūrṇaścatuṣpādaḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ yathā śaśī |
virājase devarāja sarvakālaṃ divāniśam ||
2.3.d:
सत्ये पूर्णश्चतुष्पादः पौर्णमास्यां यथा शशी ।
विराजसे देवराज सर्वकालं दिवानिशम् ॥
2.3.m: Complete with four feet in the Kṛta age, like the moon on the full-moon day, / you shine, O king of gods, at all times, day and night.

2.3.s:
tvaṃ ca naṣṭo bhavasi cetsṛṣṭināśo bhavettadā |
itikartavyatāmūḍhā vṛthāpi ca vadāmyaham ||
2.3.d:
त्वं च नष्टो भवसि चेत्सृष्टिनाशो भवेत्तदा ।
इतिकर्तव्यतामूढा वृथापि च वदाम्यहम् ॥
2.3.m: And if you were to be destroyed, the destruction of creation would follow; / bewildered as to what should be done, I speak even in vain.

2.3.s:
pādakṣayaśca bhavitā tretāyāṃ ca surottama |
pādo'pare dvāpare ca tṛtīyo'pi kalau vibho ||
2.3.d:
पादक्षयश्च भविता त्रेतायां च सुरोत्तम ।
पादोऽपरे द्वापरे च तृतीयोऽपि कलौ विभो ॥
2.3.m: There shall be the loss of one foot in the Tretā age, O best of gods, / a second foot in the Dvāpara, and a third in the Kali age, O omnipresent one.

2.3.s:
kaliśeṣe'khilāśchinnā bhaviṣyanti tavāṅghrayaḥ |
punaḥsatye samāyāte paripūrṇo bhaviṣyasi ||
2.3.d:
कलिशेषेऽखिलाश्छिन्ना भविष्यन्ति तवाङ्घ्रयः ।
पुनःसत्ये समायाते परिपूर्णो भविष्यसि ॥
2.3.m: At the end of the Kali age, all your feet will be severed; / when the Kṛta age arrives again, you shall become complete once more.”

2.3.s:
satye sarvavyāpakastvaṃ tadanyeṣu ca kutracit |
yugavyavasthayā sa tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi yathā tathā ||
2.3.d:
सत्ये सर्वव्यापकस्त्वं तदन्येषु च कुत्रचित् ।
युगव्यवस्थया स त्वं भविष्यसि यथा तथा ॥
2.3.m: In the Kṛtayuga you shall be all-pervading, and in the others only in certain places; / in accordance with the arrangement of the yugas, you will be so, exactly as described.

2.3.s:
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ satyaṃ mamāstu sukhadaṃ tava |
yāmyahaṃ patisevāyai gaccha tvaṃ svagṛhaṃ vibho ||
2.3.d:
इत्येवं वचनं सत्यं ममास्तु सुखदं तव ।
याम्यहं पतिसेवायै गच्छ त्वं स्वगृहं विभो ॥
2.3.m: May this true word of mine bring you happiness! / I am going to serve my husband; go to your own home, O lord!"

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityākarṇya vacastasyāḥ santuṣṭo'bhūd vṛṣaḥ sa vai |
tadevaṃvādinīṃ sādhvīmuvāca vidhinandana ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्याः सन्तुष्टोऽभूद् वृषः स वै ।
तदेवंवादिनीं साध्वीमुवाच विधिनन्दन ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard her speech, that bull was pleased indeed; / and to the virtuous woman who spoke thus, O son of Brahmā, he said:

2.3.s:
dharma uvāca |
dhanyāsi patibhaktāsi svasti te'stu pativrate |
varaṃ gṛhāṇa tvatsvāmī tvatparitrāṇakāraṇāt ||
2.3.d:
धर्म उवाच ।
धन्यासि पतिभक्तासि स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु पतिव्रते ।
वरं गृहाण त्वत्स्वामी त्वत्परित्राणकारणात् ॥
2.3.m: Dharma said: / "Blessed are you, devoted to your husband; well-being be to you, O faithful wife! / Accept a boon for your husband, on account of your deliverance of him.

2.3.s:
yuvā bhavatu te bhartā ratiśūraśca dhārmikaḥ |
rūpavān guṇavānvāgmī santatasthirayauvanaḥ ||
2.3.d:
युवा भवतु ते भर्ता रतिशूरश्च धार्मिकः ।
रूपवान् गुणवान्वाग्मी सन्ततस्थिरयौवनः ॥
2.3.m: May your husband become a youth, valiant in love, righteous, / handsome, virtuous, eloquent, and possessed of perpetual, enduring youth.

2.3.s:
cirañjīvī sa bhavatu mārkaṇḍeyātparaśśubhe |
kuberāddhanavāṃścaiva śakrādaiśvaryavānapi ||
2.3.d:
चिरञ्जीवी स भवतु मार्कण्डेयात्परश्शुभे ।
कुबेराद्धनवांश्चैव शक्रादैश्वर्यवानपि ॥
2.3.m: May he be long-lived, surpassing Mārkaṇḍeya, O auspicious lady, / wealthier than Kubera, and even more possessed of sovereign power than Indra;

2.3.s:
śivabhakto harisamassiddhastu kapilātparaḥ |
buddhyā bṛhaspatisamaḥ samatvena vidheḥ samaḥ ||
2.3.d:
शिवभक्तो हरिसमस्सिद्धस्तु कपिलात्परः ।
बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतिसमः समत्वेन विधेः समः ॥
2.3.m: a devotee of Śiva equal to Hari, an adept surpassing Kapila, / equal to Bṛhaspati in intellect, and equal to Brahmā in impartiality.

2.3.s:
svāmisaubhāgyasaṃyuktā bhava tvaṃ jīvanāvadhi |
tathā ca subhage devi tvaṃ bhava sthirayauvanā ||
2.3.d:
स्वामिसौभाग्यसंयुक्ता भव त्वं जीवनावधि ।
तथा च सुभगे देवि त्वं भव स्थिरयौवना ॥
2.3.m: May you be endowed with your husband's good fortune as long as life lasts, / and likewise, O fortunate goddess, may you possess enduring youth.

2.3.s:
mātā tvaṃ daśaputrāṇāṃ guṇināṃ cirajīvinām |
svabharturadhikānāṃ ca bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.3.d:
माता त्वं दशपुत्राणां गुणिनां चिरजीविनाम् ।
स्वभर्तुरधिकानां च भविष्यसि न संशयः ॥
2.3.m: You shall be the mother of ten sons who are virtuous, long-lived, / and superior to their own father; there is no doubt.

2.3.s:
gṛhā bhavantu te sādhvi sarvasampatsamanvitāḥ |
prakāśavantaḥ satataṃ kuberabhavanādhikāḥ ||
2.3.d:
गृहा भवन्तु ते साध्वि सर्वसम्पत्समन्विताः ।
प्रकाशवन्तः सततं कुबेरभवनाधिकाः ॥
2.3.m: May your houses, O virtuous lady, be endowed with all kinds of prosperity, / constantly luminous, surpassing the mansion of Kubera."

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
ityevamuktvā santasthau dharmaḥ sa girisattama |
sā taṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇamya svagṛhaṃ yayau ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्त्वा सन्तस्थौ धर्मः स गिरिसत्तम ।
सा तं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य प्रणम्य स्वगृहं ययौ ॥
2.3.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having spoken thus, Dharma stood still, O best of mountains; / she circumambulated him, bowed down, and went to her own home.

2.3.s:
dharmastathāśiṣo dattvā jagāma nijamandiram |
praśaśaṃsa ca tāṃ prītyā padmāṃ saṃsadi saṃsadi ||
2.3.d:
धर्मस्तथाशिषो दत्त्वा जगाम निजमन्दिरम् ।
प्रशशंस च तां प्रीत्या पद्मां संसदि संसदि ॥
2.3.m: Dharma, having thus bestowed blessings, went to his own abode, / and with affection praised Padmā in assembly after assembly.

2.3.s:
sā reme svāminā sārdhaṃ yūnā rahasi santatam |
paścādbabhūvuḥ satputrāstadbharturadhikā guṇaiḥ ||
2.3.d:
सा रेमे स्वामिना सार्धं यूना रहसि सन्ततम् ।
पश्चाद्बभूवुः सत्पुत्रास्तद्भर्तुरधिका गुणैः ॥
2.3.m: She constantly took pleasure with her youthful husband in secret; / later, virtuous sons were born, surpassing their father in virtues.

2.3.s:
babhūva sakalā sampaddampatyoḥ sukhavardhinī |
sarvānandavṛddhikarī paratreha ca śarmaṇe ||
2.3.d:
बभूव सकला सम्पद्दम्पत्योः सुखवर्धिनी ।
सर्वानन्दवृद्धिकरी परत्रेह च शर्मणे ॥
2.3.m: Every kind of prosperity arose, increasing the happiness of the couple, / furthering every joy for their well-being here and in the hereafter.

2.3.s:
śailendra kathitaṃ sarvamitihāsaṃ purātanam |
dampatyośca tayoḥ prītyā śrutaṃ te paramādarāt ||
2.3.d:
शैलेन्द्र कथितं सर्वमितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
दम्पत्योश्च तयोः प्रीत्या श्रुतं ते परमादरात् ॥
2.3.m: O lord of mountains, the entire ancient story has been narrated; / and with affection for that couple, it has been heard by you with supreme respect.

2.3.s:
buddhvā tattvaṃ sutāṃ dehi pārvatīmīśvarāya ca |
kuruṣaṃ tyaja śailendra menayā svastriyā saha ||
2.3.d:
बुद्ध्वा तत्त्वं सुतां देहि पार्वतीमीश्वराय च ।
कुरुषं त्यज शैलेन्द्र मेनया स्वस्त्रिया सह ॥
2.3.m: Having understood the truth, give your daughter Pārvatī to the Lord; / abandon your anger, O lord of mountains, along with your wife Menā.

2.3.s:
saptāhe samatīte tu durlabhe'tiśubhe kṣaṇe |
lagnādhipe ca lagnasthe candre svatnayānvite ||
2.3.d:
सप्ताहे समतीते तु दुर्लभेऽतिशुभे क्षणे ।
लग्नाधिपे च लग्नस्थे चन्द्रे स्वत्नयान्विते ॥
2.3.m: When a week has elapsed, at an exceedingly auspicious, rare moment, / when the lord of the ascendant is in the ascendant, and the Moon is in conjunction with its own son;

2.3.s:
mudite rohiṇīyukte viśuddhe candratārake |
mārgamāse candravāre sarvadoṣavivarjite ||
2.3.d:
मुदिते रोहिणीयुक्ते विशुद्धे चन्द्रतारके ।
मार्गमासे चन्द्रवारे सर्वदोषविवर्जिते ॥
2.3.m: when it is cheerful, joined with Rohiṇī, and the lunar asterism is pure; / in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on a Monday, free from all astrological flaws;

2.3.s:
sarvasadgrahasaṃsṛṣṭe'sadgrahadṛṣṭivarjite |
sadapatyaprade jīve patisaubhāgyadāyini ||
2.3.d:
सर्वसद्ग्रहसंसृष्टेऽसद्ग्रहदृष्टिवर्जिते ।
सदपत्यप्रदे जीवे पतिसौभाग्यदायिनि ॥
2.3.m: joined by all auspicious planets and devoid of the aspect of inauspicious planets; / while Jupiter is granting virtuous offspring and bestowing good fortune from the husband;

2.3.s:
jagadambāṃ jagatpitre mūlaprakṛtimīśvarīm |
kanyāṃ pradāya girijāṃ kṛtī tvaṃ bhava parvata ||
2.3.d:
जगदम्बां जगत्पित्रे मूलप्रकृतिमीश्वरीम् ।
कन्यां प्रदाय गिरिजां कृती त्वं भव पर्वत ॥
2.3.m: giving the Mother of the Universe, primordial matter, the sovereign Goddess, / your maiden daughter born of the mountain, to the Father of the Universe, be accomplished, O mountain!"

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā muniśārdūlo vasiṣṭho jñānisattamaḥ |
virarāma śivaṃ smṛtvā nānālīlākaraṃ prabhum ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा मुनिशार्दूलो वसिष्ठो ज्ञानिसत्तमः ।
विरराम शिवं स्मृत्वा नानालीलाकरं प्रभुम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, that tiger among sages, Vasiṣṭha, best among the wise, / remembered Śiva, the Lord who performs diverse divine sports, and paused.

Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter, entitled "Description of the Account of Padmā and Pippalāda," in the Pārvatīkhaṇḍa of the second section, the Rudrasaṃhitā, in the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutvā sagaṇo'pi himālayaḥ |
vismito bhāryayā śailānuvāca sa girīśvaraḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
वसिष्ठस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सगणोऽपि हिमालयः ।
विस्मितो भार्यया शैलानुवाच स गिरीश्वरः ॥

2.3.s:
himālaya uvāca |
he mero girirāṭ sahya gandhamādana mandara |
maināka vindhya śailendrāḥ sarve śṛṇuta madvacaḥ ||
2.3.d:
हिमालय उवाच ।
हे मेरो गिरिराट् सह्य गन्धमादन मन्दर ।
मैनाक विन्ध्य शैलेन्द्राः सर्वे शृणुत मद्वचः ॥

2.3.s:
vasiṣṭho hi vadatyevaṃ kiṃ me kāryaṃ vicāryate |
yathā tathā ca śaṃsadhvaṃ nirṇīya manasākhilam ||
2.3.d:
वसिष्ठो हि वदत्येवं किं मे कार्यं विचार्यते ।
यथा तथा च शंसध्वं निर्णीय मनसाखिलम् ॥

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
tacchutvā vacanaṃ tasya sumerupramukhāśca te |
procurhimālayaṃ prītyā sunirṇīya mahīdharāḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तच्छुत्वा वचनं तस्य सुमेरुप्रमुखाश्च ते ।
प्रोचुर्हिमालयं प्रीत्या सुनिर्णीय महीधराः ॥

2.3.s:
śailā ūcuḥ |
adhunā kiṃ vimarśena kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ tathaiva hi |
utpanneyaṃ mahābhāga devakāryārthameva hi ||
2.3.d:
शैला ऊचुः ।
अधुना किं विमर्शेन कृतं कार्यं तथैव हि ।
उत्पन्नेयं महाभाग देवकार्यार्थमेव हि ॥

2.3.s:
pradātavyā śivāyeti śivasyārthe'vatāriṇī |
anayārādhito rudro rudreṇa yadi bhāṣitā ||
2.3.d:
प्रदातव्या शिवायेति शिवस्यार्थेऽवतारिणी ।
अनयाराधितो रुद्रो रुद्रेण यदि भाषिता ॥

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
etacchrutvā vacasteṣāṃ mervādīnāṃ himācalaḥ |
suprasannataro'bhūd vai jahāsa girijā hṛdi ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां मेर्वादीनां हिमाचलः ।
सुप्रसन्नतरोऽभूद् वै जहास गिरिजा हृदि ॥

2.3.s:
arundhatī ca tāṃ menāṃ bodhayāmāsa kāraṇāt |
nānāvākyasamūhenetihāsairvividhairapi ||
2.3.d:
अरुन्धती च तां मेनां बोधयामास कारणात् ।
नानावाक्यसमूहेनेतिहासैर्विविधैरपि ॥

2.3.s:
atha sā menakā śailapatnī buddhvā prasannadhīḥ |
munīnarundhatīṃ śailaṃ bhojayitvā bubhoja ca ||
2.3.d:
अथ सा मेनका शैलपत्नी बुद्ध्वा प्रसन्नधीः ।
मुनीनरुन्धतीं शैलं भोजयित्वा बुभोज च ॥

2.3.s:
atha śailavaro jñānī susaṃsevya munīṃśca tān |
uvāca sāñjaliḥ prītyā prasannātmā gatabhramaḥ ||
2.3.d:
अथ शैलवरो ज्ञानी सुसंसेव्य मुनींश्च तान् ।
उवाच साञ्जलिः प्रीत्या प्रसन्नात्मा गतभ्रमः ॥

2.3.s:
himācala uvāca |
saptarṣayo mahābhāgā vacaḥ śṛṇuta māmakam |
vismayo me gataḥ sarvaḥ śivayoścaritaṃ śrutam ||
2.3.d:
हिमाचल उवाच ।
सप्तर्षयो महाभागा वचः शृणुत मामकम् ।
विस्मयो मे गतः सर्वः शिवयोश्चरितं श्रुतम् ॥

2.3.s:
madīyaṃ ca śarīraṃ vai patnī menā sutā sutāḥ |
ṛddhiḥ siddhiśca cānyadvai śivasyaiva na cānyathā ||
2.3.d:
मदीयं च शरीरं वै पत्नी मेना सुता सुताः ।
ऋद्धिः सिद्धिश्च चान्यद्वै शिवस्यैव न चान्यथा ॥

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā sa tadā putrīṃ dṛṣṭvā tatsādaraṃ ca tām |
bhūṣayitvā tadaṅgāni ṛṣyutsaṅge nyaveśayat ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा स तदा पुत्रीं दृष्ट्वा तत्सादरं च ताम् ।
भूषयित्वा तदङ्गानि ऋष्युत्सङ्गे न्यवेशयत् ॥

2.3.s:
uvāca ca punaḥ prītyā śailarāja ṛṣīṃstadā |
ayaṃ bhāgo mayā tasmai dātavya iti niścitam ||
2.3.d:
उवाच च पुनः प्रीत्या शैलराज ऋषींस्तदा ।
अयं भागो मया तस्मै दातव्य इति निश्चितम् ॥

2.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
śaṅkaro bhikṣukaste'tha svayaṃ dātā bhavān gire |
bhaikṣyañca pārvatī devī kimataḥ paramuttamam ||
2.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
शङ्करो भिक्षुकस्तेऽथ स्वयं दाता भवान् गिरे ।
भैक्ष्यञ्च पार्वती देवी किमतः परमुत्तमम् ॥

2.3.s:
himavan śikharāṇānte yaddhetoḥ sadṛśī gatiḥ |
dhanyastvaṃ sarvaśailānāmadhipaḥ sarvato varaḥ ||
2.3.d:
हिमवन् शिखराणान्ते यद्धेतोः सदृशी गतिः ।
धन्यस्त्वं सर्वशैलानामधिपः सर्वतो वरः ॥

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
evamuktvā tu kanyāyai munayo vimalāśayāḥ |
āśiṣaṃ dattavantaste śivāya sukhadā bhava ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
एवमुक्त्वा तु कन्यायै मुनयो विमलाशयाः ।
आशिषं दत्तवन्तस्ते शिवाय सुखदा भव ॥

2.3.s:
spṛṣṭvā kareṇa tāṃ tatra kalyāṇaṃ te bhaviṣyati |
śuklapakṣe yathā candro vardhantāṃ tvadguṇāstathā ||
2.3.d:
स्पृष्ट्वा करेण तां तत्र कल्याणं ते भविष्यति ।
शुक्लपक्षे यथा चन्द्रो वर्धन्तां त्वद्गुणास्तथा ॥

2.3.s:
ityuktvā munayaḥ sarve dattvā te giraye mudā |
puṣpāṇi phalayuktāni pratyayaṃ cakrire tadā ||
2.3.d:
इत्युक्त्वा मुनयः सर्वे दत्त्वा ते गिरये मुदा ।
पुष्पाणि फलयुक्तानि प्रत्ययं चक्रिरे तदा ॥

2.3.s:
arundhatī tadā tatra menāṃ sā sumukhī mudā |
guṇaiśca lobhayāmāsa śivasya paramā satī ||
2.3.d:
अरुन्धती तदा तत्र मेनां सा सुमुखी मुदा ।
गुणैश्च लोभयामास शिवस्य परमा सती ॥

2.3.s:
haridrākuṅkumaiḥ śailaśmaśrūṇi pratyamārjayat |
laukikācāramādhāya maṅgalāyanamuttamam ||
2.3.d:
हरिद्राकुङ्कुमैः शैलश्मश्रूणि प्रत्यमार्जयत् ।
लौकिकाचारमाधाय मङ्गलायनमुत्तमम् ॥

2.3.s:
tataśca te caturthe'hni sandhārya lagnamuttamam |
parasparaṃ ca santuṣya sañjagmuḥ śivasannidhim ||
2.3.d:
ततश्च ते चतुर्थेऽह्नि सन्धार्य लग्नमुत्तमम् ।
परस्परं च सन्तुष्य सञ्जग्मुः शिवसन्निधिम् ॥

2.3.s:
tatra gatvā śivaṃ natvā stutvā vividhasūktibhiḥ |
ūcuḥ sarve vasiṣṭhādyā munayaḥ parameśvaram ||
2.3.d:
तत्र गत्वा शिवं नत्वा स्तुत्वा विविधसूक्तिभिः ।
ऊचुः सर्वे वसिष्ठाद्या मुनयः परमेश्वरम् ॥

2.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
devadeva mahādeva parameśa mahāprabho |
śṛṇvasmadvacanaṃ prītyā yatkṛtaṃ sevakaistava ||
2.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
देवदेव महादेव परमेश महाप्रभो ।
शृण्वस्मद्वचनं प्रीत्या यत्कृतं सेवकैस्तव ॥

2.3.s:
bodhito girirājaśca menā vividhasūktibhiḥ |
setihāsaṃ maheśāna prabuddho'sau na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.3.d:
बोधितो गिरिराजश्च मेना विविधसूक्तिभिः ।
सेतिहासं महेशान प्रबुद्धोऽसौ न संशयः ॥

2.3.s:
vākyadattā girīndreṇa pārvatī te hi nānyathā |
udvāhāya pragaccha tvaṃ gaṇairdevaiśca saṃyutaḥ ||
2.3.d:
वाक्यदत्ता गिरीन्द्रेण पार्वती ते हि नान्यथा ।
उद्वाहाय प्रगच्छ त्वं गणैर्देवैश्च संयुतः ॥

2.3.s:
gaccha śīghraṃ mahādeva himācalagṛhaṃ prabho |
vivāhaya yathā rītiḥ pārvatīmātmajanmane ||
2.3.d:
गच्छ शीघ्रं महादेव हिमाचलगृहं प्रभो ।
विवाहय यथा रीतिः पार्वतीमात्मजन्मने ॥

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ laukikācāratatparaḥ |
prahṛṣṭātmā maheśānaḥ prahasyedamuvāca saḥ ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तेषां लौकिकाचारतत्परः ।
प्रहृष्टात्मा महेशानः प्रहस्येदमुवाच सः ॥

2.3.s:
maheśa uvāca |
vivāho hi mahābhāgā na dṛṣṭo na śruto mayā |
yathā purā bhavadbhistadvidhiḥ procyo viśeṣataḥ ||
2.3.d:
महेश उवाच ।
विवाहो हि महाभागा न दृष्टो न श्रुतो मया ।
यथा पुरा भवद्भिस्तद्विधिः प्रोच्यो विशेषतः ॥

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
tadākarṇya maheśasya laukikaṃ vacanaṃ śubham |
pratyūcuḥ prahasantaste devadevaṃ sadāśivam ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
तदाकर्ण्य महेशस्य लौकिकं वचनं शुभम् ।
प्रत्यूचुः प्रहसन्तस्ते देवदेवं सदाशिवम् ॥

2.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
viṣṇumāhūya vai śīghraṃ sasamājaṃ viśeṣataḥ |
brahmāṇaṃ sasutaṃ prītyā tathā devaṃ śatakratum ||
2.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
विष्णुमाहूय वै शीघ्रं ससमाजं विशेषतः ।
ब्रह्माणं ससुतं प्रीत्या तथा देवं शतक्रतुम् ॥

2.3.s:
tathā ṛṣigaṇānsarvān yakṣagandharvakinnarān |
siddhān vidyādharāṃścaiva tathā caivāpsarogaṇān ||
2.3.d:
तथा ऋषिगणान्सर्वान् यक्षगन्धर्वकिन्नरान् ।
सिद्धान् विद्याधरांश्चैव तथा चैवाप्सरोगणान् ॥

2.3.s:
etāṃścānyānprabho sarvānānayasveha sādaram |
sarvaṃ saṃsādhayiṣyanti tvatkāryaṃ te na saṃśayaḥ ||
2.3.d:
एतांश्चान्यान्प्रभो सर्वानानयस्वेह सादरम् ।
सर्वं संसाधयिष्यन्ति त्वत्कार्यं ते न संशयः ॥

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
ityuktvā sapta ṛṣayastadājñāṃ prāpya te mudā |
svadhāma prayayuḥ sarve śaṃsantaḥ śaṅkarīṃ gatim ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
dvitīyāyāṃ rudrasaṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ pārvatīkhaṇḍe
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा सप्त ऋषयस्तदाज्ञां प्राप्य ते मुदा ।
स्वधाम प्रययुः सर्वे शंसन्तः शङ्करीं गतिम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
द्वितीयायां रुद्रसंहितायां तृतीयः पार्वतीखण्डे
2.3.m:
Homage to the glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

The third section, the Pārvatīkhaṇḍa, in the second section, the Rudrasaṃhitā.

In the second Rudrasaṃhitā, the third [part], the Pārvatī section.

2.3.s:
nārada uvāca |
tāta prājña vadedānīṃ saptarṣiṣu gateṣu ca |
kimakārṣīddhimagiristanme kṛtvā kṛpāṃ prabho ||
2.3.d:
नारद उवाच ।
तात प्राज्ञ वदेदानीं सप्तर्षिषु गतेषु च ।
किमकार्षीद्धिमगिरिस्तन्मे कृत्वा कृपां प्रभो ॥
2.3.m: Nārada said: / "O wise father, tell now: when the seven sages were gone, / what did the snowy mountain do? Out of kindness, tell me that, O Lord."

2.3.s:
brahmovāca |
gateṣu teṣu muniṣu saptasvapi munīśvara |
sārundhatīṣu himavān yadakārṣīd bravīmi te ||
2.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
गतेषु तेषु मुनिषु सप्तस्वपि मुनीश्वर ।
सारुन्धतीषु हिमवान् यदकार्षीद् ब्रवीमि ते ॥
2.3.m: Brahmā said: / "When those seven sages had departed, along with Arundhatī, O lord of sages, / I shall tell you what Himavat did.

2.3.s:
tata āmantrya svabhrātṝn mervādīn sasutapriyaḥ |
mahāmanāḥ sa mumude himavān parvateśvaraḥ ||
2.3.d:
तत आमन्त्र्य स्वभ्रातॄन् मेर्वादीन् ससुतप्रियः ।
महामनाः स मुमुदे हिमवान् पर्वतेश्वरः ॥
2.3.m: Then, having invited his brothers, Meru and the others, loving his daughter, / that noble-minded Himavat, the lord of mountains, rejoiced.

2.3.s:
tadājñaptastataḥ prītyā himavān lagnapatrikām |
lekhayāmāsa suprītyā gargeṇa svapurodhasā ||
2.3.d:
तदाज्ञप्तस्ततः प्रीत्या हिमवान् लग्नपत्रिकाम् ।
लेखयामास सुप्रीत्या गर्गेण स्वपुरोधसा ॥
2.3.m: Instructed by him, Himavat then with great joy had the letter of the auspicious moment / written with fondness by Garga, his own domestic priest.

2.3.s:
atha prasthāpayāmāsa tāṃ śivāya sa patrikām |
nānāvidhāstu sāmagryaḥ svajanairmuditātmabhiḥ ||
2.3.d:
अथ प्रस्थापयामास तां शिवाय स पत्रिकाम् ।
नानाविधास्तु सामग्र्यः स्वजनैर्मुदितात्मभिः ॥
2.3.m: Then he sent that letter to Śiva, / along with various provisions, through his own joyous people.

2.3.s:
te janāstatra gatvā ca kailāse śivasannidhim |
daduḥ śivāya tatpatraṃ tilakaṃ saṃvidhāya ca ||
2.3.d:
ते जनास्तत्र गत्वा च कैलासे शिवसन्निधिम् ।
ददुः शिवाय तत्पत्रं तिलकं संविधाय च ॥
2.3.m: Those people went there to Kailāsa, to the presence of Śiva, / and, having applied the forehead mark, gave that letter to Śiva.

2.3.s:
sammānitā viśeṣeṇa prabhuṇā ca yathocitam |
sarve te prītimanasa ājagmuḥ śailasannidhim ||
2.3.d:
सम्मानिता विशेषेण प्रभुणा च यथोचितम् ।
सर्वे ते प्रीतिमनस आजग्मुः शैलसन्निधिम् ॥
2.3.m: Specially honored as was fitting by the Lord, / with joyful minds they all returned to the mountain's presence.

2.3.s:
sammānitānviśeṣeṇa maheśenāgatān janān |
dṛṣṭvā suharṣitān śailo mumodātīva cetasi ||
2.3.d:
सम्मानितान्विशेषेण महेशेनागतान् जनान् ।
दृष्ट्वा सुहर्षितान् शैलो मुमोदातीव चेतसि ॥
2.3.m: Seeing his people returned, specially honored / by Maheśa and highly rejoiced, the mountain exulted exceedingly in his heart.

2.3.s:
tato nimantraṇaṃ cakre svabandhūnāṃ pramoditaḥ |
nānādeśasthitānāṃ ca nikhilānāṃ sukhāspadam ||
2.3.d:
ततो निमन्त्रणं चक्रे स्वबन्धूनां प्रमोदितः ।
नानादेशस्थितानां च निखिलानां सुखास्पदम् ॥
2.3.m: Then, joyful, he issued an invitation to his kinsmen, / residing in various lands, all of them—a source of happiness.

2.3.s:
tataḥ sa kārayāmāsa svannasaṅgrahamādarāt |
nānāvidhāśca sāmagrīrvivāhakaraṇocitāḥ ||
2.3.d:
ततः स कारयामास स्वन्नसङ्ग्रहमादरात् ।
नानाविधाश्च सामग्रीर्विवाहकरणोचिताः ॥
2.3.m: Then with care he caused a collection of fine food to be made, / and various provisions suitable for performing a wedding:

2.3.s:
taṇḍulānāṃ bahūn śailān pṛthukānāṃ tathaiva ca |
guḍānāṃ śarkarāṇāṃ ca lavaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca ||
2.3.d:
तण्डुलानां बहून् शैलान् पृथुकानां तथैव च ।
गुडानां शर्कराणां च लवणानां तथैव च ॥
2.3.m: many mountains of polished rice, and likewise of flattened rice, / of raw sugar, and of refined sugars, and likewise of salts;

2.3.s:
kṣīrāṇāṃ ca ghṛtānāṃ ca dadhnāṃ vāpīścakāra saḥ |
yavādidhānyapiṣṭānāṃ laḍḍukānāṃ tathaiva ca ||
2.3.d:
क्षीराणां च घृतानां च दध्नां वापीश्चकार सः ।
यवादिधान्यपिष्टानां लड्डुकानां तथैव च ॥
2.3.m: and reservoirs of milks, of clarifed butter, and of curds he made, / and of flours of grains such as barley, and likewise of laddu sweets,

2.3.s:
śaṣkulīnāṃ svastikānāṃ śarkarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca |
amṛtekṣurasānāṃ ca tatra vāpīścakāra saḥ ||
2.3.d:
शष्कुलीनां स्वस्तिकानां शर्कराणां तथैव च ।
अमृतेक्षुरसानां च तत्र वापीश्चकार सः ॥
2.3.m: of twisted pastries, svastika pastries, and of sugars; / and reservoirs of sweet sugarcane juice he made there;

2.3.s:
bahvīrhaiyaṅgavānāṃ ca hyāsavānāṃ tathaiva ca |
nānā pakvānnasaṅghāṃśca mahāsvādurasām̐stathā ||
2.3.d:
बह्वीर्हैयङ्गवानां च ह्यासवानां तथैव च ।
नाना पक्वान्नसङ्घांश्च महास्वादुरसाम्̐स्तथा ॥
2.3.m: many [reservoirs] of fresh clarified butter, and likewise of spirits, / and masses of various cooked foods, and great-flavored broths;

2.3.s:
nānā vyañjanavastūni gaṇadevahitāni ca |
amūlyanānāvastrāṇi vahniśaucāni yāni ca ||
2.3.d:
नाना व्यञ्जनवस्तूनि गणदेवहितानि च ।
अमूल्यनानावस्त्राणि वह्निशौचानि यानि च ॥
2.3.m: various condiment ingredients suitable for the attendants and gods, / and priceless, varied garments cleansed with fire;

2.3.s:
maṇiratnaprakārāṇi suvarṇarajatāni ca |
dravyāṇyetāni cānyāni saṅgṛhya vidhipūrvakam ||
2.3.d:
मणिरत्नप्रकाराणि सुवर्णरजतानि च ।
द्रव्याण्येतानि चान्यानि सङ्गृह्य विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
2.3.m: kinds of gems and jewels, gold and silver; / having gathered these materials and others according to the rule,

2.3.s:
maṅgalaṃ kartumārebhe girirmaṅgalakṛddine |
saṃskāraṃ kārayāmāsuḥ pārvatyāḥ parvatastriyaḥ ||
2.3.d:
मङ्गलं कर्तुमारेभे गिरिर्मङ्गलकृद्दिने ।
संस्कारं कारयामासुः पार्वत्याः पर्वतस्त्रियः ॥
2.3.m: on the day that brought auspiciousness, the mountain began to perform the auspicious ceremony. / The women of the mountains had the preparatory rite of Pārvatī performed.

2.3.s:
tā maṅgalaṃ mudā cakrurbhūṣitā bhūṣaṇaiḥ svayam |
puradvijastriyo hṛṣṭā lokācāraṃ pracakrire ||
sotsavaṃ vividhaṃ tatra sumaṅgalapurassaram |
himālayo'pi hṛṣṭātmā kṛtvācāraṃ sumaṅgalam ||
2.3.d:
ता मङ्गलं मुदा चक्रुर्भूषिता भूषणैः स्वयम् ।
पुरद्विजस्त्रियो हृष्टा लोकाचारं प्रचक्रिरे ॥
सोत्सवं विविधं तत्र सुमङ्गलपुरस्सरम् ।
हिमालयोऽपि हृष्टात्मा कृत्वाचारं सुमङ्गलम् ॥
2.3.m:
Adorned with ornaments themselves, they performed the auspicious rite with joy; / the twice-born women of the city, delighted, performed worldly customs.

With various festivities there, preceded by auspiciousness, / Himālaya also, with joyful heart, having performed the most auspicious custom,

2.3.s:
sarvabhāvena suprīto bandhuvargāgamotsukaḥ |
etasminnantare tasya bāndhavāśca nimantritāḥ ||
2.3.d:
सर्वभावेन सुप्रीतो बन्धुवर्गागमोत्सुकः ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तस्य बान्धवाश्च निमन्त्रिताः ॥
2.3.m: was well pleased in every way, eager for the arrival of the group of his kinsmen. / In the meantime, his invited kinsmen

2.3.s:
ājagmuḥ sastriyo hṛṣṭāḥ sasutāḥ saparicchadāḥ |
tadeva śṛṇu devarṣe giryāgamanamādṛtaḥ ||
2.3.d:
आजग्मुः सस्त्रियो हृष्टाः ससुताः सपरिच्छदाः ।
तदेव शृणु देवर्षे गिर्यागमनमादृतः ॥
2.3.m: arrived, delighted, with their wives, sons, and entourages. / Listen carefully, O divine sage, to that arrival of the mountains:

2.3.s:
varṇayāmi samāsena śivaprītivivṛddhaye |
devālayagiriryo hi divyarūpadharo mahān ||
2.3.d:
वर्णयामि समासेन शिवप्रीतिविवृद्धये ।
देवालयगिरिर्यो हि दिव्यरूपधरो महान् ॥
2.3.m: I shall describe it concisely to increase love for Śiva. / The mountain that is the abode of gods, great, bearing a divine form,

2.3.s:
nānāratnaparibhrājatsamājaḥ saparicchadaḥ |
nānāmaṇimahāratnasāramādāya yatnataḥ ||
2.3.d:
नानारत्नपरिभ्राजत्समाजः सपरिच्छदः ।
नानामणिमहारत्नसारमादाय यत्नतः ॥
2.3.m: with an assembly shining with various jewels, with his entourage, / taking with care the essence of various gems and great jewels,

2.3.s:
suveṣālaṅkṛtaḥ śrīmān jagāma sa himālayam |
mandaraḥ sarvaśobhāḍhyaḥ sanārītanayo giriḥ ||
2.3.d:
सुवेषालङ्कृतः श्रीमान् जगाम स हिमालयम् ।
मन्दरः सर्वशोभाढ्यः सनारीतनयो गिरिः ॥
2.3.m: attired in fine dress, glorious, went to Himālaya. / Mountain Mandara, rich in all splendors, with his wives and sons,

2.3.s:
sūpāyanāni saṅgṛhya jagāma vividhāni ca |
astācalo'pi divyātmā sopāyana udāradhīḥ ||
2.3.d:
सूपायनानि सङ्गृह्य जगाम विविधानि च ।
अस्ताचलोऽपि दिव्यात्मा सोपायन उदारधीः ॥
2.3.m: taking various good gifts, went [there]. / The western mountain Astācala also, divine in nature, of noble mind, with gifts,

2.3.s:
bahuśobhāsamāyukta ājagāma mudānvitaḥ |
udayācala ādāya sadratnāni maṇīnapi ||
2.3.d:
बहुशोभासमायुक्त आजगाम मुदान्वितः ।
उदयाचल आदाय सद्रत्नानि मणीनपि ॥
2.3.m: endowed with great beauty, arrived filled with joy. / The eastern mountain Udayācala, taking excellent jewels and gems,

2.3.s:
atyutkṛṣṭaparīvāra ājagāma mahāsukhī |
malayo girirājo hi saparīvāra ādṛtaḥ ||
2.3.d:
अत्युत्कृष्टपरीवार आजगाम महासुखी ।
मलयो गिरिराजो हि सपरीवार आदृतः ॥
2.3.m: with a superior retinue, arrived exceedingly happy. / Indeed, the mountain king Malaya, respectful, with his retinue,

2.3.s:
sudivyaracanāyukta āyayau bahusadbalaḥ |
sadyo darduranāmā ca muditaḥ sakalatrakaḥ ||
2.3.d:
सुदिव्यरचनायुक्त आययौ बहुसद्बलः ।
सद्यो दर्दुरनामा च मुदितः सकलत्रकः ॥
2.3.m: endowed with divine ornament and possessing much good strength, arrived. / Instantly the mountain named Dardura, joyous, with his wife,

2.3.s:
bahuśobhānvitastāta yayau himagirergṛham |
niṣado'pi prahṛṣṭātmā saparicchada āyayau ||
2.3.d:
बहुशोभान्वितस्तात ययौ हिमगिरेर्गृहम् ।
निषदोऽपि प्रहृष्टात्मा सपरिच्छद आययौ ॥
2.3.m: endowed with much splendor, O dear one, went to the house of the snowy mountain. / Niṣadha also, with delighted mind and with his entourage, arrived;

2.3.s:
sasutastrīgaṇaḥ prītyā yayau himagirergṛham |
ājagāma mahābhāgyo bhūdharo gandhamādanaḥ ||
2.3.d:
ससुतस्त्रीगणः प्रीत्या ययौ हिमगिरेर्गृहम् ।
आजगाम महाभाग्यो भूधरो गन्धमादनः ॥
2.3.m: with his group of sons and wives, he went with affection to the house of the snowy mountain. / The highly fortunate mountain Gandhamādana arrived;

2.3.s:
karavīrastathaivāpi mahāvibhavasaṃyutaḥ |
mahendraḥ parvataśreṣṭha ājagāma himālayam ||
2.3.d:
करवीरस्तथैवापि महाविभवसंयुतः ।
महेन्द्रः पर्वतश्रेष्ठ आजगाम हिमालयम् ॥
2.3.m: likewise Karavīra also, endowed with great magnificence; / Mahendra, best among mountains, came to Himālaya,

2.3.s:
sagaṇaḥ sasutastrīko bahuśobhāsamanvitaḥ |
pāriyātro hi hṛṣṭātmā maṇiratnākarairyutaḥ ||
sagaṇaḥ saparīvāra āyayau himabhūdharam |
krauñcaḥ parvatarājo hi mahābalaparicchadaḥ |
ājagāma giriśreṣṭhaḥ samupāyana ādṛtaḥ | 33 ||
2.3.d:
सगणः ससुतस्त्रीको बहुशोभासमन्वितः ।
पारियात्रो हि हृष्टात्मा मणिरत्नाकरैर्युतः ॥
सगणः सपरीवार आययौ हिमभूधरम् ।
क्रौञ्चः पर्वतराजो हि महाबलपरिच्छदः ।
आजगाम गिरिश्रेष्ठः समुपायन आदृतः । 33 ॥
2.3.m:
with his followers, with his sons and wives, endowed with much splendor. / Pāriyātra, joyful, accompanied by mines of gems and jewels,

with his followers and with his retinue, came to the snowy mountain. / Krauñca, the king of mountains, possessing an entourage of great strength, / the best among mountains, arrived respectful, with gifts.

2.3.s:
puruṣottamaśailo'pi saparicchada ādṛtaḥ |
mahopāyanamādāyājagāma himabhūdharam ||
2.3.d:
पुरुषोत्तमशैलोऽपि सपरिच्छद आदृतः ।
महोपायनमादायाजगाम हिमभूधरम् ॥
2.3.m: The Puruṣottama mountain too, with his retinue and showing respect, / took a great gift and came to the snow-mountain.

2.3.s:
nīlaḥ salīlaḥ sasutaḥ sastrīko dravyasaṃyutaḥ |
ājagāma himāgasya gṛhamānandasaṃyutaḥ ||
2.3.d:
नीलः सलीलः ससुतः सस्त्रीको द्रव्यसंयुतः ।
आजगाम हिमागस्य गृहमानन्दसंयुतः ॥
2.3.m: Nīla, playful, with his sons, his wife, and accompanied by wealth, / came with joy to the home of the snow-mountain.

2.3.s:
trikūṭaścitrakūṭo'pi veṅkaṭaḥ śrīgiristathā |
gokāmukhī nāradaśca himagehamupāgamat ||
2.3.d:
त्रिकूटश्चित्रकूटोऽपि वेङ्कटः श्रीगिरिस्तथा ।
गोकामुखी नारदश्च हिमगेहमुपागमत् ॥
2.3.m: Trikūṭa, Citrakūṭa, Veṅkaṭa, Śrīgiri, / Gokāmukhī, and Nārada came to the snow[-mountain's] abode.

2.3.s:
vindhyaśca parvataśreṣṭho nānāsampatsamanvitaḥ |
ājagāma prahṛṣṭātmā sadāratanayaḥ śubhaḥ ||
2.3.d:
विन्ध्यश्च पर्वतश्रेष्ठो नानासम्पत्समन्वितः ।
आजगाम प्रहृष्टात्मा सदारतनयः शुभः ॥
2.3.m: And Vindhya, the best of mountains, accompanied by various riches, / joyful at heart, with his wife and children, auspicious, came there.

2.3.s:
kālañjaro mahāśailo bahuharṣasamanvitaḥ |
bahubhiḥ svagaṇaiḥ prītyājagāma himabhūdharam ||
2.3.d:
कालञ्जरो महाशैलो बहुहर्षसमन्वितः ।
बहुभिः स्वगणैः प्रीत्याजगाम हिमभूधरम् ॥
2.3.m: The great mountain Kālañjara, filled with great joy, / came with great love to the snow-mountain along with his numerous retinues.

2.3.s:
kailāsastu mahāśailo mahāharṣasamanvitaḥ |
ājagāma kṛpāṃ kṛtvā sarvopari lasatprabhuḥ ||
2.3.d:
कैलासस्तु महाशैलो महाहर्षसमन्वितः ।
आजगाम कृपां कृत्वा सर्वोपरि लसत्प्रभुः ॥
2.3.m: And the great mountain Kailāsa, filled with immense joy, / having shown kindness, the radiant lord presiding above all, came.

2.3.s:
anye'pi bhūbhṛto ye hi dvīpeṣvanyeṣvapi dvija |
ihāpi ye'calāḥ sarve āyayuste himālayam ||
2.3.d:
अन्येऽपि भूभृतो ये हि द्वीपेष्वन्येष्वपि द्विज ।
इहापि येऽचलाः सर्वे आययुस्ते हिमालयम् ॥
2.3.m: The other mountains too that are in other continents, O twice-born, / and all the mountains here on earth—they all came to the Himālaya.

2.3.s:
nimantritā nagāstatra tena pūrvaṃ mudā mune |
āyayurnikhilāḥ prītyā vivāhaśśivayoriti ||
2.3.d:
निमन्त्रिता नगास्तत्र तेन पूर्वं मुदा मुने ।
आययुर्निखिलाः प्रीत्या विवाहश्शिवयोरिति ॥
2.3.m: The mountains, having been invited there by him beforehand with joy, O sage, / all came with affection, [thinking,] "This is the wedding of Śiva and his bride."

2.3.s:
tadā sarve samāyātāḥ śoṇabhadrādayaḥ khalu |
bahuśobhā mahāprītyā vivāhaśśivayoriti ||
2.3.d:
तदा सर्वे समायाताः शोणभद्रादयः खलु ।
बहुशोभा महाप्रीत्या विवाहश्शिवयोरिति ॥
2.3.m: Then all the [rivers] headed by Śoṇabhadra indeed arrived, / of great splendor, with great love, [thinking,] "This is the wedding of Śiva and his bride."

2.3.s:
nadyaḥ sarvāḥ samāyātā nānālaṅkārasaṃyutāḥ |
divyarūpadharāḥ prītyā vivāhaśśivayoriti ||
2.3.d:
नद्यः सर्वाः समायाता नानालङ्कारसंयुताः ।
दिव्यरूपधराः प्रीत्या विवाहश्शिवयोरिति ॥
2.3.m: All the rivers arrived, adorned with various ornaments, / assuming divine forms, out of love, [thinking,] "This is the wedding of Śiva and his bride."

2.3.s:
godāvarī ca yamunā brahmastrīrveṇikā tathā |
āyayau himaśailaṃ vai vivāhaśśivayoriti ||
2.3.d:
गोदावरी च यमुना ब्रह्मस्त्रीर्वेणिका तथा ।
आययौ हिमशैलं वै विवाहश्शिवयोरिति ॥
2.3.m: Godāvarī, Yamunā, and the Brahmastrī Veṇikā / came to the snow-mountain, [thinking,] "This is the wedding of Śiva and his bride."

2.3.s:
